articleTitle: GIS metal particle movement and induced SF6gap breakdown characteristics under mechanical vibration
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: At present, metal particles are still one of the main insulation defects that harm the insulation performance of GIS. Especially during the moment or a period of time after GIS live operation, GIS discharge faults caused by metal particles occur frequently. However, there is currently a lack of research on the motion and induced discharge characteristics of particles under the mechanical vibration of live operation. This article built a 126 kV GIS experimental platform, simulated the process of GIS switch electrification operation through external mechanical vibration, and researched the motion and induced discharge process of wire metal particles under mechanical vibration. Research has found that the mechanical vibration generated by switch operation can reduce the jumping field strength of metal particles by about 40%, and multiple stationary particles can form a series discharge of multiple particles in the SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>gas gap after being excited to lift off, reducing the breakdown voltage of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>.

articleTitle: Quantitative analysis of industrial load evolution considering dual carbon goals
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the introduction of extensive policies to promote the dual carbon goals, energy-intensive industries adjust their production plans, and their loads show obvious periodicity, which brings severe challenges to the load forecasting accuracy. The policy involves too many factors, whose influence mechanism is complex. With limited amount of accessible data, the traditional load forecasting method fails to solve the difficult problems. A quantitative analysis of industrial load evolution considering dual carbon goals is proposed. Analysis of national policies and enterprise measures to establish the impact mechanism correlation. The evaluation index system is established based on analytic hierarchy process and sensitivity analysis. A combined model based on ARIMA, intervention model and system dynamics is established to obtain a quantitative analysis of industrial load evolution considering the dual carbon goals. Based on the four typical industries of iron and steel, cement, chemical industry and non-ferrous metals in a certain province, the simulation verification shows that the proposed method can reflect the influence of dual carbon policy, has adaptability to multiple industries, and can improve the accuracy of load forecasting.

articleTitle: Research on the online measurement method of DC GIL surface charge based on self-sensing of basin insulators
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In this paper, an online measurement method of surface charge based on self-sensing of basin insulator is proposed, which is to calculate the surface charge distribution by using the floating potential on the multi-segment shielding ring generated by surface charge. A 3D simulation model of GIL is built using finite element software, the floating potential of the shielding ring with different surface charge distributions are calculated and analysed, and the error of the estimated surface charge calculated based on the floating potential is compared with the real value. In addition, the influence of different shielding ring structures on the insulator surface electric field is also calculated and analysed. The results show that there is a linear relationship between the floating potential and the surface charge density. The surface charge distribution characteristics can be obtained by using the floating potential on the multi-segment shielding ring, and the error between the estimated surface charge and the real value is less than 4%. Considering the multi-segment shielding ring as a floating conductor, the electric field on the concave surface of the insulator is reduced by about 0.6 kV/cm, while the electric field on the convex surface is increased by about 0.9 kV/cm. This study can provide a reference for the online monitoring technology of DC GIL insulator surface charge.

articleTitle: Multi-parameter sensing scheme based on monitoring of distribution trasformers
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: As the core equipment of distribution system, its safe and stable operation of distribution transformer directly affects the reliability of distribution network operation. However, the current monitoring methods for distribution transformers are insufficient, which cannot ensure real-time online monitoring and its monitoring parameters are relatively single. Therefore, according to the multi-parameter change characteristics and related performance indicators during the fault development of distribution transformers, a selection scheme of multi-parameter sensors is proposed to meet the requirements of online monitoring of distribution transformers.

articleTitle: Broadband oscillation analysis and suppression method of direct-drive wind farm through flexible direct transmission system under oscillation frequency coupling
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The flexible VSC-HVDC transmission system with technical and economic feasibility is going mainstream in the long-distance transmission of offshore wind power along with its development. But the interaction between the control device and VSC-HVDC of the wind turbine generator might lead to oscillations at the frequency ranging from several Hz to over a thousand Hz. Moreover, there is an oscillation frequency coupling feature. This paper takes three-phase grid-connected inverter as the starting point to explain the new characteristics of the oscillation frequency coupling of the new power system, and then establishes the grid-connected model of the direct drive wind farm through the flexible VSC-HVDC transmission system, and analyzes its oscillation characteristics and influencing factors. Finally, the additional damping controller is designed with the speed as the reference, and the oscillation suppression effect is remarkable.

articleTitle: Over-voltage protection of high-voltage reverse blocking IGCT in hybrid line commutated converters
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The high-voltage reverse blocking integrated gate commutated thyristor (RB-IGCT) is a suitable power semiconductor device for hybrid line-commutated converters (HCC) to effectively reduce the risk of commutation failure. In HCC, the RB-IGCT device is required to protect itself from over-voltage destruction under some fault working conditions, but the over-voltage protection strategy for RB-IGCTs has not been proposed yet. In this article, an over-voltage protection system is designed and realized by gate driver based on the analysis of the working conditions. The function is verified by the turn-off experiments without the protection of the external circuit. Finally, the thermal and electrical pressure of the device when the over-voltage protection system is activated is detailedly analysed.

articleTitle: Study on variable speed converter based on IGCT and PWM modulation applied for variable speed pumped-storage unit
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: For the variable speed converter used in large-scale variable-speed pumped-storage units, a comparative analysis of various converter main power circuit topologies was carried out. The ANPC three-level converter topology was selected as the research object, and the working principle of ANPC converter was studied in detail. A new modulation strategy is proposed. To verify the modulation strategy and main power circuit design, an ANPC three-level converter power unit based on IGCT power switch was developed and power cycling test was performed.

articleTitle: Research on instability of HVDC system considering converter transformer saturation
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the widespread application of high voltage direct current (HVDC) in large-scale inter-regional power transmission, the issue of harmonic instability caused by transformer saturation received increasing attention. This paper focuses on this issue by analyzing the formation principle of DC bias in transformers and accurate modeling. The J-A hysteresis model and the compensating current source model in PSCAD are introduced. The mechanism of harmonic instability caused by transformer saturation is analyzed. Moreover, a resonance instability criterion is derived, which takes the saturation effect of the converter transformer into account. Then, a comparison is made between the excitation current waveforms of the two models. The simulation results in PSCAD prove the accuracy of analysis and the hysteresis transformer model has higher precision in characterizing the occurrence of cumulative instability.

articleTitle: Accurate calculation method for temporary overvoltage of power systems with diversified renewable energy sources
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Due to the detection and control delay of renewable energy source, after the grid short-circuit fault is cleared, the output current surplus of low-voltage Ride Through (LVRT) would lead to the temporary overvoltage (TOV) of the power system. Few literatures have analysed the influence of different grid-connected modes of renewable energy source and grid impedance characteristics on TOV. Firstly, the transient characteristics of the permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) and doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) after fault clearance are derived. Further, the influence of active and reactive current on temporary overvoltage under different impedance characteristics of power grid is analysed. On this basis, an iterative calculation method for temporary overvoltage considering the impact of active current is proposed. Finally, electromagnetic transient simulations are conducted to verify the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Charge distribution and electromagnetic force analysis of linear metal particles in DC GIS
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Gas-insulated metal-enclosed switchgear (GIS) generates metal particles during operation, which will affect the insulation performance of the equipment, and the linear metal particles will move to the high voltage electrode and form firefly movement. Based on this, this paper takes linear metal particles as the research object, uses the multi-physics simulation model of GIS bus in actual conditions, calculates the charge distribution characteristics and electromagnetic force of firefly metal particles in the chamber, explains the mechanism of firefly movement and the mechanism of high-voltage electrode coating, calculates the lifting voltage of linear metal particles, and explores the parameters affecting the lifting voltage. The simulation results show tha t the linear metal particle tip is prone to charge accumulation, causing the particle to swing and other motion characteristics, the conversion of electromagnetic force in contact with the high-voltage electrode causes the particle to form the phenomenon of firefly.

articleTitle: A parametric design and optimization method for an economical concentrated DCC based on thyristors with resonant self-turn-OFF ability (T-DCC)
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The off-shore wind voltage sourced converter-based high-voltage direct current (VSC-HVdc) system has very good application prospects, and the DC chopper plays an important role in the VSC-HVdc system.In order to solve the problem that it is expensive to use too many IGBT in the DC chopper that already exist. An economical concentrated DCC based on thyristors with resonant self-turn-OFF ability (T-DCC) is raised. However, its parameter selection needs to be further designed and optimized. A parameter selection method with the goal of lowest cost is proposed in this article. In addition, anomalies in the actual engineering situation are also considered in this method to make sure that the (T-DCC) can work reliably in real engineering.

articleTitle: Study on vibration characteristics of magnetic saturation AC fault current limiter
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the gradual increase of power system transmission capacity and the daily increase of user load, when a short circuit fault occurs in the system, the fault current may exceed the breaking capacity of the circuit breaker. In AC power grids, saturated core fault current limiter (SCFCL) is a highly promising current limiting method. However, vibration may occur during the operation of SCFCL, and in severe cases, it may damage SCFCL and affect the operation of the power grid. In response to the problem of vibration during the operation of SCFCL, this paper conducts simulation research using the method of multi physics field coupling, taking into account the structural characteristics of SCFCL and the numerical calculation method of vibration. Firstly, based on the electromagnetic coupling method, analyze the typical topology and operating principle of SCFCL, introduce the reasons for SCFCL vibration during operation, provide a numerical calculation method for SCFCL core vibration, and simulate the current limiting ability of SCFCL; Then, the focus is on simulating and calculating the magnetic flux density distribution, stress, core vibration displacement, and core vibration acceleration of SCFCL, which is of great significance for the design and optimization of SCFCL.

articleTitle: Transient characteristics analysis of flexible chopped-wave DC energy dissipation device
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: A DC energy dissipation device is a key equipment for the offshore wind power DC transmission system to achieve fault ride-through. This paper has conducted a theoretical analysis on the transient characteristics of the energy dissipation device in the event of a DC fault under energy dissipation and non-energy dissipation operating conditions. The software PSCAD was utilized for simulation verification to obtain the electrical stress conditions of the energy dissipation device under different fault conditions, further providing technical reference for the design and operation of DC energy dissipation devices.

articleTitle: Preparable PEI-Tantalum oxide hybrid dielectric with excellent high temperature energy storage performance
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Polymer dielectrics serve as crucial materials in electrostatic capacitors, playing essential roles in various applications. However, their performance sharply declines with increasing temperature, failing to meet the demands of emerging markets. In previous research, our group proposed enhancing the high-temperature energy storage performance of composite dielectrics by introducing organic-inorganic hybrid structures. Nevertheless, due to the extreme sensitivity of the raw materials to water, sample preparation had to be conducted in an anhydrous glove box. In this study, we optimized the composition of the inorganic phase to balance the high-temperature energy storage performance and the difficulty of preparation of hybrid composite dielectrics, enabling their fabrication process to be conducted in ambient air. The resulting PEI-TaO composite dielectric achieves a 90% efficiency energy storage density of 6.5 J cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>at 200°C. Simultaneously, large-scale, uniformly performing thin films can be successfully prepared, which shows the potential of industrial preparation.

articleTitle: Analysis on the feasibility and influence factors of VSPS to suppress continuous commutation failure of LCC-HVDC
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Variable speed pumped storage (VSPS) is a novel technical solution for peak and frequency regulation in the power industry. It also has the capability to participate in voltage regulation of the power grid when necessary. The reactive power compensation ability of VSPS units can contribute to mitigating continuous commutation failure of line commutated converter based high voltage direct current(LCC-HVDC) caused by transient voltage during connection to the receiving power network. Therefore, this paper begins with an examination of the mechanism of continuous commutation failure, followed by an analysis of VSPS control strategies and calculation of reactive power compensation limits. Finally, a simulation example is presented to validate the effectiveness of VSPS in suppressing continuous commutation failure, along with an analysis of how active power output and transmission length influence this suppression effect.

articleTitle: Comparison of impulse effective length of grounding electrode evaluated by different methods
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Extending horizontal grounding electrodes has proven to be an efficient method for dissipating lightning currents and minimizing grounding resistance. However, an overly extensive horizontal grounding electrode does not necessarily enhance lightning protection performance. This paper utilizes the moment method to analyze impulse characteristics. Through calculating the variation in impulse grounding resistance, the effective length is determined for different soil resistivities. The paper presents a comprehensive summary of diverse calculation methods for effective length under various definitions. It conducts a comparative analysis between the effective length derived through the moment method and that obtained from empirical formulas, offering both theoretical and technical support for the design of grounding devices.

articleTitle: Design, evaluation and simulation of low-carbon integrated energy supply system for data center based on medium voltage DC technology
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of data center energy supply, this paper proposes a topology of data center integrated energy supply system based on medium voltage DC, and establishes a comprehensive evaluation model of energy supply scheme. Based on the high requirements of data center for energy supply reliability, this paper designs a "hand-in-hand" data center integrated energy supply system topology based on medium voltage DC, and designs the key parameters such as the voltage level of the topology. In order to evaluate the topological performance of the designed comprehensive energy supply system, this paper designs a comprehensive energy supply system evaluation model based on the system efficiency, availability, net present value, carbon emission reduction ratio and other indicators. The simulation model of the data center integrated energy supply system is established in the PSCAD / EMTDC, and the simulation results prove the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: An operating characteristic analysis of flexible concentrated DC chopper
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In the face of potential fault types arising from the Qingzhou offshore wind power DC transmission project, and based on the application of Flexible Concentrated DC Chopper (FC-DCC) in the project, this paper developed a simulation model of the DC transmission system encompassing the wind farm, converter station, submarine cable, and DC chopper. The paper carried out simulation analysis on the three types of AC system faults specified by the project, verified the operation ability of the reliable control system of the FC-DCC to control the DC-link voltage, as well as its operation ability to automatically exit energy dissipation upon timeouts. The research provides insights into the energy dissipation operating characteristics of the FC-DCC, bolstering its practical application in the Qingzhou DC transmission project.

articleTitle: Research on all-DC offshore wind power system and its control technology in consideration of wind power fluctuation
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: DC transmission technology is an efficient solution to address the challenge of transmitting large-scale offshore wind power. Prevailing projects generally adopt the AC collection - DC transmission scheme. However, there are concerns about voltage/reactive power and synchronous stability on the AC collection side. To achieve cheaper and more efficient offshore wind power generation, this article proposes a plan for DC series collection and DC transmission. It analyses the coupling characteristics and stable control tactics of an all-DC offshore wind power system and highlights the essential role of a voltage-regulating converter in stabilizing series systems. Additionally, the hybrid MMC scheme is presented, with detailed explanations of the working principle and structural composition of the system. Furthermore, a stable control method for the hybrid MMC converter in the series system is provided, offering a practical solution for the development of large-scale offshore wind power. Finally, the accuracy and efficiency of the suggested equilibrium control technique are verified through the simulation model of the all-DC offshore wind power system.

articleTitle: Research on the improvement of test method of UHV DC dry-type bushing under long-term DC voltage
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: UHV DC dry-type bushings are the key component of the converter station, with complex working conditions, precise structure and complicated production process. However, at present, the application ratio of UHV DC casing is relatively low, lack of engineering verification. The standard method can’t completely test the defects. Even passing the IEC standard test, internal discharge may occur under long-term DC voltage. In this paper, the insulation properties of scaled model bushings under long-term DC voltages are investigated. Then the effect of temperature on the radial field strength of the bushings is simulated by the electric-thermal-fluid finite element method. Finally, an improvement of the UHV DC dry bushing test method is proposed as a supplement to the current standard. The results help to improve the bushing test method, reduce the risk of internal discharge, and improve the stability of UHV DC transmission.

articleTitle: Breakdown mechanism and repair method induced by edge porosity defect of ZnO varistor
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The ZnO varistor is a key component of lightning arresters. It inherently develops more porosity around the edge area during the sintering process, leading to varistor failure through phenomena such as puncture and explosion. This paper investigates the mechanism of pore induced failure by establishing a simulation model to calculate the electric field intensity and energy density distribution within the ZnO varistor. Through the analysis of edge treatment during the varistor manufacturing process, we highlight the existing defects in the edge area of the varistor. In response to these defects, we propose a rectification strategy that remedies the shortcomings of the current methods, thereby enhancing the performance of the varistor.

articleTitle: CNN-BiLSTM multivariate load prediction model based on MIC correlation analysis
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Load forecasting is an important prerequisite and foundation to ensure the rational design and stable operation of integrated energy systems. Aiming at the interactive coupling problem between multiple loads, this paper constructs a CNN-BiLSTM multi-load prediction model based on MIC correlation analysis. At the same time, the attention mechanism is applied to improve the weights of key features of loads. The input variables are filtered by calculating the MIC values of meteorological elements. The validation results show that the CNN-BiLSTM multivariate load prediction model based on MIC correlation analysis proposed in this paper can reduce the prediction error to a certain extent and has high prediction accuracy compared with other models.

articleTitle: Comparison of metallic particle behaviour according to AC and DC voltage
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS) concentrates the electric field locally when metallic particles levitate inside that cause breakdown when contacting high-voltage conductors. Therefore, research to prevent metallic particle levitation is continuously required. Previous studies indicate that the behaviour of metallic particles depending on the AC and DC voltage and particle shape. Additionally, most research presents particle behaviour analysis through simulations, without providing detailed methods. In this paper, a levitation experiment was conducted on spherical and wire metallic particles on a parallel flat plate electrode under AC and DC voltage in an SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>gas environment at atmospheric pressure. The recorded video was analysed using the Tracker 6.1.6 program to analyse the entire behaviour of the particles, according to shape, AC and DC and polarity.

articleTitle: The study on the compatibility of composite materials with mineral insulating oil
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: For oil-insulated power equipment, the compatibility of their construction materials with oil must be tested prior to use, as poor compatibility between them can lead to insulation failure. In this paper, an accelerated ageing test platform for liquid oil was constructed and the compatibility of several common and emerging materials used in UHV on-load tap-changers (OLTCs) with mineral oil was verified. The dielectric properties of the aged oils were evaluated and explained based on microscopic examination and molecular structure analysis. The results showed that metals normally have good compatibility with mineral oil, although an acceptable increase in conductivity loss occurred in the oil. Epoxy composites and polyformaldehyde (POM) also show good compatibility with oil. However, acrylic paint, commonly used to coat epoxy composites, should not be used as it readily dissolves in oil and significantly reduces the dielectric strength of the oil. Polyamide (PA) should be used sparingly and dried thoroughly before use due to its high-water absorption and poor intermolecular chain attraction. The experimental results and the microanalysis method can be a valuable reference and guide for material selection and optimisation in oil-insulated equipment.

articleTitle: A method to reduce the frequent action of tap changer in inverter station of HVDC transmission system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Ultra high voltage direct current transmission is the main technical means for large-scale energy bases in western China to remotely transmit power resources to the central and eastern load centers. With the continuous development of new power systems, the power grid has put forward higher requirements for the operation reliability, control flexibility, and equipment safety of ultra-high voltage direct current transmission. With the large-scale integration of new energy into ultra-high voltage DC systems, frequent voltage fluctuations and stability issues in converter stations are prominent. When the DC power or voltage repeatedly deviates from the target value, it will cause continuous action of tap changer, resulting in safety hazards for converter and on load tap changer equipment. Therefore, it is necessary to conduct research on optimization strategies for frequent operation of tap changers in ultra-high voltage direct current projects.

articleTitle: The connotation and architecture of the knowledge graph of relay protection defect diagnosis
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The reliable operation of the electric power system is highly dependent on the relay protection equipment as the first line of defense, and how to quickly and accurately determine the reason of the defect is of great significance. Aiming at the problem of insufficient coverage of defect diagnosis rules in the existing defect diagnosis methods, this paper proposes the idea of using knowledge graph to solve the problem. The connotation and architecture of the knowledge graph of relay protection defect diagnosis are proposed, and five layers of the knowledge graph are designed, namely equipment information layer, basic logic layer, extrapolation layer, inspection items execution sequence optimization layer, and retrieval application layer. This paper elaborates the internal relationship between the five layers, which lays a good foundation for the diagnosis of relay protection defects.

articleTitle: Evolutions of surface charge distribution on DC GIL insulators under under electro-thermal coupling field
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper examines various processes including the generation, migration, recombination, and diffusion of charged particles on the gas side. By employing COMSOL, a thermal-electrical multi-physics coupled surface charge accumulation model is constructed under a 500kV voltage. Consequently, the temperature distribution within the GIL cavity and the surface charge distribution of the insulator are determined. The influence of temperature gradient on the surface charge accumulation of the insulator was investigated. The research findings indicate that, during the charging process, the surface charges on the insulator primarily consist of heteropolar charges, forming a halo-shaped distribution. As the charging time increases, the charge halo spreads outward, and the charge density is maximum in the middle of the insulator. In the later stage of charging, a significant accumulation of charge occurs near the electrode, leading to an alternating distribution of high and low surface charges on the insulator.

articleTitle: Converter station selection method for VSC-DC intertie with both GFL and GFM configuration for grid resilience enhancement
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Urban power grids are facing many challenges due to necessary upgrades and expansions, particularly with converting AC lines to voltage source converter (VSC) based DC intertie to meet increasing active power support demand and reliability requirements. Owing to the various operation conditions of the urban power grid, the ideal control configuration of the VSC-DC intertie is to include both grids following control (GFL) and grid forming control (GFM) to satisfy different operation requirements of the urban power grid. However, the site selection of the converter station of the VSC-DC intertie may significantly influence the control performance of the VSC-DC intertie, especially when the VSC-DC intertie configures multiple control strategies. How to choose the best site for VSC-DC intertie locating to maximize control benefits of the VSC-DC intertie to the urban power grid. This paper introduces a novel site selection method for siting these converter stations considering the VSC-DC intertie configured by GFL and GFM. The site selection method uses voltage stability margins to exclude unregard nodes and employs a combination of Euclidean distance and grey relational analysis to identify optimal locations. To maximize the benefit of GFL and GFM control performance, the method is further refined with permutation entropy to calculate evaluation weight coefficients, enhancing the generality of the siting process. A case study conducted in an actual project validates the method’s effectiveness, demonstrating that the proposed novel site selection ensures that GFL and GFM configured converter stations are optimally placed to maximize both GFL and GFM control performance, significantly enhancing the power support capabilities and resilience enhancement at connected nodes and across the entire network.

articleTitle: LCC-MCC hybrid HVDC power flow calculation based on holomorphic embedding method
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: To capitalize on the advantages and mitigate the disadvantages of LCC and MMC HVDC systems, the LCC-MMC hybrid HVDC system has been developed. The steady-state models for LCC and MMC systems are essentially different. The derivation of the power flow model for this hybrid system is of fundamental importance. This paper first establishes the mathematical model of the LCC-MMC hybrid HVDC system. Then, based on the holomorphic embedding (HE) method, the HE formulation for the constructed model is derived. The approach for germ solution and the high-order power series calculation process is established. Furthermore, a sequential solution algorithm tailored to the hybrid system is proposed. Finally, the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method are verified using a modified IEEE 14-bus system incorporating a hybrid LCC-MCC HVDC line.

articleTitle: Impedance modeling and stability analysis of grid-forming permanent magnet direct-drive wind turbine based on multi-harmonic linearization
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The grid-forming permanent magnet direct drive wind turbine (GM-VSG) exhibits different stability when connected to the systems with different short-circuit ratios, posing challenges to the safety and stability of the system. To conduct stability analysis, the self-admittance and adjoint admittance models of VSG-PMSG are established in this paper. Considering the influence of frequency coupling, the single-input and single-output (SISO) impedance model of VSG-PMSG grid-connected system is established. The correctness of the SISO impedance model is proved by frequency scanning verification. Based on the established model, the stability of VSG-PMSG under different short circuit ratio systems is analysed. The results show that VSG-PMSG can operate stably under weak power grid and lose stability under strong power grid.

articleTitle: DC fault characteristics of battery energy storage system based on different grid-connected structures
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: To optimize the protection scheme of battery energy storage systems (BESSs) in the future, characteristics of DC fault current of BESSs with different grid-connected structures are studied in this paper. During the research, three grid-connected structures for BESS are analyzed, including battery clusters connected directly (structure_1), battery clusters connected through non-isolated DC/DC converter (structure_2), battery clusters connected through isolated DC/DC converter (structure_3). The equivalent circuit and the numerical calculation method of fault current are provided. The theoretical analysis is verified by simulation in PSCAD/EMTDC. The research results proved that the fault current has high peak value and rapid rise speed when non-isolated DC/DC is used, which poses great technical challenges to protective devices, such as fuse and DC breaker. Finally, comparison of three grid-connected structures is conducted. Only if DC breaker technology for BESS is broken through, battery clusters connected through non-isolated DC/DC converter is both cost-effective and high-efficient, making it more suitable for integration into large-scale BESS systems.

articleTitle: Impedance modelling and stability analysis of modular multilevel converter under two droop control strategies
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In recent years, grid-forming (GFM)-based modular multilevel converter (MMC) has received more attention in high-voltage DC (HVDC) transmission systems. In this paper, the AC-side impedance models of MMC with two different droop control structures are established using harmonic state-space method and validated by frequency scanning. Then, the impedance characteristics of MMC are analysed and compared. Subsequently, the stability analysis of the grid-connected MMC with the two droop control structures is conducted. Finally, time-domain simulation results are presented to verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Capacity requirement analysis of the auxiliary MMC in the series-connected hybrid diode rectifier for integrating offshore wind farms
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The flexible diode rectifier (FDR), which consists of a series-connected diode rectifier (DR) and an auxiliary modular multilevel converter (MMC), shows great promise for large-scale offshore wind farms (OFWs) connected to high-voltage dc transmission (HVdc) links. However, determining the required capacity of the auxiliary MMC to ensure the stable operation is of utmost importance. This consideration not only impacts the system’s stability but also its economic viability. This study analyses the capacity requirements of the auxiliary MMC from steady-state and dynamic-state perspectives, and proposes a capacity design methodology. The analysis results indicate that by installing fixed passive filters and wind turbines to provide appropriate reactive power compensation, the capacity of the auxiliary MMC can be designed to be around 15% of the rated transmission capacity. To validate the analysis results, simulations are conducted using a 2000MW/±500kV HVDC link based on a series-connected DR-MMC configuration for an OFW.

articleTitle: Development of a multi-pulse rectifier power supply
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the continuous development of power electronics technology, rectifier power supply equipment is facing the urgent need of green transformation. The conventional rectifier power supply device has high output voltage ripple and large input current harmonic content, which seriously affects the power quality of the power grid and the normal operation of the sensitive load. The PWM modulation technology can effectively improve the above problems, but the cost is high, the reliability is relatively low, and the high-frequency noise and interference will be introduced. Therefore, this paper adopts the multi-pulse phase-shift rectifier technology based on the extended delta connection method. Firstly, the working principle is introduced, and then the design methods of its core components such as phase-shifting transformer, rectifier component and filter circuit are calculated and analysed, and the rationality of parameter design is verified by simulation. Finally, the performance test is conducted on the 220kW multi-pulse rectifier power supply prototype. The test results are basically consistent with the simulation results, which meets the engineering requirements, and provides a reference for the subsequent design of multi-pulse rectifier power supply devices.

articleTitle: Research on cooling structure improvement of hybrid commutation converter valve
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The power transformation process at the level of hundreds of MW generates significant loss, posing great challenges to the heat dissipation of the converter valve. This paper calculates the loss under overload conditions of a 120kV hybrid conversion converter (HCC) valve and proposes a design method for a thermal-balanced converter valve cooling structure. An improved model of the converter valve cooling structure is established, and flow distribution and thermal analyses are conducted. The results show that the improved cooling system can reduce the maximum surface temperature of the power device by 1.6°C, which decreases the temperature rise by 7.3%. The proposed thermal-balanced cooling method enhances the safety margin of the converter valve, and provides support for the thermal design of the converter valve.

articleTitle: Transmission line fast pilot protection using decaying DC information
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: with the widespread integration of large-scale new energy generation equipment into the power system and the rapid construction of ultra/high-voltage transmission lines, the transient processes of faults in modern power systems exhibit characteristics that are faster and have a wider impact range than traditional power grids. The consequences triggered after a fault occurrence are more severe, and extremely high requirements are imposed on the protective performance of transmission lines. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a transmission line fast pilot protection scheme based on the fault moment voltage phase angle and the information of the decaying DC component (DDC) after the fault. Firstly, the form of fault current is thoroughly analyzed; secondly, considering the premise of transition resistance, the relationship between the fault moment voltage phase angle and the polarity of DDC is clarified, and criteria for fault direction identification are proposed; finally, an extended FFT-based fast Prony solution algorithm is used to accelerate the identification speed of the required information. Through case studies, the proposed protection scheme can reliably and quickly identify grounding faults in transmission lines.

articleTitle: Research on the evaluation method of wireless charging interoperability based on frequency impedance spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Wireless power transmission has become a critical method of electricity consumption. Interoperability testing is crucial to guarantee the interoperability of wireless charging devices. However, traditional power-efficiency and port-impedance testing have not taken into account the influence of the operating frequency on interoperability. To solve this problem, a correlation model between frequency impedance spectrum and interoperability is established according to China's national standards. Then, an interoperability evaluation method utilizing frequency impedance spectroscopy is proposed. In comparison to traditional testing approaches, it offers comprehensive frequency testing and graded assessment of interoperable devices. Finally, a 3.3 kW simulation model was designed and compared with the power method to verify its accuracy.

articleTitle: A novel power distribution strategy for battery storage units in a large-scale station to improve system operating performance
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Large-scale battery energy storage systems have the advantages of rapid response speed and high regulation precision. Their widespread application contributes to the stable operation of power grids. Nowadays, the design of an optimal power distribution strategy for the storage units that maximizes the benefits of energy storage stations is a hot spot of research. This paper presents a comprehensive power distribution model, which is suitable for energy storage stations. The model incorporates multiple objective factors such as the output power, the depth of discharge (DOD), and the uniformity of the State of Charge (SOC). One of the advantages of the designed model is its capability to optimize the longevity of the energy storage systems by managing the SOC convergence effectively and minimizing life loss through judicious power allocation. This approach improves the reliability and efficiency of energy storage system operations. Additionally, the model integrates temperature regulation costs, further enhancing its applicability and relevance to practical scenarios.

articleTitle: An enhanced LVRT control for photovoltaic systems with supercapacitor and crowbar
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Distributed photovoltaic (PV) generation systems are crucial for the utilization of renewable energy sources. Grid guidelines require that grid-connected convertors must have low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) capability. For two-stage grid-connected PV convertors, the input and output power imbalance during LVRT can result DC bus voltage fluctuations, which seriously lead to LVRT failure. To solve this problem, crowbar circuit or energy storage devices are commonly used, but both solutions have disadvantages, such as high losses or low reliability. In this work, a LVRT control strategy based on cooperative control of supercapacitor (SC) and crowbar circuit is presented. During LVRT, both devices absorb power together, and adjust the power distribution ratio according to the SC terminal voltage. After the fault removal, the SC can feed back energy into the grid. This method can improve the reliability of system LVRT while reducing the cost of SCs and improving the utilization of solar energy. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified by theoretical analysis and simulation.

articleTitle: Study on the pollution flashover performance of internal components of converter valves across diverse altitude levels
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This experiment study investigates the pollution flashover performance of external insulating components in UHV engineering converter valves, including single-stage thyristors and insulator rings. Through pollution flashover tests of single- stage thyristors under three typical salt density conditions, namely 0.03mg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 0.05 mg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and 0.08 mg/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>at 45m and 2500m altitude (simulated) and 70% and 100% humidity, respectively, the corresponding discharge characteristics of pollution flashover were obtained. The results show that under 70% and 100% humidity conditions, the altitude correction factor for single-stage thyristors is 6.4% and 7.8%, respectively. Additionally, pollution flashover tests on converter valve's insulator rings at different altitudes were carried out to find out the altitude correction pattern. These research findings can be used to guide the design of external insulation for converter valves in high-altitude regions.

articleTitle: Model predictive control for triple-active-bridge with low computational cost in microgrids
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The triple-active-bridge (TAB) converter, renowned for its flexible power flow paths, high power density, and diverse voltage levels, has garnered widespread attention in the microgrid. However, the port coupling of the TAB converter leads to a slow dynamic response and voltage fluctuations at different ports. Continuous control set model predictive control (CCS-MPC) achieves port decoupling while ensuring excellent dynamic performance compared to the traditional proportional-integral (PI) control. Nonetheless, CCS-MPC faces challenges in solving cost functions and computational complexity. A low computational cost CCS-MPC has been proposed to address these issues. Interleaving computation of phase-shift angles circumvents complex nonlinear equations solving, and the computational load and complexity are significantly reduced while preserving the superior control performance of CCS-MPC. Finally, simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Enhancing short-term overcurrent capability of MMC for energy storage system by active circulating current injection
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Certain applications of modular multilevel converter (MMC), such as MMC based super capacitor energy storage system, require MMC to have improved short-term overcurrent capability. This paper proposes an active circulating current injection control method to enhance short-term overcurrent capability of MMC. The positive peak current and negative peak current in the arm of an MMC exhibit asymmetry during active power conversion. Based on this characteristic, the asymmetry can be equalized by the injected circulating current to suppress the peak current of the MMC arm. Thus, potential damage to switching devices caused by overcurrent can be avoided. This paper analyzes the ability of the proposed method to reduce the peak current of the MMC arm, and verifies the effectiveness of the proposed method through the simulation model of the MMC based super capacitor energy storage system.

articleTitle: Planning method for the UHVDC access of UHVDC feed area
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In order to meet the new UHVDC feed area security and stable access, on the basis of the existing engineering experience, the research and puts forward the UHVDC terminal converter station in the landing point selection, technical route and AC side voltage access planning method of more feed, through the analysis of the engineering case, verify the rationality of the proposed planning method, for the subsequent feed into UHVDC engineering terminal converter station grid planning and access system scheme.

articleTitle: Location method for cable defects based on frequency domain reflectometry-constant false alarm rate
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In the process of cable defect location, conventional Frequency Domain Reflectometry (FDR) methods directly determine the defect position through the cable location spectrum, which gets low accuracy and efficiency. To solve this problem, Constant False Alarm Rate (CFAR) is introduced into FDR in this paper, and a comprehensive location method for cable defects based on FDR-CFAR is proposed. Firstly, by deriving the broadband impedance spectrum at the head of the cable and using Fourier transform to extract the characteristic information of the spectrum, the preliminary location result of the defective cable is obtained. Secondly, the data in the location spectrum is substituted into CFAR for one-dimensional calculation, which gets a threshold selected according to the variation of the amplitude at the data point. Only when the amplitude is higher than the threshold, is the data retained to extract the effective cable amplitude information and the corresponding defect position, which can optimize the defect location results. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified based on simulation and experiments on 800m and 870m cables. It is indicated that the proposed method can significantly improve the identification of cable defects, and the location error is within 0.35%.

articleTitle: Research on pollution zone division and external insulation configuration for ±800kV UHVDC lines in Northern Shaanxi
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper investigates and analyzes the climatic environment, pollution source distribution and operation experience of nearby transmission and transformation equipment along the UHVDC transmission lines in the northern region of Shaanxi Province, China, and predicts the DC pollution level along the project. By summarizing and analyzing the pollution test data of insulators on the UHVDC transmission lines in the environmentally similar northwest region, the key pollution accumulation characteristics of insulators are identified, including the law of saturated pollution of insulators, and the differences of pollution accumulation between the upper and lower surfaces, between different string types and different umbrella types. Based on the test results, the key correction coefficient of the pollution withstand voltage method was obtained. Using the artificial pollution withstand voltage method, the recommended external insulation configuration of the ±800kV UHVDC transmission lines in northern Shaanxi are proposed, respectively, for different pollution levels based on the annual ESDD and saturated ESDD.

articleTitle: Reliability analysis of microgrid
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Energy storage is an effective measure to enhance the integration of high proportions of distributed renewable energy sources. Smart switches can quickly actuate during faults to reduce outage durations, while Electric Vehicle (EV) charging stations incorporating Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) strategies serve as flexible dispatch resources. All three are integral components for the development of smart grids. This paper first models intelligent distribution networks incorporating Information and Communication Technology (ICT). Subsequently, it provides a detailed overview of the reliability assessment process for smart distribution networks. Finally, utilizing the RELSAD simulation platform, the paper conducts reliability assessment analysis on distribution networks considering distributed renewable energy sources, energy storage, electric vehicles, and smart switches. The study analyzes the impact of various components in smart distribution networks on system reliability. Additionally, it evaluates the effects of microgrids and fault isolation and supply restoration on the reliability of smart distribution systems.

articleTitle: Electro-thermal modeling of MOSFET short-circuit condition based on field-circuit coupling
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Under extreme conditions represented by short-circuiting, Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor (MOSFET) devices exhibit significant self-heating effects, leading to device over-temperature failure. To clarify the electro-thermal characteristics of MOSFET devices under short-circuit conditions, this paper establishes a MOSFET circuit model considering temperature effects based on the PSPICE platform. Simultaneously, a thermal model of MOSFET is built on the COMSOL platform. The circuit model and thermal model are then coupled together in SIMULINK, and MATLAB scripts are used to control the electro-thermal simulation with different simulation step sizes to predict the electro-thermal characteristics of MOSFET under short-circuit conditions. Finally, the model is verified through short-circuit testing of INFINEON 650V MOSFET.

articleTitle: The multilevel turn-off method and improved detection circuit are proposed for SiC MOSFET short-circuit
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: SiC MOSFET has excellent characteristics such as low loss, high switching frequency and withstand voltage value, which shows significant advantages in power electronics applications. However, its short-circuit tolerance is weak, and the protection circuit needs to have a faster response speed. Besides, under higherdI/dtanddV/dtconditions, the fast response and anti-noise ability of the SiC MOSFET short-circuit protection circuit are difficult to balance. In order to ensure the safe and reliable operation of SiC MOSFET, a detection circuit of desaturation voltage with compensation circuit is proposed, which reduces the influence of temperature change and load fluctuation on detection accuracy. At the same time, a multi-stage gate voltage reduction method is proposed, which can limit the increase of short-circuit current and improve the time of short-circuit fault detection blind zone to reduce the influence of interference noise. It can also reduce the change rate of short-circuit current and limit the turn-off overvoltage.

articleTitle: Multi-resolution optimization methodology of voltage and reactive power in new distribution systems
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Due to carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, the new distribution system for energy connection will become the development direction of the AC and DC distribution system in the future. With the high penetration of intermittent distributed energy resources and flexible load, the problems of voltage violation and fluctuation have been becoming more and more serious. Thus the urgent need arises to solve the problem of voltage and reactive power optimization in the new distribution system. In this paper, the multi-resolution model definition and its background are presented at first. Secondly, a multi-resolution optimization model of voltage and reactive power is proposed to analyse dynamic operation characteristics of the new distribution system caused by the stochastic nature of distributed energy resources and load. And then based on the above model, the corresponding optimization methodology is proposed. The simulation results show that the proposed model and methodology can not only provide systematic descriptions of dynamic operation characteristics, but also greatly reduce the computational burden and make the analysis less time-consuming. Therefore, it is significantly meaningful to make safe and stable operation of the new distribution system.

articleTitle: Transformer vibration state anomaly detection based on Jensen-Shannon divergence and ensemble learning
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Vibration analysis of transformers is significant importance for the detection of internal mechanical faults and abnormal conditions in power transformers. Traditional vibration analysis methods face limitations in processing data under complex environments. In pursuit of superior vibration analysis methods, this paper introduces a novel vibration analysis approach combining Jensen-Shannon divergence and ensemble learning. Initially, kernel density estimation and Jensen-Shannon divergence are utilized to assess the variability in transformer vibration data. Subsequently, an ensemble model based on Extra Trees Classifier and Logistic Regression is constructed to improve the accuracy and efficiency of fault diagnosis. Experimental results demonstrate the method's effectiveness in enhancing the robustness of vibration data analysis, offering new perspectives for transformer fault diagnosis and maintenance. The methodology and findings of this research hold significant importance for advancing transformer vibration analysis technologies.

articleTitle: Partial discharge signals denoising by the combination of signal decomposition and adaptive filtering
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Accurate detection of partial discharge (PD) signals emitted from gas-insulated equipment is essential for identifying potential insulation faults. However, existing PD denoising methods cannot adaptively adjust model parameters based on signal characteristics, thus limiting their generalization ability and accuracy in complex noise environments. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a parameter-adaptive PD denoising strategy based on an intelligent optimization algorithm framework. The strategy involves constructing a PD denoising program that integrates signal decomposition, entropy criteria, and filtering analysis. To enhance the program's adaptability to signals with diverse characteristics, an adaptive strategy i s introduced. Simulation results demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed method in denoising composite signals with complex components.

articleTitle: Research on suppression method of commutation recognition for modulator in weak receiving end HVDC transmission system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper presents a method using a phase shifting device to suppress the weak receiving-end high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system. Firstly, the inverse-side DC current is taken as the characteristic quantity, and its S-transform energy entropy is calculated to propose a phase failure detection method based on S-transform energy entropy. Then, the working principle of synchronous phase shifting device (SC) is analyzed. The synchronous phase shifting device is connected to the inverter side of the HVDC transmission system to suppress phase failure. Finally, a simulation model of the DC transmission system and phase shifting device is built on the PSCAD platform. The suppression effect is judged by the change in turn-off angle and the magnitude of the inverter side bus voltage. The simulation results show that the proposed method can accurately detect phase failure; the introduction of synchronous phase shifting device can suppress phase failure.

articleTitle: Versatile static synchronous machine based offshore wind farm integration scheme
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The modular multilevel converter (MMC) and energy storage are hot topics in the field of electrical engineering. The versatile static synchronous machine (VSSM) is proposed by combining MMC and energy storage, which can be used in the new type power systems with a large number of non-synchronous electromechanical sources. In this paper, the VSSM is applied to DC transmission for the offshore wind farm integration scheme based on power-frequency grid-following wind turbine, and the advantages of the VSSM as an inverter are analysed. The topology structure, submodule structure and related parameters of the VSSM based on energy-usage energy storage (EES) and the VSSM based on power-usage energy storage (PES) are determined by specific examples. This paper simulates the three-phase grounding short circuit faults of the offshore and onshore power grid of the offshore wind power transmission system based on two kinds of VSSMs by PSCAD/EMTDC, and the bidirectional AC/DC fault isolation of the VSSM is verified. It is proved that the application of VSSM in the new type power systems is viable and advantageous.

articleTitle: Study of power forward and reverse operation flexibility enhancement for back-to-back DC project
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Flexible interconnected multi-district grid operation will be the development trend of the Southern Power Grid. In view of the difficulty of the existing flexible control technology to meet the demand of flexible interconnected grid operation and security and stability under the new type of electric power system, the study of flexible control based on the multi-district grid operation flexibility and stability of the initiative to support the technology, put forward the whole area of the power flexible control technology, and the flexible project in Guangdong, Guangdong, South Guangdong and other projects have been successfully implemented, which greatly enhance the economy, flexibility and stability of partitioned grid operation, and promote the construction of "reasonable partitioning, flexible interconnection, security control, open mutual aid" main grid framework. It has greatly improved the economy, flexibility and stability of sub-district grid operation, and promoted the construction of the main grid framework of "reasonable sub-district, flexible interconnection, safe and controllable, open and mutual aid".

articleTitle: Operational performance analysis of CLCC-HVDC and LCC-HVDC based on electromagnetic transient simulation
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The new controllable line-commutated converter (CLCC) with controllable trip capability not only retains the large capacity and low cost of the conventional LCC in topology and control strategy, but also withstands the phase change failure under various AC faults. To verify the operational performance and reliability of the DC transmission system based on the CLCC converter, a CLCC-HVDC simulation model is developed within PSCAD/EMTDC. The transient performance of the LCC HVDC and the CLCC HVDC is compared under the same model. The simulation results show that, compared with LCC-HVDC, CLCC-HVDC has good suppression of phase-change failure under various operating conditions and still has good power-transmitting capability under AC faults.

articleTitle: SF6 DC circuit breaker and its fault isolation method in half-bridge MMC system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The size and cost of DC circuit breakers has been a limiting factor in their diffusion. Although SF6 circuit breakers can convert DC currents of several kiloampere levels, their inherent slower separation speed makes them more difficult to be applied in the field of DC fault isolation. However, with the advancement of MMC regulation technology, SF6 DC circu it breakers may be able to lead from load current conversion to fault disconnection with its unique advantage of highly reliable arc quenching.

articleTitle: Experimental study on low frequency discharge characteristics of typical gap
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Offshore flexible low frequency power transmission and transformation equipment will face the test of special environmental conditions of high humidity. Systematic study of the low frequency discharge characteristics of air gaps under varying humidity levels is required to guarantee the economics and safety of offshore transmission systems in external insulation. In this paper, The rod-plate gap's low frequency and power frequency discharge characteristics under relative humidity of 40% (normal temperature), 60% and 100% are tested. The low frequency and power frequency discharge characteristics curves under various humidity and gap distance conditions are obtained, and the test data are analysed. The results show that the low frequency and power frequency discharge voltages of 0.2m–0.4m rod-plate gap under different humidity are close, and the relative deviation is less than 6%.

articleTitle: Passive based control method for high compact and wide bidirectional DC/DC converter
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a bidirectional DC/DC converter suitable for wide input and output range is analysed. Compared with the traditional bidirectional DC/DC converter, the DC/DC converter has higher integration and efficiency, and can be built by external capacitors and inductors through intelligent power module (IPM). Passive analysis and controller design are performed in the Buck and Boost modes of the converter. Simulink is used for simulation to evaluate the performance of the converter under passive control (PBC) for constant power loads (CPL) and constant resistance loads (CRL). The results show that the converter with PBC strategy has better steady-state and dynamic performance than the converter with PI control strategy.

articleTitle: Research on the optimal path of live working personnel entering UHV transmission tower based on ideal solution method
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper simulates and calculates the electric field distribution characteristics of the main fitting surface and personnel surface of the jumper string in the process of entering and exiting equipotential in order to study the optimal path . Eight methods for entering and leaving equipotential are chosen based on the UHV tension tower's jumper construction and the custom of doing so using the pendulum method. When the operators reached the equipotential via various paths, the dynamic variations in the field strength values on the surface of the personnel and the large and small rings at the high voltage end of the jumper string were examined. The maximum field strength, average field strength, etc, based on the electrostatic field simulation results. The advantages and disadvantages of various equipotential entry modes are sorted by method-ideal solution method. Lastly, the optimal equipotential entrance path is suggested taking into account the jumper's structural properties and the real operating environment.

articleTitle: A magnetically controlled bridge arm reactor topology design for MMC applications
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: A bridge arm reactor is a type of reactor connected in series to the bridge arm of a voltage source converter, which is widel y used in MMCs, and mainly serves to suppress bridge arm circulating currents and bridge arm fault currents that rise too fast during short circuits. The inductance of the bridge arm reactors used so far is a fixed value, which cannot suppress the curr ent well. In this paper, a magnetically controlled bridge arm reactor is proposed, which combines the mutual inductance of the coil and the saturation of the iron core, and can automatically change the inductance value according to the working conditions, showing a larger inductance value for the circulating current and the fault, and a smaller inductance value for the AC working current, which is better to play a role, and does not affect the normal operation of the system. A prototype is designed according to the topology principle and finite element simulation is carried out in ANSYS to verify its electromagnetic and inductive characteristics, and the designed magnetically controlled bridge arm reactor performs well in the simulation.

articleTitle: Research on snow removal method of ultra high voltage DC composite bushing based on hot water jet
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The snow cover on the high-voltage composite insulation bushing leads to a decrease in its external insulation performance, thereby causing the risk of flashover. Currently, there is no technical means available for snow removal of ultra/ultra-high composite insulation bushing. This article compares the effectiveness of snow removal methods in a large-scale artificial environment climate laboratory, selects hot water jet as the snow removal method of composite insulation bushing. The research results indicate that safe length of the water column for snow removal at a voltage level of ± 500kV is not less than 6m. When the water column and the horizontal plane of the casing are at a dip angle of 5 °~10 °, snow accumulation on the front and back of the bushing can be removed simultaneously. When carrying out snow removal of composite insulation bushing with electricity, the sequence should be followed: high voltage end - middle section - low voltage end or middle section - high voltage end - low voltage end, and this working sequence ensures the safe operation of the composite insulation bushing during the snow removal process.

articleTitle: High-frequency resonance suppression of MMC-HVDC systems under frequency divided active damping control
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In the modular multilevel converter (MMC) based high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system, the high-frequency negative damping effect of the MMC output impedance induces high frequency resonances. The existing active damping controls, such as the virtual series impedance, change the range of high-frequency negative damping effects, thereby suppressing the high-frequency resonances (HFRs). However, it can only be applied to the single operating condition of AC power grid because the single damping controller cannot effectively reshape the impedance characteristics of MMC in multiple HFR risk regions simultaneously. Therefore, a frequency divided active damping control (FDADC) is proposed to address the suppression requirements of multiple HFR risk regions. Based on the simplified model of the MMC in high-frequency band, the analytical calculation method and expressions for the parameters’ selection ranges of the frequency divided damping controller are presented. The parameters of damping controller suitable for multiple operating conditions of AC systems are given, and their effectiveness is verified through electromagnetic transient simulation models.

articleTitle: Admittance shaping of multiple converters systems based on modal power
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of the renewable generation, small-signal instability of multi-converter system (MCS) may arise. This paper presents a converter admittance shaping method based on modal power theory. This paper proposes a stability enhancing converter control method, which demonstrates how the admittance shaping of converters increases the stability margin and eventually suppresses oscillation without reducing the dynamic performance. The admittance shaping method can improve the output characteristics of the converter, which ensures the stability of the MCS. Theoretical analysis and simulations demonstrate that this method can enhance the stability of the system and the performance of the converter, which provides a simple and effective solution for improving the adaptability of the converter to the power grid .

articleTitle: Research on voltage control strategy of microgrid with adaptive virtual damping and capacitance
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: To mitigate the impact of distributed photovoltaic (PV) integration on the power distribution network through energy storage microgrids in the Xuejiawan area, this paper proposes a control strategy that focuses on the stability of the direct current (DC) voltage at the point of common coupling (PCC). Initially, the internal stability of the energy storage microgrid is assessed using a virtual damping analysis method, ensuring voltage stability upon integration with the grid. Subsequently, an adaptive virtual capacitance-based voltage control approach is employed to stabilize the DC voltage at the PCC when multiple microgrids are interconnected. This dual strategy not only diminishes the impact of energy storage microgrids on the power distribution network but also minimizes the influence of the distribution network on the microgrids. Finally, a Simulink-based simulation platform is constructed to analyze the proposed control methods. The simulation results indicate that the Nyquist plot shifts towards the right half of the complex plane, suggesting an enhancement in the stability of the direct current microgrid system compared to traditional droop-based voltage control methods.

articleTitle: Power loss calculation for hybrid commutated converter
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Hybrid commutated converter (HCC) value adopts the reverse blocking integrated gate commutated thyristor(IGCT), which solves the problem of commutation failure, and the volume and interface are consistent with the traditional thyristor valve. So, the HCC value is selected as a reconstruction topology in the Lingbao project. The HCC valve adopts a new type of device, it is necessary to study the loss characteristics of the HCC valve. This paper takes the HCC valve of the Lingbao project as an example, firstly, the theoretical calculation of single-valve loss is carried out, and the total loss per valve is 92.59 kW. Then, the loss test platform is set up, and the loss test is carried out, and the result proves that the theoretical calculation and the test have a good agreement. Finally, the loss comparison and analysis with the thyristor valve are carried out, and the results show that the power loss (1.0 p.u.) of the IGCT valve is only 1.01% higher than that of the thyristor valve.

articleTitle: Scheduling optimization of distribution-microgrid coordination based on flexible DC interconnection
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: When the number and capacity of grid-connected operating new energy sources reaches a high level of penetration, microgrids can significantly affect the distribution system. Most of the current solutions either focus solely on distribution system or solely on microgrids. There are few studies that consider involvement in distribution-microgrid coordination. In order to solve the above problem, a multi-objective coordinated architecture based on flexible DC interconnections is proposed. A method of controlling active power with DC interconnection between microgrids is adopted to realize the source-load power balance of the distribution system. The distribution-microgrid multi-objective coordinated architecture is able to take into account the comprehensive benefits of the distribution system and microgrid. It can reduce the active network losses at the distribution layer and ensure that the economic and environmental indicators at the microgrid layer are dynamically balanced.
