An optimization scheduling model for the multi-objective coordinated architecture of distribution-microgrid is proposed, focusing on objectives of reliability and cost-effectiveness. Additionally, a particle swarm optimization algorithm with stochastic inertia weights is introduced to globally optimize the conflicting objectives. The simulation results verify the validity of the scheduling optimization for distribution-microgrid coordination. Moreover, the significance of flexible DC interconnection in controlling active power is verified.

articleTitle: Small-signal stabillity analysis of flux-controlled grid-forming DFIG under weak grid
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the continuous increase of global wind power installed capacity, the modern power system gradually shows the characteristics of weak damping, low inertia, and weak anti-interference ability. Aiming at the normal grid-connected wind tur-bine under weak grid conditions, the small signal stability of the flux-controlled grid-forming DFIG is analysed. Firstly, the small-signal model of the flux-controlled grid-forming DFIG is constructed based on the flux-controlled virtual synchronous generator control (VSG). Then, the eigenvalue analysis method is used to investigate the influence of different operating conditions and controller parameters on the small-signal stabilization of system. Besides, the dominant factors of low-frequency oscillatory modes are analysed based on the participation factor matrix. Finally, the safety and stability boundaries of each influencing factor are calculated by oscillation modal analysis, which provides guidance for the parameter design of the DFIG under weak grid.

articleTitle: Fault monitoring layout optimization based on acoustic simulation of 500kV transformer
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Large transformers are important devices in the new energy transmission system, and their operational stability is crucial to the power system. Ultrasonic monitoring method is a commonly used means of online monitoring of transformers, but the existing studies mainly focus on transformers of 220kV and below. In order to solve the problem of less research on the characteristics of ultrasonic signal distribution in large transformers, and to provide guidance on the layout method for the application of ultrasonic monitoring method in large transformers, this paper uses the finite element method to simulate the distribution of ultrasonic signals in 500kV transformers, and analyzes the characteristics of ultrasonic signals in different common installation positions, which provides a theoretical basis for the rapid sensing of winding faults on large transformers by ultrasonic detection method.

articleTitle: Study of hydrogen production power supply based on current source rectifier topology
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper investigates a hydrogen production power supply topology based on current source rectifiers for the application scenario of high-power hydrogen production power supply system. The system equations in the dq coordinate system are established, and the decoupled inner-loop control method is examined. Additionally, it provides an overall control scheme and equalization control method for multiple current source rectifiers connected in parallel. This paper analyses the effects of different positions of the current source rectifier damping resistor on resonance suppression for the grid-side LC filter. It suggests a passive damping configuration. The correctness and feasibility of the proposed control strategy are verified through PSCAD/EMTDC. The hydrogen generation power supply of the current source type exhibits good dynamic and static characteristics, ensuring a high quality of grid-side current and a high power factor.

articleTitle: An online estimation method of nodal inertia parameters based on steady state operation of power system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper proposes an online estimation method of node inertia and damping factor using node data during steady-state operation of power systems. Firstly, the data are pre-processed after fed back from phase measurement units (PMUs), and then the node active power deviation is taken as input and frequency deviation as output. The multivariate output error state spac e (MOESP) and prediction error minimization (PEM) composite algorithms are applied to identify the parameters of the system state-space model at the nodes, from which node inertia and damping factor can then be extracted. The method accelerates the iteration process by identifying the optimal system parameters through the MOESP algorithm. These parameters are then refined through the PEM algorithm, utilising the identified local optimal solutions as a starting point. This approach mitiga tes the impact of random errors on parameter identification, enhancing the accuracy and robustness of the identification process. Finally, the efficacy and precision of the proposed methodology are validated in the IEEE 9-bus system.

articleTitle: Research on junction temperature estimation model of RB-IGCT continuous switching process
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In H-LCC applications, RB-IGCT needs to operate reliably after continuous switching cycles. The primary challenge is ensuring that the junction temperature of the device remains within safe limits during and after these cycles. Accurate yet simple estimation of junction temperature fluctuations is crucial for device safety. This paper proposed a Foster thermal resistance and capacitor network model based on a simplified power consumption function. The model's accuracy was verified using the Temperature Sensitive Electrical Parameter method. Results indicate that the relative deviation between the junction temperature values obtained from both methods does not exceed 1.1%, confirming the model's reliability.

articleTitle: Optimal dispatch of power system including wind and solar power generation considering carbon trading-green certificate and energy storage cost
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In order to promote the green development and energy saving and emission reduction of traditional power industry, this paper introduces the carbon trade-green certificate mechanism and electric energy storage into the optimal scheduling of power system. Firstly, on the basis of the initial allocation of carbon allowances, compensation allowances are added to thermal power units, and a system carbon transaction cost model is established. Then, construct an optimal dispatch model aiming at the lowest total cost, comprehensively considering the cost of carbon trading mechanism, the cost of green certificate mechanism, the operating cost of energy storage, the operating cost of conventional thermal power units, wind power, photovoltaics and various constraints of the system condition. Finally, a simulation example shows that the carbon trade-green certificate mechanism and the introduction of energy storage can effectively reduce the carbon emissions of the system.

articleTitle: Analysis of power system inertial demand considering frequency security and stability constraints
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Under the background of new energy large-scale grid integration, the inertia of the power system gradually decreases, which brings great challenges to the operation of the power grid. The unclear demand of inertia will restrict the carrying capacity and frequency stability of the power system, and there is an urgent need to find an inertial demand analysis method considering the frequency security and stability constraints. This paper begins by outlining the source and definition of inertia. According to the dynamic frequency response characteristics of the power system, it finds the relationship between system inertia and frequency. Then, based on the relevant frequency stability indicators, a method is proposed to determine the critical inertia that takes into account the rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and the deviation constraints of the frequency. Finally, an improved IEEE9 node example is built on the PSCAD/EMTDC platform to prove the reliability of the theory proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Unified implicit Z-bus power flow solver for hybrid AC/DC distribution networks
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In the future power system, characterized by the massive integration of distributed energy resources (DERs), the AC/DC hybrid network represents a highly promising technology that will play a crucial role at power distribution levels. As essential analytical tools for AC/DC distribution networks, Newton-Raphson (N-R) based unified AC/DC power flow methods have been developed and widely used. However, the N-R method encounters challenges such as divergence, multiple solutions, and high sensitivity to initial values when solving power flow problems in distribution networks, particularly in radial and meshed distribution network topologies, especially under conditions of high R/X ratios or heavy loads. To address these issues, this paper presents a novel unified AC/DC power flow algorithm based on the implicit Z-bus (IZB) method. Considering the various combinations of nodes and feeders in AC/DC hybrid distribution networks, a unified power flow solver based on an IZB iterative mapping is proposed. Numerical tests validate the proposed solver, demonstrating its superior capability to achieve high computational efficiency while reliably converging to feasible solutions without being influenced by the choice of high R/X ratios, initial values, and heavy loads.

articleTitle: Optimized operation of a multi-platform virtual power plant combining energy efficiency and carbon efficiency service mechanisms
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: A virtual power plant is a management system used to maintain the balance of demand between electricity consumption measurement and generation measurement, which is able to integrate the source, network, load and storage data in a new type of power system to realize collaborative operation and management. In this paper, we propose a multi-platform virtual power plant optimization scheme that combines energy efficiency and carbon efficiency service mechanisms. Specifically, we first integrate various distributed resource equipment parameters, performance and timing data to establish a virtual power plant model based on multi-platform data. In addition, we use the hash data storage algorithm and multi-scale multivariate sample entropy to complete the cluster analysis and discrete mining of cloud platform data. Secondly, we propose the source-grid-load-storage co-optimization strategy, and introduce a variety of source-grid-load-storage optimization solution methods. Finally, the method of combining virtual power plant with energy efficiency and carbon efficiency services is proposed to form a complete operation scheme.

articleTitle: Accurate frequency domain model for stability analysis of VSC considering sideband effect
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Accurate small-signal modelling provides theoretical guidance for effectively addressing the oscillation problem in a grid-tied renewable energy system. The grid-tied inverter is classified as a multi-input multi-output (MIMO) system due to the sideband effect of sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM). The sideband effect refers to the periodic expansion of the frequency domain response of SPWM cantered on the switching frequency when subjected to small signal disturbance input at a specific frequency. This paper presents a comprehensive research and analysis of SPWM and develops an accurate frequency domain model using the mathematical framework of harmonic transfer function (HTF). The model effectively illustrates the impact of the SPWM sideband effect on the frequency domain response of VSC systems and exhibits a high level of accuracy across a broad range of frequencies. Furthermore, the MIMO model is equivalent to the SISO model for stability analysis. The simulation results of the electromagnetic transient (EMT) model validate the accuracy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Cathode-side natural microchannel heat sink for IGCT
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Heat dissipation has become a critical problem for the develepoment of IGCT on-state current and capacity. This paper proposed a method of cathode-side natural microchannel cooling, which takes advantage of the cell structure on the cathode-side of the chip and integrates microchannel heat sink within the device package. After research on the effect of main flow direction and serial number of cell-microchannel-ring, the cathode-side natural microchannel structure with radial main flow and single-cell-ring microchannel is found to achieve the optimum pumping power at the same temperature rise.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of different neural networks on intelligent detection of transmission line external damages
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In power system, identifying and eliminating the risks of overhead transmission line external damages plays a crucial role in ensuring safe operation of the grid. Image recognition technology based on deep learning algorithms serves as an effective method for identifying these external damages, but the detection speed and detection accuracy for different image recognition methods varies depending on the defect types and locations. In this paper, three different image recognition algorithms, i.e., YOLOv3, Faster R-CNN and Mask R-CNN deep learning models are used for detecting typical external damages of overhead transmission lines such as cranes and excavators. The detection accuracy and detection frame are compared for indicating the detection efficiencies of different neural networks. Case studies on the transmission line external damage dataset provided by State Grid of China show that all the three models could achieves a best average precision of approximately 90%, whereas Mask R-CNN generally owns the highest average precision and YOLOv3 owns the highest frame rate in detecting large machinery.

articleTitle: MMC-HVDC system with embedded ESS for large-scale renewable energy transmission
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-voltage direct current (HVDC) overhead-line transmission system with embedded energy storage system (ESS) to address the challenges posed by large-scale renewable energy transmission over long-distance. The system is designed to provide power support, suppress power fluctuations, and clear DC faults effectively. An innovative grid-stabilizing converter (GSC) with an integrated ESS, comprising new submodules (SMs), is installed in both rectifier and inverter stations. This paper includes an analysis of the operating principle of the proposed transmission system, a study on the development mechanism of GSC short-circuit fault current, and the proposal of control strategies for active power support, fast frequency response, and DC fault ride-through. Furthermore, a corresponding simulation model is constructed to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed transmission system. The results demonstrate that, with the proposed transmission system and reasonable control strategies, the delivery of large-scale fluctuating renewables energy can be achieved smoothly and stably. Moreover, the active power support and fault ride-through control of GSC exhibit effective performance during transmission.

articleTitle: Evolution analysis of stability characteristics of power systems with dominating nonsynchronous resources via voltage source converters
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The growing penetration level of power-electronics-based generation has brought unprecedented stability issues in modern power systems. Due to the relatively weak overcurrent capability of power electronics devices, voltage source converters (VSCs) are more prone to run into current saturation mode, causing transient instability issues. This paper proposes a novel simulation-based spatial-temporal integration analysis (SSTIA) method to characterize the stability evolution trends of the power system with growing penetration of nonsynchronous generation via VSCs. By setting the spatial distribution characteristics of power and disturbances, a stability mapping relationship in the spatial domain is derived. The destabilization mode of stable boundary cases can be investigated in the time domain based on spatial stability evolution while remapping key modes back to the dynamics of the control loop. Based on the modified IEEE 3-machine-9-bus system, two types of dominant instability factors are revealed by utilizing the proposed SSTIA approach. For a system with grid-following converters (GFLCs) and a synchronous generator (SG), fast active power support is required to maintain stability. For the system with GFLC, grid-forming converter (GFMC), and SG, the proportional gainK pof GFMC in inner voltage loop and setting ofi q,maxsignificantly affect the current desaturation and stability process of the system.

articleTitle: Bi-level planning of power system considering hybrid carbon leakage
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Under the carbon neutrality goals, hybrid carbon leakage due to asymmetric emission regulation of the power industry merits greater attention. This paper proposes a bi-level planning model based on carbon emission flow and locational marginal prices considering the power grid expansion in upper transmission level and the Energy Hub (EH) load transfer in lower distribution level. Moreover, mitigation measures of carbon leakage are assessed and modeled, following which provides the solution flow and bisection-based convergence method of the bi-level planning model. Simulation results verify the impact of hybrid carbon leakage in power system planning, illustrate the role and risks of mitigation measures and discuss the convergence of the proposed model and moreover provide knowledge of reasonable emission regulation in the low-carbon path of the power system.

articleTitle: Impact of PCB mechanical drilling on insulation and mechanical performance
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the increasing performance requirements of electronic devices for PCB, especially the voltage level, the electrical safety and structural stability requirements for printed circuit boards (PCBs) are also increasing. This study focuses on improving the insulation capability of PCB through drilling technology, establishes a dual-pad analysis system, and utilizes finite element analysis to evaluate the effect of different hole shapes, quantities, and positions on system insulation improvement based on indicators such as creepage distance and electric field distribution. Furthermore, considering the impact of holes on the mechanical strength of the PCB, a compromised optimal design of the PCB board is achieved, and an optimized structure with a double-slot configuration at the trisection position is selected.

articleTitle: AC fault ride-through strategy for large-scale photovoltaic power transmitted by VSC-HVDC
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In this study, the fault characteristics and fault ride-through strategies of large-scale photovoltaic (PV) systems transmitted via voltage source converter based direct current (VSC-HVDC) are investigated. Initially, the topology and fundamental control strategy of large-scale PV systems transmitted by VSC-HVDC are outlined. Subsequently, the fault characteristics of the large-scale PV systems transmitted by VSC-HVDC are examined, and the mechanisms of rectifier station controller saturation and power surplus contributing to system overvoltage are analyzed. Following this, control strategies for the rectifier station and the PV station during AC faults in the sending-end grid are proposed. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed control strategy is validated through PSCAD/EMTDC electromagnetic transient simulations.

articleTitle: DC fault protection assessment of medium voltage DC (MVDC) systems for offshore wind energy transmission
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Medium voltage DC (MVDC) systems have the advantages of fewer conversion stages and lower power losses in the MVDC collector for offshore wind energy transmission and can avoid the need of costly offshore platforms, leading to significant reduction of the capital cost. In this paper, DC fault protection of MVDC systems is assessed considering both parallel and series connection arrangements of wind turbine converters. Typical DC fault protection strategies considering selective, non-selective, and partially selective fault clearing will be assessed and their impact on fault currents and voltages and the AC onshore and MVDC offshore network will be studied. The use of different DC protection devices including fast acting DC circuit breakers (DCCBs) and DC switches/disconnectors (DCSWs), and their locations on protection and system recovery will be highlighted.

articleTitle: Online automatic analysis application methods of power grid fault and relay protection operation
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: After a power grid fault, dispatching operation, relay protection, maintenance, and other professionals urgently need to analyze and diagnose the power grid failure. They must determine the fault location, fault type, and whether the protection operation is correct. Currently, in practical applications, fault diagnosis and protection operation analysis are primarily conducted through manual analysis using fault records and protection operation reports. This process demands high technical proficiency from personnel, suffers from low analysis efficiency, and is both time-consuming and laborious. Various fault analysis and protection operation analysis methods proposed by researchers encounter issues when applied to power grids, such as difficulty in information matching, inapplicability of algorithms, and inaccurate analysis results. This article proposes an online automatic analysis scheme for power grid faults and protection operations. It employs methods such as information matching, sampling anomaly recognition, fault location, and protection operation rationality (correctness) analysis and evaluation. This scheme solves the problem of inapplicability of existing online fault and protection operation analysis methods in practical applications.

articleTitle: Development of conductor galloping distribution maps of Shandong province, China
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In winter, freezing rain may lead to eccentric icing on conductors. Due to the effects of steady wind on eccentric icing, the conductor may feature a low frequency, high amplitude vibration, which is conductor galloping. The conductor galloping can lead to electric and mechanical damage to overhead transmission lines. In this paper, based on the study on more than 1000 conductor galloping events of overhead transmission lines in China, the thresholds of meteorological parameters which are likely to fulfill the conditions necessary for conductor galloping have been defined. Via the meteorological data from 1999 to 2023 of 122 weather stations, the galloping days for each station can be achieved. Then the total number of galloping days for each winter can be computed. The type I extreme value distribution model is employed as the probability distribution model to calculate the galloping days with specific return period for each station. Finally, the galloping distribution map for Shandong province, China can be depicted by ordinary kriging interpolation method integrated in the mapping software. It is suggested that, the 30a, 50a, and 100a galloping distribution map can be used to the planning and design of OHLs for 35kV~330kV, 500kV~750kV, ±800kV~1000kV, respectively. By utilizing the above-mentioned maps, differentiated design and maintenance can be issued for OHLs with different voltages.

articleTitle: Production simulation and analysis on flexible DC transmission of an offshore wind power with fixed-speed and variable-speed pumped storage units
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Variable-speed pumped storage units possess an ability to continuously regulate power during the pumping phase, which renders them more flexible and efficient compared to traditional fixed-speed units. This paper aims to investigate the effects of variable-speed pumped storage units on the technical attributes of offshore wind power. To achieve this, a simulation model is constructed to analyse the flexible DC transmission of offshore wind power with pumped storage. The model considers both fixed-speed and variable-speed units simultaneously. The test results demonstrate that incorporating a specific percentage of variable-speed units in the pumped storage power station can significantly enhance the flexibility of pumped storage regulation. This improvement can be reflected from the lower volatility of the outgoing power curve and the enhanced anti-peaking characteristics. These results can serve as a valuable technical reference for the future implementation of variable-speed pumped storage projects in the practical power systems.

articleTitle: Crucial nodes identification based on implicit linearized power flow for grids upgrade planning
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Transmission expansion planning and energy storage siting require the identification and selection of key nodes in the grids to maximize the benefits of new facilities. The power flow (PF) equation is a nonlinear smooth manifold in space, and we obtain an implicit linearized PF model by constructing the tangent plane of working points on the manifold. Based on this model, we further establish the sensitivity matrices of the change in line PF, branch squared PF and network loss with respect to the change in nodal power injection. These sensitivity matrices can not only identify the key nodes, but also take into account the effect of the coupling between active and reactive power and the operation status of the grids, which can provide scientific reference for the online adjustment of the systems. Finally, the correctness of the model is verified through case analysis.

articleTitle: Effect of metal particles on the surface charge buildup of GIL insulators under electro-thermal coupling field
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The objective is to address the pollution problem caused by adhered and moving tiny metal particles in the GIL cavity, the effect of adhered metal particles on the problem of the charge accumulation on the insulator surface under the influence of temperature gradient was studied. Taking into account effect of temperature on the volume conductivity of the insulator and the diffusion coefficient of charged ions on the gas side, a surface charge accumulation model including the arising, reorganisation, diffusion and transport of charged particles on the gas side was established, and the surface charge distribution on insulators was analyzed with or without the effect of metal particles analyze. The results show that the metal particles attached to the center electrode will cause distortion of the electric field around it; compared with no metal particles, the surface charge of metallic particles attached to the center electrode near the electrode increases significantly, and the surface charge distribution of the insulator changes, leading to an acceleration in the charge accumulation process.

articleTitle: A battery model parameter identification method considering topology reconfiguration
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In the field of battery circuit model parameter estimation, the combination of bilinear transformation with the least squares method has garnered widespread attention due to its excellent performance under continuous current conditions. However, in dynamic reconfigurable battery network (DRBN), the network's topological structure is constantly changing, and the battery current consists of non-periodic pulse signal sequences, making it challenging for traditional methods to accurately estimate the battery model parameters within such networks. To address this issue, this paper proposes a lithium-ion battery circuit model parameter estimation method that takes into account network topology reconfiguration. This method, based on the operational modes and sampling methods of DRBN, derives a new discrete transformation formula for the transfer function and constructs a least squares model parameter identification model using this formula. By establishing an experimental platform for DRBN, the effectiveness of the proposed method is validated in this paper.

articleTitle: DC-side impedance modelling and analysis of MMC under different control strategies
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the large-scale operation and extensive access of modular multilevel converter (MMC) based high voltage direct current (HVDC) systems, stability issues such as wideband oscillations can be easily caused due to the complex internal harmonic characteristics of MMC. Based on harmonic state space (HSS) method, this paper firstly establishes the DC-side impedance models of MMC under different control strategies, encompassing open-loop control, AC voltage control, DC voltage control, and power control, which consider the multiple harmonic coupling and the influence of different control loops. Then, the established DC-side impedance models are validated by frequency scanning. Furthermore, the DC-side impedance characteristics of MMC with different control strategies are analysed and compared. The results show that factors significantly influencing the AC-side impedance, such as the phase-locked loop (PLL), control delay, outer-loop control, and circulating current suppression, exhibit minimal effect on the DC-side impedance. While, the DC-side impedances within different frequency ranges are mainly affected by the current inner-loop control, DC voltage control, main circuit parameters, and DC transmission cables.

articleTitle: Control strategy of DC breaking resistor in offshore wind farm DC integrating system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The control strategy in current research of chopper controlled DC breaking resistor in offshore wind farm DC integrating systems shows many shortcomings, such as its large voltage fluctuating range, uncontrollable switching frequency, and significant difference in control performance under different operating conditions. To overcome these shortcomings, a control strategy of DC breaking resistor in offshore wind farm DC integrating system is proposed, in which the DC voltage is collected as the only input signal, and the surplus power is calculated based on the voltage change rate and the equivalent charging capacitance of DC system; duty cycle of the power electronic switches are roughly determined by the surplus power, and then further adjusted according to the error between DC voltage and its reference value, so as to stabilize the DC voltage. Simulation results show that this control strategy successfully realizes the function of automatically deblocking when a fault occurs at the receiving AC power grid, maintaining DC voltage stable during the fault, and automatically blocking after the fault is cleared. At the same time, the control strategy performs stable under different operating conditions, with the characteristics of fast adjustment speed, small adjustment oscillation, and low steady-state ripple.

articleTitle: Diagnostic methods for circuit breaker faults
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: At the same time, the mechanical characteristic data and vibration data during the action process of the circuit breaker are collected in the article, and the same time reference point is set through the fracture to establish the vibration data threshold of the components. By determining the position of the operating mechanism during the occurrence of abnormal vibration signals, the cause of the malfunction can be diagnosed. The research results can detect faults before the circuit breaker leaves the factory, avoiding safety hazards that may arise during the use of the circuit breaker.

articleTitle: Accurate single-ended fault location for ultra high voltage long transmission lines
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Faults may occur on transmission lines, which may damage power equipment or even cause large-scale power outages. Accurate fault location technology is very important to ensure reliable operation of the power system. In this article, a single-ended model-based phasor domain fault location method for ultra high voltage transmission lines is proposed. The proposed method only requires local measurement information and does not require communication technology and synchronization technology, which is low-cost and friendly to practical applications. The existing Eriksson method is widely adopted in practice. However, the Eriksson method utilizes lumped parameter impedance model, which will affect the location accuracy. The proposed method is based on the distributed parameter line model. The proposed method is verified by simulation in PSCAD. The results prove that the proposed method has improved fault location accuracy with various fault locations and fault resistances.

articleTitle: Maximum penetration level and optimal placement of photovoltaic power station in distribution network
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the rapid development of photovoltaic power generation, the optimization of photovoltaic power station in distribution network becomes an important issue. This paper uses the static load model, firstly, set voltage and line current carrying capacity as constraint conditions, and set up photovoltaic power station acceptable maximum capacity as objective function, through the interior-point method to solve optimal power flow model; Secondly, set the network loss minimize as the target function, and by using the second-order cone method to calculate the flow model of the branch, this method can effectively solve the optimization problem of photovoltaic power station. The planning personnel can easily use the calculation process proposed to determine the access capacity and access location of the photovoltaic power station in the distribution network. The effectiveness and superiority of the method in the optimal configuration of the distribution network photovoltaic power station are verified by the optimization results in CPLEX environment.

articleTitle: Power prediction-based photovoltaic hybrid MPPT control strategy
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Addressing the challenges associated with the single maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control strategy for photovoltaics, which often struggles to rapidly and accurately track the global maximum power point (GMPP) of the photovoltaic array in complex external environments, leading to significant power oscillations, we propose a photovoltaic compound MPPT control method grounded in power prediction (PF-IAFSA-IP&O). This innovative approach utilizes an enhanced photovoltaic current sorting kinematic projectile model to establish a photovoltaic power prediction model. The model is then solved using an improved adaptive artificial fish swarm algorithm (IAFSA), enabling the photovoltaic array to swiftly operate at the maximum power point. Furthermore, to mitigate prediction model errors, the adaptive perturb and observe (IP&O) algorithm is employed for local search, ensuring more precise optimization. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed MPPT control strategy offers significant improvements compared to traditional methods, effectively reducing power oscillations during the maximum power tracking process.

articleTitle: Coordinated protection of low-voltage DC distribution system based on the front zone braking coefficient
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the continuous integration of renewable energy into the power system, low-voltage DC distribution systems have received increasing attention. Low-voltage DC distribution system has the advantages of high energy conversion efficiency and high-power quality. However, the complex fault characteristics of low-voltage DC distribution systems and the existence of distributed energy sources make it difficult to apply traditional AC protection methods directly. Therefore, this paper proposes a coordinated protection scheme based on the front zone braking coefficient, which realizes fast fault detection and accurate positioning by judging the range of the front zone braking coefficient and combining the fault differential characteristics. The simulation analysis and results show that it can significantly improve the reliability and stability of low-voltage DC distribution systems.

articleTitle: Influence of O2content on discharge characteristics of C4F7N/CO2/O2ternary mixed gas

abstract: The substitution of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>gas in power equipment is a hot topic. articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of energy storage on the line protection of the collecting line in the wind-photovoltaic-storage power station
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In some wind-photovoltaic-storage power station, energy storage are gathered on 35kV AC lines. The control strategy of energy storage converter will affect the fault current external characteristics of the energy storage system, and then affect the action of line protection equipment and fault removal. To solve the above problems, based on the current mainstream energy storage converter control strategy and national standards, the response of the control strategy during the relay protection operation time are analyzed. Then the fault current external characteristics of the energy storage system are obtained. The effect on the collecting line current protection is analyzed. The accuracy of the external current characteristics of the energy storage system obtained in this paper is verified by simulation. Combined with simulation, The accuracy of the analytical results are further proved by simulation, and the improvement measures of the current protection tuning scheme are proposed.

articleTitle: Chaos-adaptive multi-objective PSO algorithm for microgrid optimization scheduling
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: To enhance the economic and environmental benefits of daily microgrid operations and address the optimization accuracy challenges in particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithms, a chaotic adaptive multi-objective particle swarm algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the Logistical chaotic mapping is introduced to generate the initial population, enhancing population diversity. Secondly, based on chaotic theory, the control factor γ adaptively adjusts the chaotic search range, and the algorithm's adaptability is further improved through the adaptive adjustment of the inertia weight parameter ω and acceleration coefficients c1, c2. The proposed algorithm is simulated using six typical test functions, demonstrating superior performance in terms of optimization accuracy, solution stability, and convergence speed compared to heuristic algorithms such as the grey wolf algorithm. Finally, the enhanced PSO algorithm is applied to solve multi-objective optimization and scheduling problems in microgrid integration. Simulation results indicate that the algorithm effectively enhances the overall benefits of daily microgrid operations.

articleTitle: Research on the voltage gradient in DC-link capacitors
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Based on the analysis of theRLCcircuit, the limit VG of the ideal capacitor is equal to the product of the voltage of the capacitor and its natural frequency, namely:(duc/dt)0=U0ω0 . The maximum VG of DC-link capacitor is equal to the product of limit VG and inverse peak ratio when the actual capacitor discharge current is damping. That is: (duc/dt)m=β(duc/dt)0=βU0ω0 . For DC-link capacitors, the inverse peak ratio is close to 1.0, and it can be considered that the maximum VG of DC-link capacitors is its limit VG. The relationship between the maximum VG and the maximum surge current are deduced by analyzing the surge discharge test of DC-link capacitor. The condition that VGV is greater than VGC is that the equivalent inductance of the circuit is not more than 88.2nH, and the conclusion that VGC is greater than VGV is put forward in general. The maximum VG of the surge current discharge test circuit of DC-link capacitor can be calculated as (duc/dt)z≈βzU0ω0 . It is suggested that the reasons for the damage of DC-link capacitors due to VG are proposed VG of the circuit is greater than the limit VG of DC-link capacitor, or the reverse peak ratio of the circuit is too large, or the maximum surge current and over-frequency. It is of great significance to understand the relationship between VG and surge discharge current of DC-link capacitors, and can also provide theoretical reference for the surge discharge test.

articleTitle: Study on the influence of distributed photovoltaic access grid on voltage quality based on virtual synchronous control strategy
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In recent years, with the continuous improvement of the grid-connected scale and installed capacity of distributed photovoltaic, especially for grid-connected local photovoltaic power generation in rural areas, mountainous areas and tidal flats, vicious voltage quality problems such as voltage increase in load station area have become increasingly prominent. This paper proposes photovoltaic grid-connected converters based on virtual synchronous control as the object. By establishing the sequence impedance model of PV grid-connected converters in the maximum power point tracking mode, the generation mechanism of voltage quality problems in the distribution network of PV access station area is deduced. Then, the impedance model of PV grid-connected converter based on virtual synchronous control strategy is established, and the simulation analysis shows that the control strategy can reduce the equivalent impedance of the grid in the station area, enhance the voltage support capability of the PV converter, and improve the voltage fluctuation and rise of the grid, providing a new idea for the distributed PV grid access area power generation and voltage quality problem management.

articleTitle: Converter station configurations for GW-scale MVDC systems using superconducting cables
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: High-temperature superconducting (HTS) cable technology is appearing as a promising candidate for implementing bulk power Medium Voltage Direct Current (MVDC) corridors with reduced footprint and considerably lower losses. HTS demonstrators have achieved currents of 5-10 kA, raising a challenge for substation ratings, limited to 3 kA for Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) and 6 kA for Line Commutated Converter (LCC) topologies. This paper studies topologies for implementing 10 kA/100 kV substations suited for HTS-based GW-scale MVDC links. The study addresses challenges and possible benefits of four high-current MMC-based substation designs in terms of hardware/control requirements, fault handling considerations and substation overall design (Valve Hall size modifications, AC/DC yards requirements). The first configuration presents challenges related to the increased energy per submodule, raising concerns regarding internal converter fault scenarios. The rest of the topologies use a standard submodule voltage and current rating matching those used in existing HVDC MMC designs. A 3D modelling approach is used to estimate valve hall size for each case and a reference 500 kV MMC hall of the same rating, with results showing potential for a 60% volume reduction. This size reduction is especially relevant in offshore applications, where size of platforms is a large cost driver.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of short circuit faults on wind turbine ride-through capability in offshore wind collection system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The MMC-HVDC connection to offshore wind farms constitutes the offshore wind power flexible and direct delivery system, and the main purpose of studying the AC faults at the delivery end is to obtain the fault operation characteristics and design the control strategy that can traverse the faults, while the influence of fault factors on the fault operation characteristics is rarely mentioned in the literature, especially the influence of these related factors on the important offshore grid connection point voltage is rarely studied, which determines whether offshore wind soft and direct feed-out scenarios can directly apply the grid connection criteria of fault voltage ride-through curves for onshore wind turbines. At present, the main problem facing offshore wind transmission is the lack of specific assessment standards, which makes it difficult to assess the WTGs. This paper mainly analyses the impact of the most serious three-phase ground faults on the grid-connected voltage when the most serious three-phase ground faults occur on the pooled system transmission line considering different fault resistances, and carries out a comprehensive fault calibration, and these results can be used to guide the offshore WTG fault ride-through grid connection standards to provide reference<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]</sup>.

articleTitle: Start-up control strategy for offshore wind power transmitted by DRU-MMC series hybrid HVDC system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the large-scale and remote development of offshore wind power, the scheme based on diode rectifier unit (DRU) and modular multilevel converter (MMC) in series has lower volume, weight, cost and better economic benefits than the more widely used schemes of MMC at both ends, so it has been widely concerned. However, the MMC of the sending end of the system cannot be started directly through the MMC of the grid side like the MMC of the both ends because it is connected with the DRU in series. At present, there are many researches on control methods based on DRU and MMC series scheme, but there are few researches on startup methods. Firstly, this paper takes DRU and MMC series scheme as the research object, and conducts in-depth research on its control strategy. The control strategy enables series MMC to not only provide power, voltage and frequency support required for wind farm start-up, but also distribute DC voltage and active power. Then, an economical and reliable system start-up strategy of DRU and MMC in series on the offshore is proposed. Finally, the control strategy is verified in the electromagnetic transient simulation software PSCAD.

articleTitle: An approach for calculating ion flow in HVDC transmission line based on algebraic multi-grid method
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: As the geometric configuration and physical model of HVDC transmission lines become more complex, the solver increasingly becomes a performance bottleneck in research on ion flow field problems. The preconditioner is a key component for the performance of iterative solvers. Although the algebraic multigrid method is proven to be an optimal preconditioner for elliptic equations, it results in significant stability issues when applied to convection-dominated transport equations. In this work, the algebraic multigrid method employing an approximate ideal restriction operator is applied to solve the transport equation arising in ion flow field problems. Compared to the classical algebraic multigrid method, the Petrov-Galerkin algebraic multigrid method demonstrates good performance in solving the transport equation for ion flow field simulations. This improvement helps address the large-scale electromagnetic environment issues of HVDC transmission lines.

articleTitle: Modeling and analysis of key impact mechanisms of voltage quality considering large-scale wind power grid-connected scenarios
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: As the scale and proportion of new energy connected to the grid continue to increase, the grid voltage quality problem is more and more prominent, gradually threatening the safe and stable operation of the grid. This paper analyzes the impact mechanism of voltage quality problems such as voltage overruns at grid-connected points through Norton equivalent modeling of large-scale wind farms, and analyzes the impact mechanism of voltage quality problems such as voltage overruns at grid-connected points by deducing the mathematical relationship between the voltage at grid-connected points of wind farms, the equivalent impedance of the AC grid, and the voltage at the neighboring nodes. Finally, through the full electromagnetic transient software PSCAD/EMTDC on the IEEE 39-node simulation example of wind turbine operation characteristics and the characteristics of the impact on the voltage quality of the grid and neighboring nodes were simulated and analyzed to verify, and give measures to improve the voltage quality of the feeder AC grid, and combined with the 220 kV Qianjin substation in Wenzhou area of Zhejiang Province, wind power centralized feeder AC power grid exists in the voltage quality problems, including a reasonable voltage quality management strategy, such as reasonable selection of wind turbine installed capacity, access location and access mode, load control and installation of reactive power compensation equipment.

articleTitle: Research on control strategy of hybrid HVDC circuit breaker assisting MMC start-up
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In order to realize the online passive startup of modular multilevel converter (MMC) for the renewable energy access of multi-terminal flexible DC network. Firstly, the passive start-up mechanism of MMC is analyzed based on the operational principle of HVDC circuit breakers; Then, combining the flexible control and high resistance characteristics of the power electronic module unit of the hybrid HVDC circuit breaker transfer branch, a staged conduction control strategy of the power electronic module unit of the transfer branch is proposed to realize the passive start-up of MMC. Finally, the proposed hybrid high-voltage direct current circuit breaker (Hybrid DCCB) control strategy is verified by PSCAD/EMTDC modeling and simulation.

articleTitle: A novel nonisolated high gain DC-DC converter for microgrids applications
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: A novel non-isolated high step-up dc-dc converter specifically designed for microgrids was introduced in this paper. The converter provides a wide range of high voltage gains, having two different duty cycles, reduced voltage stress, and the use of a modular structure. The paper provides a brief description of the topology of the proposed converter. It then proceeds to analyze in detail the operating principle and the voltage stress experienced by the device. Finally, the waveform obtained by Psim software proves the theoretical analysis. So the topology can be used as a boost converter for microgrids.

articleTitle: Analysis and model of high frequency harmonic impedance of grid connected DFIG wind turbines
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With more and more doubly fed inductor generators (DFIG) connected to the grid, high frequency resonance may occur due to the interaction between DFIG wind turbines and the grid, resulting in serious safety problems. Impedance analysis is one of the methods analysing high frequency oscillations in MMC-HVDC systems. However, the existing models are incomplete due to the lack of simulation validation of each section of the impedance model, this paper establishes an impedance model of a DFIG wind turbine for high frequency analysis, which considers rotor side converter (RSC), grid side converter (GSC), filter capacitor and transformer. In addition, this paper investigates the characteristics of a grid connected DFIG wind turbine under high frequency by electromagnetic transient simulation and calculation. The correctness of the developed model is evaluated by electromagnetic transient simulation.

articleTitle: Research on diode converter valve for HVDC transmission system of offshore wind power
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In the present, the offshore wind power transmission system through modular multilevel converter (MMC) has problems such as large size and weight of converter valve, large area and high cost of offshore platform construction. The diode rectifier unit (DRU) has become one of the research hotspots of offshore wind power delivery technology, due to it has advantages of small conduction loss, low cost, small size and weight, and high reliability. In this paper, a DRU-MMC DC transmission system topology scheme for offshore wind power grid connection is proposed. The electrical and structural design of the diode converter valve is carried out, and the selection basis of key components is proposed. Based on the research results, the prototype of diode converter valve was developed. In order to verify the performance of the prototype, a test circuit system was set up, and the operation and insulation tests of the diode converter valve were carried out, and the test results proved that the design and development of the diode converter valve met the requirements. The results of this paper can provide a reference for the systematic study of offshore wind power DC transmission project and the design of key equipment for offshore converter platform in the future.

articleTitle: Carrying capacity of distribution networks for distributed photovoltaics considering wideband oscillation
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The utilization of power electronic devices is on the rise in the distribution network, resulting in considerable alterations to its dynamic characteristics. One such alteration is the occurrence of wideband oscillation due to power electronic devices, which has emerged as a significant obstacle impeding the integration of renewable energy. Consequently, when calculating the carrying capacity of the distribution network for distributed photovoltaics, it is vital to consider the impact of wideband oscillations. This paper presents a frequency impedance model of the distribution network that includes distributed photovoltaic units to address this issue. The model calculates the distribution network's operational boundaries, considering wideband oscillations, to ensure safe and stable operation. Additionally, a method for determining the range of the distribution network's capacity to accommodate distributed photovoltaic units is obtained. Finally, a PSCAD-based electromagnetic transient model of the distribution network was developed to verify the accuracy of the theoretical analysis results.

articleTitle: Multiphysics-constrained safe charging boundary of lithium-ion battery with model predictive control
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The lithium-ion battery (LIB) is susceptible to overheating and rapid degradation during fast charging. Therefore, it is crucial to actively manage the key intermediate physical states of the LIB within acceptable parameters while maintaining fast charging speeds. Motivated by this concern, our paper proposes a multiple physics-constrained fast charging strategy for LIBs. We establish a comprehensive electro-thermal-aging model under typical charging scenarios. Building upon this foundation, we design a model-based observer to accurately estimate the state of charge and internal temperature of the LIB in real-time. To address the conflicting objectives of charging speed, temperature control, and degradation rate, we propose a model predictive control-based strategy to optimize the charging process. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed strategy effectively keeps the internal battery temperature below the predetermined threshold while maintaining a comparable charging speed. Furthermore, our strategy leads to slower degradation compared to the widely-used constant-current-constant-voltage charging approach. After 200 charge-discharge cycles, the capacity decay rates are 2.12% and 4.88% for our proposed strategy and the traditional method, respectively. Through model predictive control, our fast-charging strategy effectively manages battery internal states, resulting in significant improvements in speed, safety, and battery lifespan extension.

articleTitle: Parative research on the lightning protection of ± 800kV UHVDC transmission lines
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper carried out the parative research on the lightning protection of UHVDC transmission lines based on the ± 800kV UHVDC project from Qinghai to Henan in China. According to the existed operating experience, the flashover rate reference value for this project was proposed. Two methods were used in this paper to calculate the whole flashover rate of this transmission line. One method was based on the statistical value of the thunderstorm days, and the other method was based on the statistical value of ground flash density. The results obtained by the two methods mentioned above has been used as reference for the engineering design.

articleTitle: Transient control and prototype verification of high capacity IGCT-DCT with quasi-zero switching loss
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In this paper, DC transformer based on IGCT and lossless buffer capacitor (IGCT-DCT) and transient control for IGCT-DCT; are proposed. In IGCT-DCT, the loss of zero voltage switching (ZVS)under light load or no load is solved through soft converter modulation (SCM) based on minimum backflow power injection, and the buffer capacitor can greatly reduce the turned-off loss of IGCT. As a result, the switching loss of IGCT is approximately zero and IGCT-DCT can achieve greater capacity. However, when the power step is performed under SCM, a large bias current will be generated, which will affect the ZVS of IGCT, result in the direct discharge of lossless buffer capacitors through IGCT. Therefore, the transient control for SCM also needs to satisfy the ZVS condition. In order to solve the above problems, by analyzing the current characteristics of SCM, this paper proposes a transient control based on prediction, which can realize power step and power reversal without bias current and does not affect the ZVS of IGCT. Finally, a 1.5kV 3MW prototype is used to verify the effectiveness of the proposed theory.

articleTitle: Analysis of key influencing factors of transient voltage stability based on generalized polynomial Chaos
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: To analyze the transient voltage stability of grid-connected power systems containing a high proportion of new energy sources, this paper proposes a method for identifying key influencing factors of power system transient voltage stability based on generalized Polynomial Chaos. This method considers the dynamic characteristics of new energy output, establishes the correlation between system transient voltage stability and influencing factors, and quantifies the impact of each factor on system transient voltage stability. It is difficult to establish an analytical model for complex nonlinear power systems, so the generalized Polynomial Chaos expansion is first used to establish the correlation between the transient voltage response of the system load point and the influencing factors. Secondly, the Sobol index is introduced into the correlation relationship to define the global sensitivity of the transient voltage and quantify the degree to which each factor affects the system's transient voltage stability. Compared with the traditional method, it is more efficient and more accurate. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of this method are verified in the CSEE-VS example system, and the key influencing factors of transient voltage stability of the grid-connected power system containing a high proportion of new energy are analyzed. Compared with the Monte Carlo method, this method can accurately and quickly calculate key influencing factors with a small number of samples.

articleTitle: Small signal stability analysis of PV-BESs based on discrete state space
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: New energy is gradually replacing fossil energy and becoming the main source of electricity. It is of great significance to analyze the small signal stability of new energy stations, while the traditional eigenvalue analysis method has limitations such as difficulty in selecting independent state variables. In this paper, the discrete state space method is applied to photovoltaic-battery energy storage system (PV-BESs) for the small signal stability analysis. The discrete state space model based on the trapezoidal integration rule is first constructed, accompanied by its eigenvalues. Then, the discrete eigenvalues are transformed into those real eigenvalues of the system. Correspondingly, the small signal stability of the system is analyzed. The eigenvalues and participation factors calculated by the two methods are compared to verify the correctness of the discrete state space model.

articleTitle: High-frequency oscillation analysis of wind farm-side MMC station under no-load charging condition
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Existing research on high-frequency oscillation indicates that the high-frequency oscillation during no-load charging of modular multilevel converter (MMC) station is primarily linked to time delay and the ground capacitance of AC lines. Nevertheless, a high-frequency oscillation around 2000 Hz has been observed in Rudong high voltage direct current project even when the AC lines are not connected. Except time delay, there still exists another key factor of the high-frequency oscillation, i.e., the transformer stray capacitance. This paper delves into the interaction among the dynamics of MMC station and the transformer. And the mechanism of high-frequency oscillation under no-load charging condition is determined. Firstly, the harmonic state space (HSS) model of MMC station considering the effect of stray capacitance is established. By plotting the eigenvalue trajectory, the essentiality of taking into account stray capacitance is elucidated. Subsequently, a simplified model is obtained by neglecting the dynamics of elements with low participation in the oscillation modes. Next, the mechanism of high-frequency oscillation is clarified according to impedance characteristics. Finally, the impact of proportional gain and shear frequency on small signal stability is revealed. The correctness and accuracy are identified by electromagnetic transient simulations.

articleTitle: Sequential linear programming-based parameter optimization of dynamic reactive power compensation devices for security enhancement and new energy power transmission increasing
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: To enhance security and increase inter-area power transmission capacity of sending-end power systems of large-scale new energy, a systemic approach is proposed of parameter optimization of dynamic reactive power compensation devices of Synchronous Condenser (SC) and Static Var Generator (SVG) in new energy power stations. The critical contingencies that restricting transmission capacity is screened out for the purpose of variable number reduction. Meanwhile, controlled and control variables are reduced through checking of fulfilment of stability and fault ride through requirements and evaluation of trajectory sensitivities. A quadratic optimization model is established, whose objective function is minimization of the difference between the voltage response and expectation curve under critical contingencies. The established quadratic model is linearized by Taylor’s series expansion and solved sequentially accompany with multiple calling of the transient simulation. The proposed approach is tested in a real power system with large scale new energy power and Ultra-High Voltage DC (UHVDC) and Ultra-High Voltage AC (UHVAC) lines for inter-area transmission. The optimized parameters of SVG and SC are applied and the results prove that they can make voltage fulfil the requirements under critical contingencies, enhance the security and increase the inter-area transmission capacity.

articleTitle: System strength analysis of multi-converter systems from the perspective of disturbance rejection performance
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the access of massive power electronic converters, multi-converter system has become a typical form of modern power system. The safe and stable operation ability of such a multi-converter system is closely related to the voltage response performances under the disturbances. The concept of system voltage support strength (referred to as ‘system strength’) is commonly used in the industry to describe the voltage response performance of the multi-converter system composed of power grid and the converters. Some metrics, such as short-circuit ratio (SCR) are proposed to characterize the system strength of the above system. Most of the existing metrics focus on the system strength from the perspective of stability analysis. However, few studies start from the definition of system strength to elaborate system strength from the perspective of disturbance rejection performance. To this end, this paper focuses on the nominal multi-converter system, and construct the closed-loop transfer function model of the system under the disturbances. Then, this paper reveals the system strength assessment principle of the system based on the modal decoupling theory from the perspective of disturbance rejection performance. On this basis, this paper proposes the system strength assessment method based on the generalized short-circuit ratio (gSCR) metric and device critical short-circuit ratio metric. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified by simulations based on MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: The effect of electrostatic probe on flat insulator surface charge distribution during online measurement
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The accumulation of surface charge on the DC GIL insulator will reduce the flashover voltage along the surface of insulator. The online measurement for the dynamic accumulation process of surface charge can better reveal the mechanism of surface charge accumulation. Therefore, the study of surface charge online measurement is of great significance. In this paper, a needle-plate charging experimental model with an electrostatic probe for online measurement is constructed. The surface charge online measurements on a flat insulator made of epoxy/Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>are also performed. Meanwhile, the electric field distribution during online measurement is calculated. The results show that: compared with the case without probe, the maximum of the positive charge density accumulated on the surface of flat insulator increased by more than 50% when the probe was measured online. The positive charge region expands towards the probe position, a mass of positive charge accumulated near the sharp corner of the probe. In addition, the electrostatic probe obviously distorts the space electric field distribution, which further changes the original surface charge density distribution. This work can serve as a reference for online measurement of surface charge.

articleTitle: Optimized balance factor assisted neutral-point voltage balance for three-level T-type inverter
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The three-level T-type inverter features multiple-level outputs and low harmonic content, making it suitable for applications with high power and performance requirements. However, due to the inherent defect in the topology of the three-level T-type inverter, this type of inverter is prone to the issue of neutral-point voltage imbalance. Traditional modulation strategies aimed at addressing this issue are often limited in their practical application to resistive loads, leading to the limitations in these strategies. A neutral-point voltage control method based on optimized balance factor is proposed by analyzing the role of basic vectors. This method utilizes the phase current corresponding to the small vector as a correction factor, separating the influence of small vector current on the potential. By combining the correction factor with the balancing factor, the feedback signal is employed in the specific working conditions of the small vector, thereby simplifying the control complexity. According to the results of simulation experiments, the method proposed can restrict the deviation of the neutral-point voltage to within 0.5V less than 6ms, and it is also applicable to resistive and inductive load conditions, demonstrating its correctness and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research on lightning warning technology of transmission line based on multi-source heterogeneous data
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Lightning is one of the most serious natural disasters, and it is the main cause of overhead transmission line flashover in the power system. For lightning protection of overhead transmission lines, previous research has mainly focused on strengthening line insulation design and installing lightning protection facilities, with less research on lightning warning for transmission lines. Establishing an effective lightning strike prediction and warning method for overhead transmission lines is of great significance in reducing lightning flashover and power outage losses. At present, the lightning prediction and early warning methods used domestically and internationally generally use three types of equipment: radar, lightning positioning system, and atmospheric electric field detection. By studying the changing characteristics of various monitoring data under thunderstorm weather, ideal prediction models and factors were found, and meteorological lightning prediction methods were established. However, these studies only conducted thunderstorm meteorological warning, and there was relatively little research on lightning warning for overhead transmission lines, which cannot be directly used for lightning protection of overhead transmission lines in the power system. This article not only utilized three commonly used data, namely radar, lightning positioning system, and atmospheric electric field detection, but also introduced numerical weather forecast data. Combined with research results on lightning performance of transmission lines, a calculation method that can predict the lightning strike probability and flashover probability of transmission lines in real time was proposed, and a lightning warning model was established.

articleTitle: Online and offline power reversal methods for bipolar LCC-HVDC systems
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy sources (RESs) has increased the utilization of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) technology for power transfer purposes. However, there are emerging requirements for HVDCs to provide grid flexibility due to the inherent variability of RESs. Line-commutated converter-based HVDC (LCC-HVDC) systems hold the highest installed capacity among all HVDC technologies and are well-suited to offer the much-needed grid flexibility by providing fast and accurate power flow controls. This paper focuses on one of the key aspects in providing such flexibility - power reversal function of bipolar LCC-HVDCs. This paper categorizes the power reversal methods for bipolar LCC-HVDCs into offline and online types and conducts a comparative analysis of these methods from the perspectives of regulating capacity and reversal duration. Both types of power reversal methods are validated using PSCAD/EMTDC. The simulation results show that the online method can provide continuous active power control without a dead-band, which enables greater controllability in terms of regulating capacity and reversal duration compared to the offline method.

articleTitle: Pollution distribution characteristics of suspension insulators for transmission lines under different environments
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The study of insulator contamination characteristics is of great significance to the electrical design, operation and maintenance of transmission lines. In order to obtained natural contamination characteristics of insulators, this paper carried out the agricultural, industrial, coastal and desert environments in natural pollution characteristic test of insulators, analyzed the characteristics of pollution distribution, surface pollution severity and pollution depositing rate, the influence of the different operating conditions normal insulator, porcelain anti-pollution insulator, porcelain binary-umbrella insulator, porcelain triple- umbrella insulator and composite insulators. The distribution of pollution accumulation shows regional differences. Agricultural insulator surface pollution severity is the smallest, industrial insulator surface pollution degree is the largest. The saturated pollution coefficient of insulators in agricultural, industrial, coastal and desert environments is 1.4, 2.4, 2.1 and 1.7. Finally, this paper proposes the shape pollution coefficients of typical insulators in different environment. The conclusions have important guiding significance for the configuration and selection of pollution external insulation.

articleTitle: Research on system DC side arresters configuration scheme in flexible DC distribution network
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Flexible DC distribution network has become an important part of future distribution network because of its many advantages. DC circuit breakers are important equipment in constructing flexible DC distribution network, whereas, the overvoltage generated during the operation of DC circuit breaker endangers the insulation safety of the system. Based on a ±10kV three-terminal flexible DC distribution network model and a mechanical DC circuit breaker model in the PSCAD/EMTDC platform, this paper conducted simulation analysis of operating overvoltage of mechanical DC circuit breakers opening DC side fault, compared the maximum overvoltage and equipment insulation level of the system under two system DC side arrester configuration schemes, and analysed the effect of arrester residual voltage on the system overvoltage. The research in present work provides a reference for the insulation coordination of flexible DC distribution networks.

articleTitle: Carbon emission prediction and carbon emission reduction potential analysis of cement enterprises based on electricity data
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This study focuses on the carbon emission forecast and carbon reduction potential analysis of cement enterprises based on electricity data. The cement industry is an important carbon emission industry that will soon be included in China's national carbon trading market.
