The State Grid provides digital carbon management services for electricity-using enterprises, and has jointly innovated with Tsinghua University a model for carbon emission forecasting and analysis in the cement industry and carbon emission reduction potential assessment for cement enterprises based on electricity data, which solves the problems of high economic cost, technical difficulty and long term cycle faced by electricity-using enterprises in carbon emission accounting and carbon emission reduction. Discovered the electricity-carbon correlation relationship of cement enterprises, proposed a carbon emission reduction potential assessment model for cement enterprises, assessed the emission reduction potential of 42 cement industry technologies, and put forward the three technologies with the highest emission reduction potential, as well as the three technologies with the highest cost-effectiveness of carbon emission reduction. Carbon market users are provided with carbon emission reduction decision-making services to realize accurate and efficient services and help China realize the "3060" strategic goal of low-carbon green transformation.

articleTitle: Simulation and test on lightning protection of large photovoltaic power station by gas arc-extinguishing device
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Large photovoltaic power station are built in wide deserts, mountains and fields, and lighting accidents occur frequently. This paper proposes a gas arc-extinguishing device to lightning protection and ensure that photovoltaic power stations can continue to generate electricity safely. The gas arc-extinguishing device principle is analyzed, and then the arc extinguishing process is simulated by COMSOL Multiphysics simulation software. Finally, the power-frequency continuous current interruption test is performed. The simulation and test results show that the device can effectively arc extinguishing on the insulator of the transmission line of large photovoltaic power station.

articleTitle: Multi-parameter detection of discharge defects in the gap multi-metal conduit in transformer bushing
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In power transformer, oil-paper insulation bushing is a common outlet assembly, which has many failures and causes great losses. Due to its randomness, the gap discharge of multi-metal conduit is difficult to be detected by the monitoring device during operation, resulting in the failure of the insulation oil inside the casing, and the casing can not continue to run in serious cases. In this paper, the discharge process of multi-metal tube inside casing is simulated, and the changes of local discharge, temperature in oil and dissolved gas in oil are studied. The research conclusion shows that:with the increase of withstand voltage time, the discharge phase width increases, the discharge peak develops from double-peak in half period to double-peak in full period, the discharge frequency increases, but the discharge energy shows a trend of decreasing first and then increasing. During the development of discharge defects, the hydrogen content increases significantly, although the discharge energy is small and the heating rate is low, it still leads to a slight increase in the oil temperature.

articleTitle: Method for detecting LCC-HVDC phase shifiting failures bsaed on S-transform energy entropy
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In response to the frequent occurrence of phase shifting failures on the weak receiving -end LCC-HVDC system's inverter side, this paper proposes a method for detecting phase shifting f ailures based on S-transform energy entropy. Firstly, the local variations of the inverter side's DC current during phase shifting failures are analyzed. Then, the S-transform is applied to the DC current of the inverter side and combined with information entropy theory to obtain the S-transform energy entropy. The energy entropy undergoes a sudden change when phase shifting failures occur in the LCC-HVDC system. By setting a threshold value and considering the rate of change of the DC current, phase shifting failures can be detected. Finally, extensive simulations using PSCAD/EMTDC software validate the rationality of the threshold value selection and the correctness of the phase shifting failure detection method under various fault conditions, thereby ensuring the safe and stable operation of high-voltage DC transmission systems.

articleTitle: Field observation of conductor icing at Nanyue Mountain
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The ice thickness plays a key role for design and maintenance of overhead transmission lines. The direction and diameter of the conductors have an impact on the ice thickness. The design specifications propose different types of conductor diameter correction formulas. In order to further accumulate basic icing data, in this paper, we introduces the conductor icing field observation conducted in the winter of 2020–2021 in Nanyue Mountain, Hunan province, China, as well as the related results. The analyzing results show that in the case of fog and mixed glaze, the smaller the diameter of the conductor, the larger ice thickness, and the ice thickness of conductors in most east-west directions is greater than that in the north-south direction.

articleTitle: Design of user secondary development system based on visual programming
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In order to meet the diverse needs of smart substation users for relay protection devices, and to realize the personalized customization function of protection logic by engineering users, a user secondary development system with a visual logic interface is designed. In the system, the user performs the secondary modification of the logic diagram on the visual logic design interface on the tool side to generate a user logic code file containing a variable length instruction set that can be interpreted and executed, and the file is downloaded to the embedded relay protection device. It is parsed and executed by the device to realize that the secondary development logic of the engineering user takes effect inside the device. The test results prove the reliability and real-time performance of the system, and provide a technical path that can be used for reference for the hierarchical development of relay protection devices.

articleTitle: Research on the active shutdown caused by negative voltage in MMC-HCC power cycle system test
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This article analyzes the abnormal situation of IGCT device active shutdown caused by negative voltage in the MMC-HCC power cycle system test. Firstly, the background of the power cycle system test is introduced, and the problem of negative voltage detection triggering active shutdown is described. Secondly, feature extraction of abnormal working conditions is carried out on the recording waveforms, and the feature information of the three abnormal working conditions is analyzed. Finally, an analysis is conducted from the perspectives of stray inductance, stray capacitance, saturation reactor, electromagnetic interference, and converter control strategy, etc. The final conclusion is that the abnormal active shutdown is caused by a combination of factors such as stray inductance, stray capacitance, and electromagnetic interference.

articleTitle: Diagnosis and risk evaluation of hidden fault at voltage and current acquisition section of relay protection equipment based on primary and secondary information fusion
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The hidden fault of voltage and current acquisition is the important cause for the incorrect action of the relay protection equipment. Technology research and engineering application on how to effectively extract the characteristic parameter and accurately identify the hidden faults of the relay protection equipment is in the initial stage. According to the actual wiring, loop and configuration of the relay protection equipment, the article constructs a state quantity transmission logic matrix, builds a multi-source information state quantity set based on online data, identifies hidden faults by comparison of homologous data, build fault trees to evaluate the risk of incorrect actions for hidden faults. Practical cases verify the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Preparation and performance analysis of vegetable insulating oil doped with surface modified nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Compared with mineral insulating oil, vegetable insulating oil, as a kind of green cleaning material, has the disadvantage of insufficient insulating properties, which can be improved by nano-doping modification. In this paper, vegetable insulating oil models of nano SiO2 (NSD) doping system and silicane coupling agent 3-Aminopropyltriethoxysilane (KH550) modified nano SiO2 (NSDS) doping system with different mass fractions and surface grafting rates were established by Materials Studio simulation software to explore the optimal modification conditions of nano-modified vegetable insulating oil and analyze the microscopic modification mechanism. The modified conditions for achieving the optimal breakdown voltage were determined as follows: the doping mass fraction was 3.50%, and the surface grafting rate was 20%. The ratio of reactants is 10:4 and the reaction temperature is 725 K under simulated conditions.

articleTitle: Scaling principle analysis and layout optimization design of grading electrode for inner cooling system of MMC valves
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper analyzes the relationship between the scaling principle of the grading electrode for inner cooling system and the potential, leakage current, and electric field. The research results show that the electric field intensity of the grading electrode is generally large. On the main water pipe, the scaling site is generally at the position with high potential, and the higher the potential, the thicker the scaling layer. That is scaling is related to the electrode potential and the direction of leakage current. Based on the analysis results, the electrical wiring method and the layout mode of grading electrode is proposed to reduce the scaling of the grading electrode and facilitate maintenance.

articleTitle: Fast calculation of conductor impedance in utility tunnels with the virtual medium method
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: As a part of urban infrastructure, underground utility tunnels encompass various pipelines for water, natural gas, electricity, and telecommunications, and also serve as pathways for urban transportation and other service facilities. However, there is a lack of systematic research on the electromagnetic environment in underground utility tunnels, which may lead to neglect of potential issues. In this study, a model based on the virtual medium method is proposed and improved by introducing Galerkin averaging and calculations involving high-order tensors composed of two sets of integral points, significantly reducing the solution domain. The effectiveness of the algorithm is validated through comparisons with analytical solutions and results from the literature, and it is applied to utility tunnel computations. The results demonstrate the high precision of the approach, and the optimization of the data structure significantly reduces computational time. This approach shows practical potential and feasibility for research on electromagnetic environments in underground utility tunnels.

articleTitle: Optimization study of the 100-us-level mechanical switch for natural commutation DC circuit breaker
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: DC circuit breaker (DCCB) is the best choice for DC grid fault clearing and isolation. The naturally commutated hybrid DC circuit breaker (NHCB) has the characteristics of low cost, low loss, and fast breaking speed, which has wide promotion significance. However, currently the breaking time of NHCB is at the ms-level. Therefore, this paper focuses on the research of fast mechanical switches. Firstly, we analyse the working principle of the fast mechanical switch, study the mechanical characteristics of the electromagnetic repulsion mechanism, and analyse the influence of electrical parameters on the motion characteristics by simulation. Then we optimize the parameters of the switching mechanism based on the genetic algorithm-particle swarm optimization algorithm (GA-PSO). Finally, according to the optimized parameters, we developed a naturally commutated DC circuit breaker with hundred-us-level switching capability. We conducted tests on its mechanical and commutation characteristics, achieving the initial contact separation time of 162 us. Both the initial contact separation and commutation processes can be completed within 320 us.

articleTitle: Active frequency support strategy of diode rectifier unit based HVDC transmission system for offshore wind power
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Through collaboration between the onshore modular multilevel converter (MMC) and the offshore wind farm (OWF), the diode rectifier unit (DRU) based high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system for offshore wind power can contribute to the inertia and frequency support of the onshore grid. Firstly, the DC capacitor dynamic self-synchronization control strategy is implemented in the onshore MMC to provide inertia support for the onshore AC grid. The mechanism of the OWFs participating in providing inertia support is then analysed. Subsequently, the onshore MMC adjusts the DC voltage to transmit the onshore frequency information to the OWFs, enabling wind turbines (WTs) to participate in onshore frequency regulation. A model is built in PSCAD/EMTDC, and the results demonstrate that the proposed frequency support strategy allows the system to actively participate in onshore frequency adjustment.

articleTitle: A centralised fault diagnosis method for DC microgrids based on LPV-ROUIOs
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Facing the complexity of fault influences in highly integrated DC microgrids, model-based centralised fault diagnosis methods often offer greater advantages. This paper designs a set of reduced order unknown input observers based on the linear parameter varying model of DC microgrids, and proposes a centralised fault diagnosis method. This method utilises multi-point measurement signals within the system, divides the system into two subsystems through coordinate transformation, and decouples the unknown input disturbances to eliminate the impact on fault diagnosis results. By designing sensitivity matrices for observers, each observer exhibits good selectivity towards different faults, and fault identification is achieved ultimately using fault characteristic codes. Simulation results demonstrate that this method can reliably identify five types of faults in about 1.5 ms, reducing the computational complexity while meeting the rapid protection requirements for DC microgrids, and exhibiting strong robustness and applicability.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of single-phase solid-state transformer for high-speed railway propulsion
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: For the supply of electric power to the High-speed Railway vehicle, the 25kV/60Hz AC source is connected to the power conversion system in the vehicle through a pantograph. The power conversion system in the high-speed railway vehicle consists of a bulky low-frequency transformer, which is used to step down the high AC voltage, and a DC/DC converter. Finally, the converted DC voltage is supplied to the inverter for motor traction. Thanks to the advance of power semiconductors and magnetic components, the power converter efficiency of the converter can be increased with reduced size. Therefore, a new concept of the transformer, called a Solid-State Transformer (SST), has been studied in recent years, substituting the bulky low-frequency transformer and DC/DC converter. In this paper, a 4.2MW SST is established, and the control method is proposed. The soft-start method of SST to diminish the inrush currents is also presented. The control and soft-start method is validated in the test setup with the reduced scale of SST. In addition, the thermally stable operation of the established module is also verified.

articleTitle: Research on the selection of BVR line current density for HVDC AC capacitor bank
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Based on the practical application of BVR wire, which used in HVDC capacitor bank between capacitor units is divided into two parts: the bus part and the non-bus part. Firstly, the equivalent current and equivalent loss of the BVR line are derived and calculated. The conclusion that the current density of the BVR line can be appropriately increased is obtained. The relationship between the equivalent current and equivalent loss and the parallel number n of capacitor units is deduced. The more the number of capacitor units in direct parallel, the smaller the equivalent current and equivalent loss are. Secondly, the operating temperature rise of the conductor surface of the non-bus part of the BVR wire is analyzed by thermodynamic model, and the conclusion is that the conductor surface temperature rise with insulating layer is lower. Thirdly, the energy of electromagnetic wave is transmitted by medium rather than by wire, the change law of electromagnetic wave transmission power in medium is analyzed. The deduced calculation shows that the change of transmission power of electromagnetic wave energy in the medium around the bus conductor comes from the change of transmission speed of electromagnetic wave, and the transmission speed and wave impedance of electromagnetic wave in the medium are inversely proportional to the square of their relative dielectric constant. The phenomenon of low conductor temperature rise of BVR conductor with insulation layer is explained from the perspective of electromagnetic wave transmission, which is the same as the calculation result of thermodynamic model.

articleTitle: Research on the suppression method of STATCOM commutation recognition for HVDC transmission systems with weak receiving end based on singular entropy
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper proposes a method using STATCOM to suppress the weak receiving-end high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system. Firstly, the inverter-side DC current is taken as the characteristic quantity, and the S- transform singular entropy is calculated to propose a phase shifting failure detection method based on S-transform singular entropy. Then, the working principle of STATCOM is analyzed, and it is connected to the inverter side of the HVDC transmission system to suppress phase shifting failures. Finally, a simulation model of the DC transmission system and STATCOM is built on the PSCAD platform. The suppression effect is judged by the change in turn-off angle and the magnitude of the inverter-side bus current. The simulation results indicate that the proposed method can accurately detect phase shifting failures. Additionally, when the inverter side of the weak receiving-end HVDC system experiences an AC system fault, the introduction of STATCOM can suppress phase shifting failures.

articleTitle: Multi-port hybrid DC circuit breaker using controllable voltage source for commutation and cost reduction
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Multi-port hybrid DC circuit breaker (MPHCB) is considered to be the most suitable device to protect the DC grid and can solve the problem of high cost of DC circuit breaker (DCCB) and promote its large-scale use in dc grid. At present, many MPHCB topologies include load commutation switches (LCS), which have the problem of large losses. This paper first proposes an MPHCB using negative voltage source (NVS). By analyzing the short-circuit current and the commutation auxiliary device needs to provide commutation current, the pre-charged capacitor is designed with detailed parameters, which provides a theoretical basis for parameter selection. Secondly, the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed MPHCB under different fault scenarios are verified through simulation. Finally, the economics and functionality of the proposed MPHCB are compared with existing solutions to highlight the advantages of the proposed solution.

articleTitle: Frequency control strategy of standalone microgrids with high penetration of renewable generation
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The frequency stability of standalone microgrids with high penetration of renewable generation is not satisfied, due to intermittent power and poor inertia. To this end, we propose a coordinated frequency control strategy by considering the electromechanical dynamics of wind turbine and synchronous generator. The rotor kinetic energy of wind turbine generator is larger than diesel generator, and the electromagnetic power adjustment rate is faster. Therefore, the wind turbine generator is used to regulate the frequency instead of the synchronous generator. And then, the synchronous generator is used to adjust the wind turbine rotor speed deviation. Through the conversion of roles and functions between the two generators, the coordinated control between generators is realized. Simulation and experiment results prove the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: Analysis of the impact of energy storage power stations access on the multiple renewable energy stations short-circuit ratio
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of new energy power generation access in the power system, making new energy access to weak AC power grid scenarios in local areas, bringing new problems to the stable operation of the power grid. Multiple renewable energy stations short-circuit ratio,(MRSCR) is an important index to measure the support strength of the power system, and the configuration of energy storage can not only enhance the flexibility and security and stability of the power system operation, but also has a great significance to enhance the MRSCR. Firstly, the basic structure of energy storage and the establishment of electromechanical transient simulation model are introduced; secondly, based on the expression of MRSCR, the impact analysis of energy storage access on MRSCR is qualitatively analyzed; finally, based on the actual grid data, the impact analysis of energy storage access on MRSCR is verified from the three dimensions of energy storage with different capacity configurations, different access locations, and different power output states.

articleTitle: Research on the breaking low direct current technology of ±800kV HSS
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: High speed switch (HSS) is the key equipment for online switching of the third station and fault isolation in hybrid multi-terminal HVDC transmission systems, requiring the ability to break low DC currents (1000 V/35 A). In this paper, the composition of HSS in the ±800 kV multi-terminal DC system and the working principle of low DC current breaking of HSS are introduced, and the key factors affecting the performance of HSS current breaking are analysed. Based on MATLAB/SIMULINK software, combined with the circuit structure of ±800 kV multi-terminal HVDC system and the actual parameters of the Kunliulong ultra-high voltage hybrid multi-terminal DC transmission project, the equivalent models of converter stations, DC transmission lines, and HSS are established. Through simulation calculations, the effects of breaking current, power supply voltage, arc voltage, and length of DC transmission line on the low current breaking performance of HSS are studied. The validity of the simulation model is verified by comparing the simulation data with prototype test results. The research results of this paper provide a basis for the development and operation of high speed mechanical switch HSS in multi-terminal DC transmission projects.

articleTitle: Decomposition production calculations in oil impurity under partial discharge faults in GIS/GIL by molecular dynamics
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>is widely used in GIS/GIL as an excellent insulating and arc extinguishing medium. However, SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>gas contains trace amounts of mineral oil impurities. In the case of partial discharge induced by defects such as metal particles, mineral oil impurities participate in reactions to generate decomposition products, which can lead to insulation degradation. This paper employs molecular dynamics simulation methods to investigate the influence of localized strong electric fields on the generation of products from mineral oil impurities. The simulation results indicate that with electric field intensity increases, the decomposition products of mineral oil impurities gradually increase, particularly H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>and CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>. This result is consistent with the gas production characteristics of mineral oil under partial discharge faults in practical, which verifies the accuracy of the molecular dynamics simulations. In addition, the quantities of H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>and CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>indicate that these components are likely to be involved in the decompositions of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>gas in GIS/GIL.

articleTitle: Modelling of electric vehicle charging load based on trip chains
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: To address uncertainties regarding spatiotemporal transitions of electric vehicles (EVs) travel, charging behavior, and the phase connection to three-phase distribution grids, a method is proposed for stochastic simulation of three-phase EV charging load distribution based on trip chains and K-Means clustering. Firstly, a user travel pattern model is established using data from the 2022 Next Generation National Household Travel Survey (NextGen NHTS) for the United States. Then, by employing Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) to extract the spatiotemporal characteristics of user travel, and marking the phase connection for each electric vehicle connected to the distribution network, the three-phase electric vehicle charging load for different regions over multiple travel days can be obtained. Finally, the distribution of three-phase charging loads across various regions and time periods is determined through K-Means clustering.

articleTitle: A topology map search algorithm for power grid fault location
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In this paper, the topology of the variable circuit breaker is analysed. The complementary variable circuit breaker related to the variable circuit breaker is determined by constructing a fork tree with a certain variable circuit breaker as the apex to determine the minimum cut set of the variable circuit breaker, and the power grid primary equipment within the minimum cut range is used as the fault candidate primary device, to analyse the power grid candidate fault equipment accurately.

articleTitle: A voltage strength calculation method of receiving end grid for large-scale renewable energy DC transmission
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Driven by the carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals, China is planning to strengthen the construction of new HVDC channels to support the large-scale renewable energy consumption, and it is necessary to evaluate the voltage strength of the receiving end grid at the inverter station bus. The short-circuit ratio(SCR) is no longer applicable in systems with a high proportion of renewable energy, as it only considers the short-circuit current provided by the synchronous machinesources and does not take into account the supporting effect of the non-synchronous-machine sources on the system voltage. This article proposes a voltage strength calculation method of receiving end power grid for large-scale renewable energy DC transmission. On the basis of the concept of voltage stiffness, this method takes into account the influence of dynamic components during transient processes and simplifies the influence between DCs. Finally, the voltage strength calculation method proposed in this paper is verified to have more significance than SCR by combining a case study of the East China Power Grid with a high proportion of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Facile construction of functionally graded insulator using integrated 3D printing-vacuum casting approach
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Functionally graded insulation (FGI) is a novel concept of electrical insulation, which has a spatially non-uniform distribution of permittivity and/or conductivity. Previous studies have verified that the effectiveness of FGI in the field of electric field equalization without increasing the complexity of insulation structure. However, the complexity of the conventional fabrication process challenges the industrial-grade application of FGI insulation. Herein, a facile method, named as integrated 3D printing-vacuum casting, is introduced to address the challenge of FGI construction. General step of the proposed method is firstly introduced, and two cases including an 12kV non-uniform post insulator and a lattice-based permittivity graded insulator. The proposed fabrication method provides a novel approach for high-performance insulation system in both AC and DC GIS/GIL devices with advanced insulation performance and elevated operation reliability.

articleTitle: Fault diagnosis of batteries in energy storage systems based on model fusion
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the widespread application of energy storage systems, thermal runaway of lithium-ion batteries has become an increasingly serious concern. Currently, most studies related to battery fault diagnosis focus on exploring external characteristics of the batteries to detect potential faults. However, some external characteristics like voltage inconsistency may not be strongly correlated with battery faults, thus traditional fault diagnosis fail to establish sufficient and necessary relationships with faults. To solve this problem, we propose a novel solution to the deficiencies of traditional battery fault diagnostics by considering both the internal states of batteries and risky usage behaviors throughout operational life. To fulfill this idea, an electrochemical model is established to capture battery internal states and a risk accumulation coefficient to characterize battery risky behaviors. On top of these, a self-attention mechanism model is employed to identify potential faults by fusing results from both aspects. The proposed method is trained and verified using data from real-world batteries and achieves an accuracy rate of 97.37%. Compared to existing methods, the proposed method offers higher fault identification accuracy with deeper understanding of fault development and triggering mechanisms.

articleTitle: Test device, method, and result analysis for impulse breakdown characteristics of frozen soil in high altitude regions up to 5500m
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Frozen soil is an important characteristic of the soil in high altitude regions up to 5500m, and its impact on the grounding characteristics of grounding devices cannot be ignored. However, there has been limited research in the past, especially on the impact characteristics of grounding devices in frozen soil environments. This article introduced the impact test of frozen soil, including the test devices, test steps, test methods, test results, and analysis of influencing factors. In the experiment, the effects of temperature, moisture, and salinity on the breakdown characteristics of frozen soil were mainly considered. Through experiments, the following conclusions have been drawn. (1) As the temperature decreased, the initial breakdown field strength of the soil would continue to increase. Subsequently, as the temperature further decreased, the rate of increase in the initial breakdown field strength of the soil slowed down and saturation occurred. (2) The higher the soil moisture content, the greater the increase in the initial breakdown field strength of the soil as the temperature decreased. When the temperature was constant and the soil moisture content changed, the change in the initial breakdown field strength was more complex, depending on the size of the soil temperature. (3) The intervention of salt increased the concentration of conductive ions in soil solution and further lowered the freezing point of soil moisture, thus greatly reducing the initial breakdown field strength of frozen soil.

articleTitle: Thermodynamic theory-based calculation model for transformer oil pyrolysis gases
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Accurately quantifying gas production during internal faults in transformers is paramount for advancing the digitization and intelligence of electric power equipment. This paper introduces a model grounded in thermodynamics to calculate transformer oil pyrolysis gases, leveraging chemical equilibrium theory to explore temperature-dependent factors such as heat capacity, reaction enthalpy change, and equilibrium constants. By introducing a reaction factor to quantify gas molecule molar fractions, the model establishes a system of chemical equilibrium equations to track gas molecule evolution with temperature. Employing 1 mol of propane as a research subject, our study demonstrates that chain scission reactions predominantly govern thermal cracking reactions of alkanes, with their likelihood increasing with temperature, followed closely by dehydrogenation reactions. The observed evolution of molar fractions aligns well with actual gas generation in oil, offering a reliable method for accurately calculating dissolved gases. This advancement holds promise for enhancing fault diagnosis and maintenance strategies in transformer systems. Further research could explore practical implementations and expand the model's scope to diverse fault scenarios.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation of flexible ultrasonic technology for detection of internal defects in cable sealing layer
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The lead sealing layer has an important sealing and waterproofing role in various terminal joints and intermediate connections of the metal lead sheath of the cable. In this paper, the finite element analysis method is used to investigate the detection and localisation effect of array ultrasonic technology in the simulation of cable lead sealing layer defects. In COMSOL Multiphysics software to build a two-dimensional cable structure model containing different sizes of sealing layer defects, the establishment of "acoustic-thermal-solid mechanics" multi-physical field coupling model, to achieve the acoustic field inside the cable terminals, the coupling effect of thermal field and solid mechanics, simulated ultrasonic propagation characteristics of the cable structure, and analysed the detection and location of defects in the cable. The propagation characteristics of ultrasonic wave in the cable structure are simulated, and the echo signals received at the detection point are analysed to achieve the detection and positioning of sealing defects. By analysing and simulating typical defects, the results show that there is a significant difference between the echo signals received at the detection point of a defective sealing layer and a non-defective sealing layer.

articleTitle: Research on active filter control strategy for 5th background harmonic amplification at Jinhua station
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Ultra high voltage direct current transmission is the main In this paper, the principle and topology of APF are compared firstly, and then the scheme of adding APF is designed according to the phenomenon that the 5th harmonic of Jinhua converter station exceeds the standard. The control target of APF is studied, and the minimum current output capability of APF is calculated by mathematical formula, and the specific control strategy is designed based on the result of control target. Finally, the simulation model of PSCAD is built to verify the correctness of the control strategy. The results show that the scheme of adding active filter can effectively reduce the low order harmonics of converter station.

articleTitle: Research on the decoupling dimension reduction method for control boundary of the new distribution system considering network constraints
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The construction of a new power system dominated by new energy sources urgently requires the exploration of flexible load-side regulation resources to participate in grid regulation. It is difficult to control a large amount of distributed resources that are dispersed. By aggregating distributed resources into a unified entity to participate in the regulation of the system, the control boundary faces the challenge of high-dimensional variables considering the internal limitations of the aggregation. This paper abstracts the above problem as solving the projection problem of high-dimensional nonlinear state space on the P-Q coupling plane: establishing control boundary projection resolution models considering the nonlinear constraints for safe operation of the aggregation and employing a novel high-dimensional state space projection algorithm. Through a two-step solution process of vertex “search-mapping,” an accurate projection of the aggregation's control boundary is obtained, and the feasibility of the proposed method is verified through IEEE case studies.

articleTitle: Transmission line dynamic thermal rating capacity enhancement for utility-scale renewable integrated grid considering the dust effects
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Renewable energy bases are typically in uninhabited, dry, and windy areas. These bases are highly susceptible to dust impacts due to the atmospheric environmental changes brought about by the recent rise in global temperature. Since 2023, influenced by global meteorological changes, China's northwest and northeast regions have experienced the fourth large-scale dust storm event. However, the widely used line thermal balance equations still need to be restructured to model the meteorological conditions of renewable energy bases, leading to overly optimistic conclusions in capacity increase calculations. Therefore, this study first analyzes the impact of the environment on the thermal stability limit of a specific renewable energy transmission network in China; it focuses on the dust impact in renewable energy bases, analyses the effect of dust heating on the thermal stability of the lines, and proposes an improved thermal stability model considering the dust heating effect. Furthermore, to address the uncertainty associated with dust effects, a fuzzy analysis-based method is introduced for calculating control parameters of the dust heating power. The proposed methods have been validated for accurately estimating the capacity enhancement of lines under dust impact through an actual power grid case in a specific location in northwest China.

articleTitle: Research and implementation of low frequency harmonic detection in power grid based on sliding window peak search algorithm
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: By studying complex algorithms for detecting low-frequency harmonic signals in the power grid, including Prony method, ARMA, wavelet analysis method, FFT transformation method, etc., most of these algorithms are numerical calculations and offline analysis, with huge computational complexity and are not suitable for online analysis. On this basis, a method of sliding window analysis for the power point sequence of the power grid was proposed, which comprehends the principle of simplicity and simplicity. Based on low-pass filtering of the power sequence, the peak and valley were found according to the characteristics of low-frequency harmonics through sliding window differentiation. A series of logical algorithms were used to infer and locate the peak and valley, and on this basis, the frequency of low-frequency oscillation was calculated. This algorithm has simple calculation, small computational complexity, fast computation speed, and is suitable for real-time online analysis and other detection scenarios. The algorithm has undergone practical simulation and verification, with high detection accuracy and can replace traditional mathematical calculation methods, and has high practical value.

articleTitle: Research on the optimal control strategy of voltage management in distributed photovoltaic grid-connected station area
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the promotion of the national "dual carbon" target policy, the installed capacity and scale of distributed photovoltaic have expanded rapidly. The new energy power generation represented by photovoltaic itself has fluctuations, intermittency, as well as the problems of on-site grid-connected power generation and local consumption difficulties in photovoltaic station areas, resulting in large-scale photovoltaic power stations across the country being connected to the power grid will affect the power quality of distribution networks and rural electricity, especially causing voltage elevation and affecting the reliability of users' electricity consumption. Therefore, the construction of distributed photovoltaic stations in high-permeability areas not only changes the power flow distribution of the distribution network, but also affects the voltage level, harmonic content and fluctuation degree of the distribution network. In this paper, the voltage overrun problem of distributed photovoltaic station area is realized based on the residual capacity of the inverter, and the voltage tracking control is realized through instruction synthesis and current tracking control algorithm, and the simulation analysis and verification of the grid-connected scenario of photovoltaic station area in a certain area of Zhejiang Province are verified by MATLAB/Simulink, and the results show that the method has strong robustness and stability.

articleTitle: A flexible hybrid EMT-RMS simulation framework based on the unified fault matrix method
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The hybrid electromagnetic (EMT) and root-mean square (RMS) simulation is an effective simulation method for investigating the dynamic performance of a hybrid AC/DC transmission system. This work presents a ﬂexible combined EMT and RMS simulation framework, including a RMS-type simulation framework based on a uniﬁed fault matrix method for AC networks. Both symmetrical and unsymmetrical short circuits can be simulated in the AC network just through selecting the corresponding fault matrix. The comprehensive simulation framework is developed using MATLAB/Simulink, with each component meticulously modelled using matrices or Simulink blocks. Notably, no masks are used in the implementation, allowing the reader to gain a deep understanding of the framework and facilitating future development efforts. Throughout this work, power system engineers and researchers are enabled to model their hybrid AC/DC transmission systems in own ways in the future.

articleTitle: The adaptive suppression method for high-frequency oscillations in renewable energy generation system integrated with multi-terminal MMC-HVDC
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the increasing scale of renewable energy bases, multi-terminal modular multilevel converter based High voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) transmission technology has gradually become an important technical way of renewable energy transmission. However, the high-frequency oscillation (HFO) problem is becoming more and more prominent since the fast control dynamics of renewable energy unit and the long control time delay of MMC. The characteristics of HFO in terms of amplitude, frequency and evolution are affected by the operating conditions of renewable energy sources, and the existing active HFO suppression strategies are difficult to respond to the oscillations under different operating conditions. Therefore, this paper proposes an adaptive HFO suppression strategy for renewable energy transmitting system via multi-terminal MMC-HVDC system based on upper-layer coordinated communication. This strategy can accurately locate the dominant converter station by uploading the oscillation information of each station, transforming the multi-terminal cooperative suppression into single-station adaptive control, simplifying the difficulty of control system design, and solving the problem of poor suppression of HFO since the change of oscillation characteristics under multiple operating conditions.

articleTitle: Analysis of multi-source oscillation characteristic of PV-thermal-bundled power transmission by LCC-HVDC system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the integration of large-scare renewable energy, the dynamic interaction among heterogeneous devices becomes stronger and the oscillation issue may be more prominent in the photovoltaic (PV)-thermal-bundled power transmission by line commutated converter based high voltage direct current (LCC-HVDC) system. This paper establishes the state-space model for such system. Eigenvalue analysis is employed to extract the weak-damping oscillation modes in the sub-synchronous frequency band. Then the stability variation characteristics of these oscillation modes are investigated by the eigenvalue loci analysis under different ratios of thermal power and PV. It is found out that three interactive oscillation modes may be successively excited with the decrease of thermal power proportion, which can be classified into the synchronous generator (SG)-dominated mode, PV-dominated mode and LCC-dominated mode. That is, there exists a risk of multi-source oscillations at the low thermal power proportion in the PV-thermal-bundled power transmission by LCC-HVDC system. The simulation results verify the multi-source oscillation characteristic in such system.

articleTitle: Arc simulation analysis of circuit breakers under different current breaking conditions
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Breaking short-circuit current and harmonic current are two strict breaking conditions for circuit breakers. Current experimental methods are difficult to test the breaking ability of circuit breakers under the influence of harmonic current, short-circuit current , and arc after arc under high voltage and high harmonic components. Therefore, based on the coupling simulation method of magnetohydrodynamics and circuits, this paper numerically models the arc characteristics of SF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sub>circuit breakers under power frequency and harmonic current, as well as the arc characteristics under short-circuit current. The influence of harmonic current and short-circuit current on the opening of SF6 circuit breakers is analyzed, The conclusion is drawn that the arc current may have an earlier zero crossing at higher harmonic frequencies and is more likely to cause arc reignition when the short-circuit current recovery voltage rise rate is large.

articleTitle: Research on the altitude correction coefficient for pollution flashover of 420kN DC insulators
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper covers the test and research on the altitude correction coefficient for 420kN DC porcelain insulators used in UHV projects. The insulator pollution flashover discharge tests were carried out in Beijing Pollution Test Base (45m) and Xizang High Altitude Test Base (4300m), which yielded the pollution flashover altitude correction coefficients for 420kN insulators of varying umbrella types at an altitude of 45m and 4300m. The test results showed that the insulators had an altitude correction coefficient of 0.035 and 0.045 respectively at 0.05 and 0.08 salt deposit density conditions. Given application of the withstand pollution test, the external insulation configuration of I type and V type insulator strings for ±800kV DC lines at an altitude of 0-4000m is recommended.

articleTitle: An insulation evaluation method of transformer OIP bushings based on WGAN under unbalanced samples
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of poor classification and difficult diagnosis of multi-source information caused by the imbalance between normal and abnormal samples, a method of fault data expansion based on WGAN was proposed. To solve the problem of unbalanced amount of 275 OIP bushings produced from 1990 to 2017 in the southern region of China, WGAN was used to effectively expand the fault data to balance the data set. SVM was used to classify and train the data to test the effect of data expansion. When the fault state casing data is expanded to 125 groups, the classification effect is the best. SVM has a classification accuracy of 91.5% for the expanded data set, which is 22.39% higher than that without expansion. By sample expansion, the problem of low evaluation accuracy of fault casing caused by sample imbalance is effectively solved, which has broad engineering application prospects.

articleTitle: The research and application of differentiated prediction methods for flexible load types in virtual power plants
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the development of smart grids and distributed energy resources, virtual power plants serve as a key platform for integrating and optimizing distributed resources. Their operational efficiency and stability are crucial to the overall performance of the power system. As an essential component of virtual power plants, flexible loads exhibit diverse and adjustable power consumption patterns. Therefore, accurate prediction of these loads is pivotal for optimizing the operation of virtual power plants. This paper first analyzes the characteristics of different types of flexible loads in virtual power plants, including their power variation properties, ability to respond to scheduling instructions, and external influencing factors. To address the prediction challenges associated with various types of flexible loads, this paper proposes differentiated prediction methods. These methods combine multiple techniques such as time series analysis, machine learning, and deep learning to improve prediction accuracy and real-time performance, meeting the precise control requirements of flexible loads in virtual power plants. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods, this paper selects actual virtual power plant cases for simulation analysis. The results show that compared to traditional prediction methods, the differentiated prediction methods proposed in this paper achieve significant improvements in accuracy and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Research on harmonic impedance characteristics of low- and medium-frequency grid-forming wind turbine generators
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Due to the effects of control systems, wind turbine generators (WTGs) can exhibit complex dynamic characteristics and may cause harmonic or resonance problems in the interconnected system. Impedance analysis is one of the effective means to analyze such problems. Existing studies usually focus on grid-following WTGs or grid-forming (GFM) WTGs operating at the power frequency, while GFM-WTGs operating at low or medium frequencies do not get much attention. However, these two types of WTGs are considered to be promising for remote offshore wind farms. Therefore, this paper set out to investigate the harmonic impedance characteristics of low- and medium-frequency GFM-WTGs. Firstly, the structures of these two types of WTGs are introduced. Then, their analytical impedance models are established by the harmonic linearization method. Finally, based on the derived models, the harmonic impedance characteristics of low- and medium-frequency GFM-WTGs are analyzed, as well as the effects of different controllers on the impedance. It is found that they exhibit negative resistance effects around the fundamental frequency, and their harmonic impedance characteristics are strongly influenced by the voltage controller.

articleTitle: Research on turn-off control strategy of novel hybrid commutated converter based on reverse blocking IGCT
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Commutation Failure (CF) is an inherent problem faced by Line Commutated Converter based High Voltage Direct Current (LCC-HVDC) technology. To completely solve the problem of commutation failure, a novel Hybrid Commutated Converter (HCC) technology based on reverse blocking integrated gate commutated thyristor (RB-IGCT) has been proposed, which can utilize two methods for commutation: grid voltage commutation and active turn-off forced commutation. Based on the principle of HCC commutation, this paper proposes four different active turn-off control strategies and analyses them to determine two feasible active turn-off criteria: current change rate and natural commutation point. Then, the HCC with two control strategies is modelled, and the effects of the two control strategies acting alone and together are simulated and analysed using the simulation model. Based on the simulation results, an active turn-off control strategy suitable for HCC is proposed. Finally, the requirements of the active turn-off strategy for the control system were proposed, and the advantages brought by the application of HCC were analysed, providing a reference for the control strategy design of HCC.

articleTitle: Study on the aging characteristics of silicone rubber for ultra-high voltage indoor composite insulators
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Material aging is an unavoidable problem in the operation of composite insulators, but due to the fact that indoor composite insulators operate in a relatively good environment compared to outdoor, there has been little attention paid to the possibility of failures of indoor composite outer insulating equipment under long-term operation. In this paper, an ultra-high project indoor a composite insulator silicone rubber sheath to carry out research, through Hydrophobicity test, Water Absorption test, Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), Thermogravimetric Analysis (TGA) and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM) and other means to analyse the aging characteristics and the degree of the composite insulator silicone rubber sheath has been found to have a significant aging phenomenon, the aging depth should be in the range of one millimetre, and much less than one millimetre. The results of the experimental study in this paper can support the operation and maintenance and fault diagnosis of external insulating equipment in future UHV projects.

articleTitle: The research of the control and protection adaptability for the controllable line commutated converter
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The high capacity and long-distance transmission ability are the major advantages of the high voltage DC transmission system using Line Commutated Converter, which makes it one of the major transmission approaches in our country. However, the single-time or consecutive commutation failures during the AC system fault are the main drawbacks of the HVDC transmission using LCC valve, severely affecting the normal operation and power transmission. In this case, a new type of controllable line commutated converter (CLCC), which is embedded with the power electronics IGBT forcing commutation, is applied to avoid the commutation failure, therefore preventing the disturbance caused by the commutation failure like the traditional HVDC transmission system using LCC valve. This paper proposes the adaptive control and protection approaches according to the operation characteristics of the CLCC, and the optimizing approaches are also provided to improve the performance of the HVDC transmission system. This article provides reference for the world’s first HVDC transmission system using CLCC.

articleTitle: Analysis of key construction techniques for the Ge'nan HVDC renovation project
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of continuous blocking of multi-infeed DC system, State Grid Corporation proposed controllable line commutated converter(CLCC) scheme in 2020, which can fundamentally eliminate the long-term threat caused by commutation failure. Taking the Ge'nan HVDC Renovation Project as an example, this paper elaborates the installation details of the new controllable line commutated converter from three aspects: valve tower installation process, installation point analysis and risk control, so as to provide reference for similar projects in the future.

articleTitle: Analysis of oscillation events and optimization of low-voltage ride-through logic for buckwheat photovoltaic power plants in Yunnan
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the large-scale access of new energy, the impact on the security and stability of the power grid has become increasingly prominent [1]. From 2011 to 2012, there were a number of large-scale off-grid accidents of wind farms in China, so that the safety and stability of wind power operation quickly received attention from all parties in the industry, and the industry also began to actively respond from technical specifications, unit transformation, automatic voltage control (AVC), system deployment and other aspects. Get a significant improvement. Subsequently, the problem of broadband oscillation caused by new energy grid-connection has received extensive attention, and a large number of research results have been formed in terms of mechanism, analysis methods and suppression measures [2]. In recent years, some new engineering practical problems have been exposed in the field operation of new energy. Among them, the non-periodic and repeated voltage fluctuations of the wind power collection system occurred in the Northern Hebei Power Grid, resulting in large-scale off-grid of wind turbines for several times, with the maximum wind power output loss of 476,000 kW[3]. On August 15, 2023, Yunnan Qiaodi Photovoltaic Station (Qiaodi photovoltaic power station installed capacity of 240MW, Qiaodi photovoltaic power station has a total of 2 sets of 120MVA combined transformer, a total of 12 collector wires, 76 box transformers, 1064 sets of Tebsike 228 kW series inverter, The out-of-area disturbance of two Sisource 50MVar SVG causes the PV inverter to enter and exit the low-voltage crossing logic repeatedly, and causes the output power of the PV station to appear forced power oscillation. The paper presented solutions to solve the problems.

articleTitle: An improved YOLOv5 algorithm for fault diagnosis of infrared transmission line images
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the rapid development of society, our demand for electricity is increasing. We need to lay more power transmission cables. Transmission lines will undergo various harsh environmental tests and encounter various problems during operation. The occurrence of transmission line faults can cause serious hidden dangers to the power grid, and the safety issues of transmission lines have become increasingly serious. To effectively solve this problem, we need to quickly detect faults in transmission lines to ensure the safe operation of the power transportation system. However, traditional infrared fault detection methods are mainly based on manual detection and are now difficult to meet the development needs of today's era. Therefore, this article proposes a deep learning based fault target detection algorithm for transmission lines. We can effectively achieve automatic identification of transmission line faults through an improved Yolov5-TL algorithm.

articleTitle: The tendency of grain boundary potential barrier changes of water-induced degraded ZnO arrester – experimental and simulation results
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: ZnO arrester plays an important role in protection of transit overvoltage to power equipment. The degradation is inevitable as the equipment is operated for a long period of time. Water-induced degradation is one of the most common causes of arrester failure. The sensitive of leakage current to monitor the tendency of water-induced degradation is relatively low. To improve the monitoring method, the mesoscopic characteristics and mechanisms of the water-induced degradation of ZnO arrester need to be investigated. In this paper, the experiments of water-induced degradation of ZnO arresters re conducted using three types of ZnO arrester with different kinds of glazes. The grain boundary potential barrier (PB) changes before and after experiments are measured and compared. A microstructure model of ZnO arrester based on the Voronoi mesh is established. The influence of PB change of ZnO arrester is calculated.

articleTitle: Research on small signal modeling of MMC-HVDC under asymmetric operating conditions
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The modeling of modular multilevel converters (MMC) under symmetric conditions have received widespread attention. In practical engineering, the modular multilevel converter may operates under asymmetric operating conditions, such as asymmetrical bridge arm inductance and asymmetrical AC-side voltage. Unlike in symmetric conditions, where the MMC only exhibits coupling between a pair of mirrored frequencies, when operating under asymmetric conditions, the system experiences coupling between multiple frequencies and different phase sequences. Considering the multi-frequency coupling effect of the system and accurately characterizing the coupling admittance for each frequency is a challenge in small signal modeling of MMC-HVDC under asymmetric operating conditions. Therefore, this paper mainly establishes an impedance model suitable for asymmetric conditions of MMC. In addition, this paper introduces the Sequence Coupling Coefficient (SCC) to quantify the degree of system asymmetry, and investigates the impact of various factors on the system's level of asymmetry. Finally, Taking the Lu Xi back-to-back asynchronous interconnection project in Guangxi side as an example, the accuracy of the established model under various asymmetric conditions were verified through electromagnetic transient simulation using PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Emergency control of energy storage system to improve multi-timescale frequency stability in active distribution networks
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the integration of large-scale renewable energies into the grid, the uncertainty of source-load dual ends increases the operational fluctuations of the system, leading to reduced system inertia and frequency stability, thereby significantly increasing the security risks in power grid operation. Traditional load shedding directly impacts social and economic activities, and conventional power sources, constrained by their response speeds, are increasingly inadequate for the emergency control requirements of modern power systems. Taking energy storage power support as the starting point, this study elucidates the mechanism of improving multi-timescale frequency stability in the power grid through the participation of electrochemical energy storage in emergency control. The research investigates the frequency stability effects of energy storage participating in emergency control under different influencing factors and conducts simulation experiments to validate the frequency stability effects under different control parameters.

articleTitle: Research on the localization of latent fault sections in distribution networks based on the ratio of main and side resonance frequencies energy values
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In response to the difficulties in selecting the centroid frequency of transient latent fault currents in distribution networks and the unclear frequency-domain amplitude information, a method for locating distribution network latent faults based on the ratio of main and side resonance frequencies energy values is proposed. After a latent fault occurs in the distribution network, its transient zero-sequence current contains rich frequency-domain information. For faults upstream, there is a significant difference between the energy values of main and side resonance frequencies, resulting in a higher ratio. Conversely, for faults downstream, the energy values of main and side resonance frequencies are closer, and the ratio approaches 1. Therefore, utilizing the maximum absolute difference in the ratio of energy values of adjacent detection points enables the determination of the latent fault section. MATLAB/Simulink simulations confirm the reliability of this method in identifying fault sections under different latent fault conditions.

articleTitle: Investigation on long-distance 10GW new energy transmission technology
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The Badain Jaran desert in Inner Mongolia is rich in scenic resources with over 10GW of renewable energy that can be developed. However, there is a severe lack of conventional power sources near the Badain Jaran desert which is too far from the AC power grid, only ultra-high voltage AC or DC technology can be used to ensure the safe and stable transmission of new energy electricity as much as possible. Therefore, this paper focuses on the application of ultra-high voltage AC and DC transmission technologies in the large-scale external transmission of new energy in the Badain Jaran desert, analyzes the possible stability issues under the two technologies, and proposes the supporting engineering or power grid requirements that the two technologies should have. The investigation can provide ideas for the development of new energy in other remote Shagohuang bases, and thereby improve the utilization rate of new energy.

articleTitle: High-frequency impedance modeling and analysis of LCC-HVDC transmission system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: High voltage direct current (LCC-HVDC) technology based on grid commutation converter is increasingly used to connect large-scale new energy to the grid and transmit power over long distances. However, high-frequency oscillation in the output system of HVDC can limit power transmission capacity and impact the safe operation of the power grid. Existing impedance modeling often fails to consider the influence of the receiving end converter station and power network strength. To accurate ly analyze the impedance characteristics of LCC-HVDC systems, this thesis establishes an impedance analytical model that considers the impact of the receiving end. Using double Fourier transform, the frequency domain expression of the switching function is obtained and combined with the DC transmission line model to establish the impedance model of the LCC-HVDC transmission system. The analysis of parameters on the impedance characteristics of the converter station provides a basis for understanding the oscillation mechanism.

articleTitle: Data-enabled predictive control for frequency regulation in grid-forming controlled energy storage systems
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Recently, the increasing integration of power electronic converters interfaced renewable energy sources (RES) has posed great challenges to the stability of modern power systems. Grid-forming (GFM) energy storage systems (ESS) are an effective means to mitigate issues such as weak grid support capacity and frequency fluctuations. This paper establishes a hybrid system model comprising grid-following (GFL) renewable energy converters and GFM energy storage converters. The adopted virtual synchronous generator (VSG) enhances the stability of weak grids with high renewable energy penetration. Based on this model, a data-enabled predictive control (DeePC) is applied to GFM-ESS. The algorithm predicts future trajectories based solely on the input/output data of the system and adjusts the power output reference values of the GFM-ESS in real-time quickly and accurately, improving the frequency regulation capability of GFM-ESS and enhancing the stability of weak grids with high renewable energy penetration. Finally, a hybrid system simulation model is established to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy in enhancing system transient stability.

articleTitle: A modeling method for DC microgrid based on improved time domain model
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In DC microgrid modeling, power electronic converters generally adopt the state-space average model, which can achieve higher computational efficiency by ignoring higher harmonics. In order to achieve accurate modeling of the system, it is necessary to consider the sideband component generated by the modulation link, and the increase of the harmonic component will lead to the complexity of the modeling process and the large variable dimension. In view of the above problems, an improved modeling method for DC-DC converter is proposed on the basis of the average model. By analyzing the generation mechanism of harmonic components under different control modes, the discontinuous switching function is fitted with high precision based on the Fourier expansion of triangular form. The simulation results show that the method can maintain higher model accuracy without increasing the number of variables. Then, the proposed method is applied to DC microgrid modeling under constant power load. Compared with detailed switching model, state space average model and dynamic phasor model, it is proved that the proposed method can meet the requirements of model accuracy and solution efficiency.

articleTitle: Harmonic resonance analysis and parameter optimization method for DC distribution systems considering different interlinking converters
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In a DC distribution system, the strong coupling between multiple converters and busbars often leads to the phenomenon of harmonic resonance interaction, posing a threat to the safe and stable operation of the system. This paper firstly establishes a harmonic impedance model for a double-bus DC system, and then analyses the resonance transmission amplification characteristics through the different interlinking converters, including the isolated DC-DC converter, i.e., Dual active bridge (DAB), and the non-isolated DC-DC converters, i.e., Buck and Boost. Subsequently, a method for optimizing the control parameters of interlinking converters is proposed according to the transmission characteristics of the converters. The proposed method utilizes the hierarchical variable weighting approach to score the impedance matrices under different parameters and identifies the optimal parameters based on the highest scores. The results show that the proposed method provides a guidance for parameter optimization to suppress harmonic resonance transmission and amplification in DC distribution system.

articleTitle: Failure analysis of blocking leakage for high voltage RB-GCT
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The GCT chip is the core component unit of the integrated gate commutated thyristor (IGCT) device, which mainly includes three electrodes: gate, cathode, and anode. The gate is controlled by the driving current to switch and block the cathode-anode current. In this paper, combining the structure and manufacturing process of the GCT device, a failure analysis method combining macroscopic and microscopic analysis, such as bidirectional blocking characteristic detection of the gate-anode, hot spot positioning on both sides, optical detection, SEM detection, composition analysis, and SRP test, was used to locate and analyse the failure of the high-voltage GCT chip with abnormal problems caused by excessive leakage of the gate-anode blocking characteristic. Finally, the key failure location and failure reasons were determined.

articleTitle: Adaptive Spearman correlation coefficient-based unit protection for collection clusters in DC series-parallel offshore wind systems
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: DC series-parallel systems are a critical technology to the development of distant offshore wind power. However, most existing DC line protection methods suffer from restrictions when applying to the collection cables characterised by multiple interconnections and weak boundary features. To overcome the limitations, this paper proposes a unit protection method for collection clusters based on the adaptive Spearman correlation coefficient (ASCC) of line-mode current. Firstly, this paper elaborates on the configuration of a DC series-parallel system and analyses its fault characteristics. Then, the ASCC improved by dynamic time warping algorithm is utilised to assess the waveform similarities of line-mode current with different time window lengths, and the faulty zone identification criterion is established. Finally, the proposed unit protection method is evaluated on the MATLAB/Simulink platform. The results verify that the method can accurately identify faults of different resistances and distances, and is robust against 30-dB noise.

articleTitle: High-power high-voltage cascaded energy storage system based on IGCT-plus
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: A high-power energy storage system (HESS) with the capability to directly connect to power grids operating at over ten thousand volts and store and release energy exceeding hundreds of megawatts is a key device for enhancing large-scale new energy consumption and addressing deficiencies in active support capabilities. This article proposes a high-voltage HESS topology based on high-capacity IGCT-Plus devices, analyzes the commutating characteristics of IGCT-Plus power modules, and conducts experimental tests to validate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed HESS scheme based on IGCT-Plus devices.

articleTitle: Research on on-site measurement error of tuning frequency of AC filters in HVDC converter station
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In HVDC transmission project, it is necessary to carry out AC filter tuning test before the AC filter is put into operation to ensure that the error between actual tuning frequency and design tuning frequency is within 1% (refer to Q/GDW 11750.5-2017 Sub-system test standard in UHV converter station Part 5: Sub-system test for AC filter field). Taking the HP24/36 filter of Shanghaimiao station as an example, the tuning frequencies are designed to be 1200 Hz and 1800 Hz. However, the on-site measured tuning frequency of HP24/36 filter is 1179 Hz and 1775 Hz respectively.
