After research, it was found that the main reasons for the error in the measured tuning frequency of AC filters are as follows:(1) The element value of AC filter has deviation; (2) Considering the resistance element in the filter, there is a small deviation between the actual tuning frequency and the designed tuning frequency; (3) There are measurement errors in measuring instruments; (4) The stray inductance of the connecting wire used in the measurement results in the measurement error. Therefore, it is recommended to take the filter tuning frequency obtained by the tuning characteristic tester (such as Bodian PF3000) as the reference, and take the tuning frequency calculated by the measured value of each filter element as the final result. When the error between the design tuning frequency and the calculated tuning frequency is less than 1%, it can be considered that the tuning test is passed.

articleTitle: A simple common-mode voltage reduction method for back-to-back five-level ANPC converters
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The back-to-back five-level active neutral-point clamped (BTB 5L-ANPC) converter is gaining attraction for high-power medium-voltage motor drives, especially in offshore wind power applications. However, its complex modulation introduces a challenge: the generation of a high-frequency common-mode voltage (CMV) with significant amplitude and dv/dt. This paper proposes a simple yet effective solution based on carrier-based pulse-width modulation (CBPWM). The method involves injecting two optimal zero-sequence voltages (ZSVs) into the rectifier and inverter sides, reducing the CMV amplitude to 1/12 of the DC-bus voltage. Unlike the more complex space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) alternative, this CBPWM- based approach offers a practical and easily implementable means to address CMV issues in BTB 5L-ANPC converters. The significance of this method lies in its potential to enhance the reliability and longevity of motor bearings, crucial for the robust performance of high-power medium-voltage motor drives in the context of offshore wind power generation.

articleTitle: Analyze overvoltage characteristic on flexible DC chopper type energy dissipation facilities
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Flexible DC chopper type energy dissipation device is a novel DC chopper for offshore wind power HVDC system,power module is the series connection by IGCT-Plus,its characteristic include simple structure and control strategy clearly.This paper analyze over voltage characteristic of component which is IGCT valve, series inductor,and series resistor base on the novel topology.Base on the PSCAD/EMTDC simulations, the withstand voltage level of the key equipment in the DC chopper device of YangJang converter sbstation is calculated.

articleTitle: Research on high frequency grounding grid technology in high-altitude ultra-high voltage test halls
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The development of high-voltage test halls of power transmission and transformation category urgently needs to obtain the ground potential distribution law of grounding device under the action of high-frequency current, so as to optimize the design of the grounding system of the test hall, and improve the safety and stability of the grounding system. In this paper, based on the very fast transient (VFT) voltage process that exists in the switching operation or ground fault of gas-insulated equipment, the high-frequency transient characteristics of the grounding device of the high-altitude ultra-high-voltage testing hall for gas-insulated equipment testing are analyzed and evaluated, and the technical research on high-frequency grounding network is carried out, which puts forward a kind of highly efficient and accurate computational model of the high-frequency characteristics of the grounding device, and provides the design of the grounding system of the test hall with It provides a strong computational simulation support for the design of the grounding system in the test laboratory.

articleTitle: Frequency domain fault ranging method based on parameter estimation for single-ended faults with anti-transition resistance in distribution networks
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: A frequency domain fault ranging method based on parameter estimation is proposed for the single-end transition resistance in distribution networks, which is based on the ratio η of the corresponding frequency component of the zero sequence current spectrum between the upstream side of the fault point and the first end of the faulted feeder. The equivalent circuit is used to simulate the spectral characteristics of η, the optimal equivalent circuit parameter values are obtained through parameter estimation, a neural network describing the mapping relationship between the fault distance, the fault closing angle and the equivalent circuit parameter is established, and the fault ranging objective function is constructed to solve the fault distance. Example analysis shows that the fault ranging method proposed in this paper is not affected by the transition resistance, and is suitable for distributed photovoltaic access distribution system.

articleTitle: Ultra-high speed non-unit protection for flexible DC transmission lines based on the ratio of second derivative of line-mode voltage
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Flexible DC transmission technology is crucial for addressing the current issues of integrating large-scale renewable energies , and effective line protection is essential for maintaining system safety. Current protections for flexible DC lines encounter challenges in handling high resistance and noise interference, which can result in failures to activate for internal high-resistance faults or trigger false operations due to noise. To address this problem, this paper proposes a non-unit protection principle for flexible DC transmission lines based on the ratio of positive to negative integrals of the second derivative of the line-mode voltage. This method utilizes the distinct waveform characteristics of the second derivative of line-mode voltage to identify fault locations, unaffected by transitional resistance; it also employs an information-entropy-based auxiliary criterion to prevent noise-induced false operations. Simulation results from PSCAD/EMTDC show that the proposed protection scheme quickly and reliably detects faults. It demonstrates strong resistance to transitional resistance and noise interference.

articleTitle: Islanding detection method for grid-forming inverter by reactive power injection
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The operation of grid-connected inverters in islanding presents critical issues for grid operation, utility workers' safety, and stakeholders, due to the control of voltage magnitude and frequency, reconnection caused by phase mismatch, among others. In such cases, grid-following inverters can detect islanding due to their current source operational characteristics, whether they are supplying 100% power or not. However, grid-forming inverters, during islanding with droop control, supply power at a frequency lower than the grid frequency under load, and cannot detect islanding when not supplying power due to their voltage source operation mode. To overcome this limitation of grid-forming inverters, this paper proposes a method to detect islanding by injecting reactive power into the power command of the droop controller. The method is validated through simulations in a 380V/60Hz system using PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Research on thermal aging decomposition characteristics of transformer oil
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In order to slow down the transformer thermal fault caused by thermal aging of insulating oil during the operation of oil-immersed transformer, this paper uses the simulation software Materials Studio to simulate the thermal aging process of mineral insulating oil based on the thermal aging conditions under actual working conditions of oil-immersed transformer, and adds nano SiO2 particles for modification to slow down its thermal aging rate and analyze its modification principle. The results show that the surface groups of nano SiO2 particles can react with the active particles produced in the thermal aging process of insulating oil, thus reducing the interreacting rate of the active particles and slowing down the cracking process of insulating materials. Moreover, the amount of acetylene produced by the modified insulating oil during the thermal aging process is greatly reduced, which indicates the probability of accidents can be reduced.

articleTitle: A novel nonlinear droop control for voltage stability performance in VSC-MTDC system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The linear droop control has been wildly applied in voltage source converter (VSC) based multi-terminal DC transmission (MTDC) systems to perform automatic power balancing. However, the large droop slope can increase the voltage ripple and risk of instability at the steady state although it narrows the voltage deviation. The voltage performance cannot be consistent at different operating points when involving the nonlinear droop control for various equivalent droop slopes to overcome the contradictions. To address the issues mentioned above, a novel nonlinear droop control with the reference self-correction algorithm is proposed, the essence of which is to guarantee that the equivalent droop slope could be rapidly magnified by the nonlinear relationship to the scale of disturbance, and the nonlinear droop curve could be moved to the new operating point to recover designed steady state performance so that keeping the consistency of voltage regulation after every disturbance. Thus, the benefits of the nonlinear droop curve, e.g., small dc voltage deviation will be preserved, meanwhile, the negative impact, e.g., voltage ripple, instability, and inconsistent power-voltage performance will be eliminated. The theoretical evaluation and simulation results of a four-terminal VSC-MTDC system in the PSCAD/EMTDC demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: The frequent commutation failure and solutions in UHVDC inverter station
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: An in-depth analysis is made on the frequent commutation failure of ±800kV UHVDC power transmission project in the initial operation stage. The investigation shows that the commutation failure is mainly caused by two factors. One is that the zero crossing of AC voltage caused by harmonics causes displacement, which causes the VBE to send trigger pulse to thyristor VBE (Valve Base Electronics) can not correctly recognize the negative voltage establishment signal of TCE (Thyristor Control Electronics), resulting in inverter side commutation failure, and in serious cases, multiple commutation failure occurs to block HVDC. The second is affected by the harmonic of the AC system, the commutation failure occasionally occurs, but the probability of occurrence is low. For the first case, the delay detection of negative voltage signal sent by VBE to TCE is proposed to cancel, and its correctness is verified by field simulation DC line restart test and DC line ground fault test. For the second case, an improved strategy for preventing commutation failure based on harmonic distortion rate is proposed. Simulation results verify the correctness of the scheme.

articleTitle: Stability analysis of sub-synchronous oscillation of VSCS connected to HVDCS in weak grids
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The renewables transferring electricity through HVDC has become a typical form in sending-end power systems of China. However, compared with the renewables transferring with ac grid, the interactions between renewables interfaced to voltage-source converters (VSCs) and HVDC may be more complicated, especially in a weak grid, which may cause sub-synchronous oscillation issues. To prevent such an oscillation issue, this paper proposes a novel impedance-based analysis method and investigates the crucial parameters of such an oscillation instability issue. Firstly, we derive thedq-impedance model of a system of a VSC connected to HVDC and the impedance model fully considers the dynamics of VSC and HVDC. Then, we reduce the obtained impedance model into a single-input single-output (SISO) model for evaluating the whole system's stability margin. The reduced SISO model not only considers all elements in the impedance matrix, but also facilitates analysing the dynamic interactions between the VSC and HVDC. The simulation results by MATLAB/Simulink verify the validity and accuracy of proposed method.

articleTitle: Surface charge accumulation characteristics with variations in location of adhered metal particle
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The study of the effect of the interaction between metal particles and surface charge within GIL is of great significance for DC GIL insulation performance enhancement and design. Therefore, we use the finite element method to establish the insulator surface charge accumulation model with metal particles attached to the center electrode, and consider the effect of different attachment heights on surface charge accumulation under microdischarge conditions. The results show that when metal particles are attached to the center electrode, homopolar charge spots appear on both the convex and convex sides of the insulator at the late charging stage. On the convex side of the insulator, the lower the height of the metal particles promot es the development of charge spots. For the region directly below the metal particles, the height increase reduces the pre-charge density and increases the speed of charge accumulation, which improves the charge density at the late charging stage.

articleTitle: A current balancing method with carrier-phase-shifted six-step direct-PWM stategy in multimodule current source converter
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper proposes a current balancing technique with carrier-phase-shifted six-step direct-PWM (CPS-SSDPWM) strategy in Multimodule Current-Source Converter (MCSC). The proposed method is able to balance the current of positive and negative inductors in parallel modules with no additional switching behaviors or losses realized by slightly adjustment of submodule (SM) modulation index. The fundamentals of MCSC and the principles of current balancing in MCSC are introduced. Then the six-step direct-PWM (SS-DPWM) in different carrier phase shifted modes are presented. A proposed current balancing method, of which the effect in odd and even modulation sectors are analyzed, is realized by adjusting the modulation index of SM with the measurement of ac-side voltage and dc current of SM inductance. Finally, the modulation and current balancing strategy is verified in RTDS digital real-time simulation, which presents expected current balance of 16 inductors in 8 parallel-connected SMs.

articleTitle: A hierarchical index evaluation system based on analytic hierarchy process (AHP) for photovoltaic collection system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the development of power electronics technologies, photovoltaic (PV) DC convergence can now effectively solve the problems caused by PV power stations connected to microgrids. In order to explore the advantages and disadvantages of AC and DC PV collection systems, this paper proposes a hierarchical index evaluation system of PV collection systems based on analytic hierarchy process (AHP). Under three different PV power levels, microgrids including PV, energy storage (ES) and electric vehicles (EV) are constructed, and the AC and DC PV convergence topologies are evaluated by considering five indicators: the comprehensive loss rate of the converter, the comprehensive line loss rate, the net exchange of electricity with the grid, the average power supply radius and the investment cost. The results show that the PV DC collection system has obvious advantages compared with the traditional AC collection system for the above five indexes. In addition, at each power level, the differences between different pooling schemes are evaluated, and the results show that the scheme with the photovoltaic capacity matching the charging demand of the electric vehicle connected to the low-voltage bus, and the remaining photovoltaic connected to the medium-voltage bus has the highest performance.

articleTitle: Modulation strategy of a DAB-type isolated DC-AC converter with reactive power support capabilities
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper investigates and designs a Dual Active Bridge (DAB) type DC-AC converter with reactive power support capabilities to enhance the energy efficiency of photovoltaic (PV) systems and improve grid power quality. The converter, which utilizes a transformer for voltage isolation and stepping up, connects to the grid through matrix-based bidirectional switches. Characterized by high conversion efficiency, a wide soft-switching range, and fewer power conversion stages, this design is particularly well-suited for distributed microinverter applications. By employing an extended phase-shift modulation strategy, the converter achieves wide power factor auto-regulation. It injects reactive currents with either leading or lagging phases into the grid, thereby ensuring stable operation. The performance and effectiveness of the proposed design are confirmed through experimental verification on a 450W prototype.

articleTitle: Optimised design of electric field simulation for insulated panels of 12kV environmentally friendly gas ring main unit
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: To solve the problem of electric field concentration at the three-phase junction of the insulating plate screw in the environmental gas ring main unit, this paper establishes a three-dimensional electric field simulation and analysis model of the insulating plate screw, calculates the distribution of the electric field at the three-phase junction of the insulating plate screw by using the finite-element electric field simulation and analysis software, and puts forward two optimization design schemes for the simulation of electric field, which is finally verified by the insulation test. The results of the study show that: the use of button type equalizing shell and equalizing ring two structural design can effectively improve the electric field strength distribution of the three-phase junction of the insulating plate screw, the maximum electric field strength value decreased by about 50%, the electric field coefficient of unevenness is reduced, and the insulation level is improved. At the same time, the insulation level of phase-to-phase IF withstand insulation level and lightning impact withstand insulation level have a 10% insulation margin. The results of this study provide a reference for the optimized design of the three-phase junction of the insulating plate screws of the environmental gas ring main unit.

articleTitle: Research on primary and secondary collaborative planning method of distribution network for self-balancing and self-optimizing
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The current distribution network planning and self-balancing and self-optimizing assessment are disconnected, resulting in the inability to directly feed back the self-balancing and self-optimizing assessment to the adjustment strategy of the primary and secondary system planning. To address the above issues, first, an embedded self-balancing constraints primary system planning method is proposed. On this basis, further consideration is given to the sensitivity of distribution automation equipment on the self-balancing and self-optimizing of the system, optimizing the configuration of circuit breakers and distribution automation equipment. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed planning method is verified based on actual engineering cases.

articleTitle: Modelling of high mesa structure, analysis of medium layer delamination and structural optimization
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The Gate-commutated thyristor (GCT) is a novel type of power semiconductor device primarily utilized for high-voltage and high-power control in power electronics applications. Our research observed a significant increase in gate-cathode leak current during high-temperature and high-current tests, often linked to delamination and fracture of the SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>dielectric layer on the cathode mesa sidewall. Our research establishes a thermal stress calculation model for the gate-commutated thyristor chips based on the fundamental principles of thermodynamics. Through thermodynamic simulations at 120°C, our research identified thermal stress as the primary cause of SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>dielectric layer failure. To reduce the probability of this kind of failure, it is advisable to minimize the angle of the cathode mesa during chip manufacturing.

articleTitle: The research on reduced order modeling based on singular perturbation theory in PV microgrid
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The model of PV microgrid exhibits high-order and nonlinear characteristics, which brings difficulty in stability analysis and parameter design. In order to address this issue, a method of reduced order modelling based on singular perturbation theory is proposed. Firstly, a full-order mathematical model is established, and the state variables are divided into fast response variables and slow response variables. Secondly, the reduced order model was derived based on the singular perturbation theory. Subsequently, a comparative analysis of eigenvalues and transient response were conducted, which demonstrate that the reduced order model was remaining the dominant dynamic characteristics to the greatest extent. Finally, the control parameters are optimised by stability analysis. The simulation results verify its validity and accuracy of the reduced order model.

articleTitle: Research on the customization of IGCT driver chip
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Integrated Gate Commutated Thyristor (IGCT) gate driver unit (GDU) is the key hub of secondary control systems and primary high-voltage and high-current power devices. However, the utilization of discrete devices in the driver design presents several drawbacks, including numerous components, limited electromagnetic immunity, reduced reliability, and increased power consumption. Consequently, the trend towards chipization in the advancement of IGCT drive technology is deemed inevitable. Due to the high level of integration required for digital-analog-power hybridization, the development of IGCT driver chips faces substantial hurdles, with current research efforts lacking both domestically and internationally. The study focuses on the customization research of IGCT gate driver chips, exploring their operational parameters and external constraints within the domain of energy and power applications. Subsequently, the architecture design and characteristic requirements of power specific integrated circuits (PSIC) are delineated, encompassing aspects such as functional module division, power sequencing, cross-domain ESD comprehensive protection schemes, and chip parameter definitions. Finally, a comprehensive layout floorplan strategy of the entire chip is conducted, considering area utilization, power distribution, and signal integrity. This paper contributes to the advancement of customized PSICs by providing insights and references within this realm.

articleTitle: Design and optimization of edge termination for 8.5kV RB-IGCT
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: A new double negative beveled angle edge termination structure, which utilises a mesa-like chamfer and decouples the junction depth of the active region and edge termination, has been proposed and the rule of the effect of various structural parameters on the edge termination’s breakdown voltage has been analysed. An optimization approach for the edge termination's structural parameters is presented, which can resolve the dual contradiction between the edge termination’s breakdown voltage and the active region's performance, as well as the edge termination’s breakdown voltage and process feasibility. TCAD simulation studies indicate that, under given conditions, the effective utilization rate of the chip area reaches 90.572%, while the breakdown voltage efficiency reaches 93.3%.

articleTitle: Analysis of internal stresses in porcelain parts of large tonnage disc suspension insulators subjected to internal hydrotesting
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Line insulators are an important part of overhead transmission lines. Among them, the suspended porcelain insulators need to be subjected to internal hydrostatic testing of the porcelain parts before gluing. In order to explore the internal hydrostat ic internal hydrostatic test of porcelain internal stress distribution and the actual working conditions of the insulator is subjected to tensile load the relationship between the internal stress distribution between the seat and the rationality of the design of the internal hydrostatic test conditions, the establishment of the hydrostatic load and tensile load insulator force model, calculated in the hydrostatic load and tensile load of the insulator porcelain stress distribution. The results show that: under the two working conditions, there are roughly the same stress concentration area inside the insulator; the maximum first principal stress at the corner of the neck is greater than that at the corner of the top of the head, which is greater than that on the inner wall of the head, and the maximum principal stress at the corner of the neck is most likely to be close to the permissible stress value, which will result in fracture damage.

articleTitle: Power tracking and control strategy of regional power grid with high permeability of renewable energy
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy will bring enormous difficulties to power grid scheduling. Although centralized power transmission can alleviate the peak shaving pressure of local units to some extent, the external transmission curve generally exhibits similar characteristics to the load curve, and the output of new energy may decrease from maximum output to zero or increase from zero to maximum output within the day. These two factors determine that the peak shaving task faced by new energy after large-scale integration into local regional power grids is still challenging. Therefore, in order to maximize the consumption of renewable energy while achieving the tracking of the given external transmission curve, it is necessary to carry out reasonable regulation of the units in the regional power grid. This paper comprehensively considers various power sources within the regional power grid, proposes a strategy for coordinated peak shaving of each power source at a weekly time scale, and establishes a unit combination optimization model for thermal power units to meet the peak shaving demand under high energy penetration rates. This model ensures that while tracking the external power curve and maximizing the absorption of new energy, it meets the requirements for safe system operation.

articleTitle: Research on simulation modeling of transient overvoltage in submarine cable transmission system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Submarine cable transmission engineering has developed rapidly in recent years, and it is of great significance to study the switching overvoltage levels of long-length cable lines during power system operation. This article relies on the 500 kV submarine cable project of an offshore wind farm to establish the simulation model. The simulation results show that after the three-phase circuit breaker tripped, the residual voltage caused the reclosing overvoltage. Affected by the line capacitance rise effect, the closer to the end of the line, the greater the overvoltage amplitude. When the circuit breaker is equipped with a 400Ω closing resistor, the overvoltage amplitude is significantly reduced. Furthermore, this article summarizes the factors affecting the switching overvoltage level of submarine cable systems and the corresponding solutions.

articleTitle: Research on droop control of power conversion system based on dynamic reconfigurable battery system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The dynamic reconfigurable battery system (DRBS) is very promising because it can overcome the “barrel effect” of conventional battery storage by flexibly connecting battery modules through process control. However, there is still a lack of research on the cooperation between DRBS and the power conversion system (PCS). In this paper, a reconfiguration strategy is designed based on a matrix dynamic reconfigurable battery network, considering SOC balancing and PCS output power demand. A droop control strategy is adopted to control the corresponding PCS. Finally, a converter droop control model based on a DRBS with the proposed control algorithm is built and its accuracy and effectiveness are carefully verified by detailed simulation results in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Strategy for improving fault ride-through capability of cascaded STATCOM
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The cascaded STATCOM is an advanced reactive power compensation device in the power system, but its application is limited by the insufficient fault crossing ability, especially asymmetric faults. This article proposes a three-level capacitor voltage balancing control strategy, which includes global average DC voltage, capacitor voltage phase to phase and phase to phase balancing control, effectively suppressing capacitor voltage fluctuations under faults, improving the device's fault crossing ability, and balancing three-phase current to maximize reactive power output. The effectiveness of this strategy was verified through simulation experiments based on single-phase and two-phase faults.

articleTitle: Physics informed data-driven approach for ultra-short term wind power forecasting based on temporal and graph convolutional networks
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With increasing penetration of renewables, wind power forecasting (WPF) is of great importance for the stable operation of modern power grid. The rapid development of artificial intelligence (AI) enables higher accuracy for WPF. This paper proposes a data-driven ultra-short term WPF method that incorporates physics information within the WPF problem. Firstly, the physics model of WPF problem is built, and the mapping from the wind speed to the wind power is approximated through physics. With the predicted wind speed from numerical weather prediction (NWP) and the physics model, the preliminary wind power output can be approximated. Secondly, the residual between the preliminary predicted value and the actual wind power is described by a data-driven network. Specifically, the structures of temporal convolutional network (TCN) and graph convolutional network (GCN) are adopted to extract the time-space features within the input data, and to determine the mapping between the input data and the residual. Finally, the preliminary predicted value and the predicted residual value are added together to get the final predicted wind power. Experimental results using practical wind farm data show that the proposed ultra-short term WPF method presents higher forecasting accuracy compared to methods that are only based on physics or data-driven method.

articleTitle: Characteristic harmonics suppression strategy for LCC-MMC based HVDC system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: This paper proposes a characteristic harmonics suppression strategy for the LCC-MMC based HVDC system using the MMC. Firstly, the topology of the LCC-MMC based HVDC system is introduced, in which the sending end converter station adopts the LCC-MMC hybrid converter valves despite of the structure of receiving end converter. Secondly, in the outer voltage loop of the MMC, high pass filters, band pass filters, and notch filters are used to extract the characteristic harmonics of the LCC converter for performance comparison, and they are reverse superimposed onto the reference current. In the inner current loop, a PIR control strategy is proposed to track and compensate for the characteristic harmonics without influence on the fundamental components. Finally, the LCC-MMC based HVDC system is constructed in MATLAB/Simulink to verify the effectiveness of the proposed characteristic harmonics suppression strategy.

articleTitle: Discussions on the applicability of optical methods on metal-particle triggered surface charge accumulation and unpredictable flashover
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The presence of metal particles in the cavity of GIS/GIL can cause the accumulation of surface charge and potentially result in severe surface flashover on insulators. This presents a significant obstacle to the progress of DC GIS/GIL development. This paper discusses the process and mechanism of metal particle-induced surface flashover on DC GIS/GIL insulators, including the source, hazards, and possible solutions in metal particle detection. Particularly, the effectiveness of optical detection methods, such as photon counting technology, is discussed in detecting the motion characteristics of metal particles and early-stage discharges induced by metal particles. The research conducted in this paper aims to provide valuable insights and guidance for effectively preventing and suppressing metal particle discharge faults in future DC GIS/GIL designs and applications.

articleTitle: Research on capacity configuration scheme of hybrid energy storage equipment in wind farm based on wavelet packet decomposition
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Based on the actual operating data of a wind farm in Inner Mongolia, the amplitude frequency characteristics were analyzed, and a hybrid energy storage system with battery supercapacitors was determined to suppress wind power fluctuations. Compare the characteristics of energy storage systems under centralized and decentralized topologies, and use centralized topologies as a way to connect hybrid energy storage systems with wind farms. This article proposes a power allocation algorithm for hybrid energy storage systems based on wavelet packet decomposition, and determines the capacity of hybrid energy storage devices on this basis. Build a simulation model of a doubly fed wind power generation system with a hybrid energy storage system consisting of battery supercapacitors in an RTLAB environment, and verify that the hybrid energy storage system using this capacity configuration scheme can effectively suppress wind power fluctuations.

articleTitle: A novel equivalent testing circuit for MMC submodule
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Modular multilevel converter based on high voltage and high power are the future development direction of VSC-HVDC power transmission. To ensure the reliability of VSC-HVDC transmission projects, it is necessary to test the MMC submodule before the project is put into operation. However, directly building a complete MMC system is time-consuming and costly, thus requiring a simple and effective submodule equivalent experimental method. This paper focuses on the equivalent testing method of MMC submodules, studying the electrical stress of submodules during the steady-state operation of modular multilevel converter, and clarifying the key parameters for equivalent testing of submodules. A novel submodule equivalent testing method and control strategy have been proposed. This method achieves testing of MMC submodules at low loss. Simulation verification shows that the proposed method can stably generate electrical stress under actual operating condition.

articleTitle: Topology design of distribution transformers for magnetic coupled energy storage devices
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The development of new power systems containing large-scale energy storage devices is rapid, and it is of great significance to achieve efficient and reasonable utilization of energy storage. This article proposes to design a new topology of distribu tion transformer by magnetic coupling the energy storage device to a traditional dual winding transformer in the form of a third winding. In addition to its normal voltage transformation function, it can also balance peak shaving and valley filling functions to cope with short-term peak overload problems caused by impact loads such as electric vehicles. The advantage of this topology is that it has minimal structural changes to traditional transformers, lower investment costs than power electr onic transformers, and magnetic coupling also achieves electrical isolation for easy maintenance and replacement of energy storage devices. This article first proposes and analyses the new topology of distribution transformers. Then, followed by matching control strategies for charging and discharging energy storage devices. Finally, based on MATLAB/Simulink, the circuit model is completed and its basic peak shaving and valley filling functions are verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Impedance modeling of DRU based HVDC system with grid-following and grid-forming converters
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The escalating capacity of offshore wind power introduces substantial challenges for offshore integration and transmission systems. Diode rectifier unit (DRU) based high voltage direct current (HVDC) system has been acknowledged as a potential method to achieve economical offshore wind power transmission. For the purpose of the uncontrollability of DRU, grid-forming (GFM) converters are necessary to support offshore AC voltage. Moreover, the clamping effect of DRU cause unconventional power characteristic of active power-voltage and reactive power-frequency, thus leading to untraditional control loop. Simultaneously, due to the immaturity of GFM converters, grid-following (GFL) converters could be applied for a long period. However, considering the effect of the phase-locked loops (PLL), the stability of entire system is decreased. In this regard, this article aims at studying thedq-frame impedance model of GFL converters and DRU based GFM converters, which including active power-voltage loop and reactive power-frequency loop. Finally, a simulation of the two converters are built in MATLAB/Simulink, results are shared to prove the correctness.

articleTitle: The non-unit protection for flexible DC transmission lines based on the instantaneous energy ratio of voltage
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: To address challenges in identifying high-resistance faults and reducing noise interference in traditional frequency-domain protection for flexible DC transmission lines. A non-unit protection method based on the ratio of energy accumulation at fault moments is proposed. Firstly, expressions for internal and external faults are derived to discern their respective energy distribution characteristics. The protection identification principle is based on the attenuation effect of boundary components on high-frequency components. Secondly, the impact of the Gaussian window function in the S-transform on energy distribution is investigated. Based on the enhancement effect of the high-frequency energy of internal faults in the amplitude-frequency curve at the fault moment, a protection method utilizing the instantaneous high frequency and low frequency ratio is proposed. Finally, the results of PSCAD simulation show that the proposed protection scheme can rapidly and reliably identify internal and external faults, demonstrating high tolerance to transition resistance.

articleTitle: A inter-turn fault protection scheme for stepped controllable shunt reactor based on parameter identification
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Under the background of the “dual carbon” goal, new energy and new power systems have increasingly become the focus of social attention, and offshore wind is increasingly seen as a low-cost and safe source of renewable energy. But the reactive power problem of offshore wind power AC transmission is serious, and the voltage fluctuation is also more frequent. The stepped controllable shunt reactor can adjust the reactive power capacity according to the demand and has a simple structure and high reliability, which is an effective way to solve the reactive power problem of offshore AC transmission. However, when inter-turn short-circuit fault occurs in the stepped controllable shunt reactor, the voltage and current change characteristics are not obvious, and the existing protection methods need to be improved. In this paper, a new protection method is proposed for inter-turn short-circuit fault of the stepped controllable shunt reactor, in which the fault is identified by directly recognizing the parameters of hierarchical controllable reactance and comparing the changes of parameters, and can be used as a supplement to the existing protection methods.

articleTitle: Voltage stability and frequency stability analysis of Zhejiang power grid
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Under the dual requirements of increasing electricity demand and energy cleanliness, Zhejiang power grid is developing into become a multi-infeed DC receiving-end grid with high proportion of renewable energy, and the operating characteristics of Zhejiang power grid have changes. Therefore, it is necessary to reassess the voltage stability and frequency stability of the Zhejiang power grid. This paper combines the influence of DC and renewable energy units, and analyzes the voltage stability and frequency stability of multi-infeed DC receiving-end grid with high proportion of renewable energy from static and transient time scales. Finally, the voltage stability and frequency stability of Zhejiang power grid are specifically analyzed in PSS/E software based on the 2025 planning data of Zhejiang power grid. The stability analysis results of Zhejiang power grid in this article have important guiding significance for ensuring the safe and stable operation of Zhejiang power grid.

articleTitle: Analysis of busbar-insulator mounted air gap electric field based on three-dimensional parametric modeling
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Aiming at a certain type of switchgear in the lightning impulse test process insulator and busbar installation position abnormal discharge problem, this paper establishes a three-dimensional (3D) parametric model, the use of Ansys Maxwell electric field simulation software, calculation and analysis of busbar width (W), busbar thickness (T), busbar and insulator spacing (H) and screw specifications size and other parameters on the electric field characteristics of the impact and put forward to improve the program for experimental verification. The results show that: when the width of the busbar is larger than the insulator diameter (O), the electric field strength is maintained at a low level and should be given priority in the design; when the width of the busbar is smaller than the insulator diameter, the installation of circular insulating gaskets between the busbar and insulator can effectively reduce the electric field strength, the insulating gasket specification size R=40mm, H=3mm when the electric field strength of the air gap for the Eair=2.5E6 v/m, mounting bolt The electric field strength is Eair=2.6E6 v/m when the mounting bolts are replaced with hexagonal bolts of the same specification, and the improved scheme passes the lightning impulse test.

articleTitle: A voltage balancing method for isolated modular multilevel DC-DC converters with asymmetric arm impedance
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The isolated Modular Multilevel DC-DC Converters (IMMDC) with asymmetric arm impedance will induce the capacitor voltages unbalance between the upper and lower arm sub-modules (SMs). For addressing this issue, in this letter, the energy difference between the upper and lower arms is analyzed and a balance equation is given. An arm voltage balancing strategy based on inter-arm phase shift angle (IAPSA) and inter-phase phase shift angle (IPPSA) is proposed. The proposed strategy has a simple structure and can achieve voltage balance between different phases. The proposed strategy is validated by experimental tests.

articleTitle: SOC balancing strategy for parallel-connected power conversion system based on PQ decoupling control
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Nowadays the battery energy storage system (BESS) plays a significant role in power grid due to its excellent function in energy regulation. In most cases, BESS connects to the power grid through Power Conversion System(PCS). However, the state of charge (SOC) of different battery modules tend to be different during the working process. The difference bet ween SOC would intensify buckets effect, and the performance of BESS would be degraded due to the abnormal feature (low SOC) of single battery cell. To avoid such shortcoming, it is necessary to eliminate the difference of SOC though control strategy. In this paper, we propose a SOC balancing strategy for parallel-connected power conversion system based on PQ decoupling control, which can also adjust the active power output of each battery module converge to optimization solution. Simulation and experimental results from a 2 × 700V, parallel-connected power converter system are presented in order to validate the method.

articleTitle: Infrared arrester detection based on improved YOLOv4
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Aiming at the issues of complex background, low contrast, and low signal-to-noise ratio in infrared images of arresters, as well as the suboptimal performance of unmanned aerial vehicle intelligent inspections, a modified YOLOv4 object detection algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the CSPDarkNet backbone network of the original model is replaced with GhostNet, significantly reducing the network parameter size to 17.76% of the original network. Secondly, the adaptive Adam optimizer is used for backpropagation computation, which improves the detection accuracy of arresters in infrared images without increasing computational complexity. Compared to the model with the modified backbone network, it achieves a 3.54% improvement in accuracy. Lastly, the IoU Loss in the confidence loss calculation process is replaced with Focal Loss, which allows the network to focus more on difficult-to-classify samples.

articleTitle: AC-DC transmitting simultaneously along the same feeder line in distribution network
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With rapid growth of global economy, power demand has increased rapidly. It is uneconomic and difficult to build new feeder lines. As an alternative, making full use of the existing AC line is a solution for the problem. Based on zigzag transformer, this paper presents a simultaneous AC-DC power transmission scheme in distribution network by superimposing a certain amount of DC on usual feeder. The composited current is very close to thermal limits of the line. The maximum of the total power transmitted in the AC-DC system is analyzed theoretically and numerically. Simulation is conducted by PSCAD/EMTDC. Economic analysis between AC-DC system and conventional AC distribution network is performed. The results illustrate the feasibility of the proposed scheme. Substantial gain in the capacity of the feeder is obtained and economical efficiency of the scheme is remarkable. The scheme is a new subject worthy of consideration and it also provides one way for more and more distributed generation and DC load access to distribution network.

articleTitle: A review of the optimal configuration of fault current limiter in power system
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the continuous development of new power systems, the short-circuit currents at each node of the grid continue to increase, and there will be multiple sites with excessive short-circuit currents and insufficient margins, and the optimal configuration of fault current limiters will effectively and economically limit the system short-circuit currents. The paper first introduces the modeling method for optimal configuration of fault current limiters in power grids, and lists the commonly used objective functions and constraints. Then three approaches to multi-objective functions and their modeling and solution algorithms are presented. Finally, combined with the future development trend of the power grid, it summarizes the problems that need to be considered in the future research on the optimal configuration of fault current limiters, such as the consideration of the optimal configuration of new energy sources after joining the power grid, the development of new algorithms, and so on, to make an outlook for the direction of the research on the optimal configuration of fault current limiters.

articleTitle: Study on corrosion inhibition effect of dendritic ionic liquid polymer for corrosion protection of ultra-high voltage direct current transmission towers
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The manufacturing and processing of metal materials have greatly promoted the development of chemical industry. However, the resulting metal corrosion phenomenon also comes one after another. Metal corrosion not only does great harm to production and manufacturing equipment, but also poses a great burden on the environment. Coating hydrophobic compound on metal surface as a coating for anti-corrosion is a major way to protect metal corrosion in recent years. After the hydrophobic compound is adsorbed on the metal surface, a hydrophobic protective film is formed as the protective layer of the metal, so as to delay the corrosion of the metal. The hydrophobic substances adsorbed on the metal surface separate the metal surface from the corrosive medium by using the formed hydrophobic film, so as to delay the metal corrosion.This paper mainly explores the corrosion inhibition performance of linear and dendritic ionic liquid inhibitors for metal.

articleTitle: Overview of research on distribution network voltage regulation devices in the context of high penetration of distributed photovoltaic integration
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the proposal of the dual carbon goal and the rapid development of China's photovoltaic power generation industry, the penetration rate of distributed photovoltaics in the distribution network is constantly increasing, and the safe and stable operation of the distribution network is facing huge challenges, especially the problem of voltage exceeding the limit. For this purpose, systematic research has been carried out on voltage regulation equipment for distribution networks, aiming to provide some reference for voltage regulation equipment and strategies that can be used when high proportion distributed photovoltaics are connected to distribution networks. Firstly, the types of middle note equipment in the current distribution network are analyzed. Secondly, the structure and voltage regulation principle of each voltage regulation equipment were analyzed. Once again, the voltage regulation strategies of each voltage regulation device were studied. Finally, the advantages and disadvantages of each voltage regulation device were summarized, and the selection of background voltage regulation devices for high proportion distributed photovoltaic integration into the distribution network was discussed.

articleTitle: Summary of stability analysis and collaborative control technology research on multi PCS parallel connection of grid type energy storage power stations
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: To sort out the stability analysis and collaborative control technology of multi PCS parallel connection in grid type energy storage power stations, and further explore their potential and application in the power grid, relevant sorting and research work will be carried out. Firstly, summarize and summarize the research status of PCS multi machine parallel stability, multi PCS collaborative control strategies, and black start control strategies related to the construction of grid type energy storage power stations; Then, summarize and analyze the mechanism and theory of multi PCS parallel stability analysis and collaborative control technology; Finally, further thoughts and prospects are proposed regarding the key issues that urgently need to be addressed in the application of PCS parallel stability analysis and collaborative control in the power grid for grid type energy storage systems.

articleTitle: Bi-level optimized planning for hybrid energy storage based on AHP and TOPSIS fuzzy evaluation
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In order to promote renewable consumptions while meeting the ever-increasing load demands and maintaining power system reliability, a dual-layer optimized model of the hybrid energy storage (ES) system consisting of battery, thermal and hydrogen Ess is established. An evaluation system of ES planning is proposed, which combines analytic hierarchy process (AHP) with technique for order preference by similarity to ideal solution (TOPSIS) and fuzzy comprehensive analysis. An improved niche multi-objective particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is proposed, which combines the niche processing mechanism with external file selection technology and chaotic mutation technology. Cases study shows that the optimal configuration of the hybrid ES system can improve the economy of the system, reduce the active power loss and the voltage offset and enhance the voltage stability.

articleTitle: Analysis and approximate solution method of DC current transient characteristics of LCC-HVDC considering the influence of line distribution parameters
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: UHV DC transmission technology is a key means realize long-distance energy transmission. Commutation failure exposes the converter valve to withstand high short-term fault current stress, endangering the safe and reliable operation of devices and key components. The evolution law of fault current is affected by the coupling effect of multiple factors and is difficult to analyze. However, the fault current peak value is an important indicator for converter valve control protection and electrical parameter design. Based on this, this paper proposes a fault current evolution characteristic and time domain solution method that takes into account the influence of DC line distribution parameters, and establishes the impedance model of the converter in the transient stage and the DC transmission of the converter valves at the sending and receiving ends during the fault current evolution process. The side current time and frequency domain expressions clarify the fault current evolution mechanism and realize the calculation of the system fault current peak value. Finally, this article verifies the accuracy of the fault current analysis method in this article through comparative analysis of the actual simulation model and calculation results of the 'Hami-Zhengzhou Bipolar Double 12 Pulsation LCC-HVDC' project.

articleTitle: Fault current calculation method for FID-based interconnected distribution networks
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Flexible interconnection device led by voltage-sourced converters (FID-VSC) provides advantages such as power decoupling control and fast fault isolation for interconnected distribution networks, but it also brings about changes in fault characteristics generated by reverse power flow. In this paper, a FID-based fault current calculation method for interconnected distribution networks is presented. Considering the conditions of converter controllers and various types of faults (both non-severe and severe cases), this paper provides a comprehensive analysis of the operational characteristics of FID in distribution network faults. Then a FID-based fault current calculation method for interconnected distribution networks is given, which identifies the FID-VSC capacity, connection points, power flow direction, fault location and fault type, thus providing an effective fault characterization method. Dynamic simulation and comparison with calculation results of fault currents of a twin-substation interconnected distribution network based on 10kV-5.5MW IGCT-based FID in PSCAD/EMTDC and Matlab verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. It provides an efficient and universally applicable method for analyzing the operation of protective devices and reconfiguring protection arrangements in FID-based multi-substation distribution networks.

articleTitle: Fault-line selection in distribution networks with distributed power sources based on energy storage station control strategy
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the continuous access of large-scale distributed power sources to the grid and the expansion of the distribution network scale, it is difficult to ensure the accuracy of the traditional fault-line selection scheme for distribution networks. Considering that the new distribution network contains a large number of power electronic devices, characteristic signals can be actively injected for fault-line selection. A low-frequency signal active injection method based on the control strategy of energy storage power stations and its parameter selection principle are proposed in this paper. The different fault characteristics presented by the low-frequency injected signals in the faulted and non-faulted lines when a single-phase grounding fault occurs in the distribution network are analyzed, and a selection criterion based on low-frequency signals in zero sequence current was proposed. Finally, the correctness of the theory and the effectiveness of the scheme are verified by PSCAD/EMTDC simulation.

articleTitle: The research and implementation of key technology for zero-carbon operation in DC buildings
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In order to explore the implementation path of achieving “carbon neutrality”, this paper conducts research and development on DC system configuration scheme, “flexible load regulation strategy, photovoltaics, energy storage, direct current and flexibility”(PEDF) energy regulation strategy based on SiC converter for medium-sized office buildings. This forms a zerocarbon operation solution based on DC networking technology and carries out demonstration project construction. Compared with traditional buildings, this project significantly enhances the load regulation capability and application potential of new energy both on-site and off-site. It achieves extremely low energy consumption operation and utilization of full zero-carbon energy while obtaining third-party certification for zero-carbon building.

articleTitle: Retired battery sorting method via feature visualization and machine learning under partial charging voltage segments
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the rapid development of the electric vehicles, the echelon utilization of retired power batteries has become a current research hotspot. A retired battery sorting method based on Gramian angle difference fields (GADF) and Swin Transformer models is proposed to address the issues of poor sorting accuracy, low efficiency, and complex feature engineering in the echelon utilization of retired batteries. Part of the charging voltage curve is converted into images using the GADF, and the images are classified using the Swin Transformer model. Firstly, we extract voltage segments from the constant current charging stage to obtain voltages above 3.9V. Then, we perform Piecewise Aggregate Approximation (PAA) data dimensionality reduction on some voltage segments and encode the voltage information into the image using GADF method. Finally, Swin Transformer is used to classify the transformed image. Due to the existence of a shifted window, this algorithm can integrate information between different patches, making the resulting image contain more comprehensive and authentic information. Finally, we validated and compared the effectiveness of different retired battery sorting methods on the modified NASA dataset, and the results showed that the proposed method achieved an accuracy of 97.67% for retired battery sorting, achieving high precision and efficiency.

articleTitle: Open-winding transformer based dual modular multilevel converters with DC fault ride-through capability
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In this paper, a novel multilevel converter topology, which is called open-winding transformer based dual modular multilevel converters (OWT-DMMC), is proposed for DC-fault ride-through in high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission. OWT-DMMC has two individual DC output ports, which can be used for double-circuit transmission or multi-terminal interconnected HVDC networks. The proposed topology can achieve uninterruptible power transmission in the case of a DC fault. Furthermore, the power flow across the two DC ports can be adjusted flexibly in the proposed topology. The proposed topology structure and control scheme are elaborated in this paper. The feasibility of the proposed topology and the control scheme is validated by simulation results and experimental tests.

articleTitle: A study for critical factors on power transmission of large-scale renewable energy base in desert regions
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Large-scale renewable energy bases in desert regions often feature extensive scale, wide geographical distribution, weak grid infrastructure, distance from load centers, and lack of conventional power support. Traditional planning and operation methods are no longer suitable for large-scale renewable energy transmission scenarios. Therefore, focusing on large-scale renewable energy bases in desert regions, this study proposes a time series production simulation model aimed at maximizing renewable energy output at the sending terminal via flexible DC transmission. Based on actual data from a domestic renewable energy base, production simulation was conducted to evaluate, for the first time, the impact of various critical factors on renewable energy consumption rate and annual utilization hours of the transmission channel. These critical factors include different capacity configurations and combinations of wind and solar power stations, the temporal characteristics of wind and solar power data, and various configurations of storage and transmission channel capacities. The results indicate that these critical factors have different impacts on the performance indicators, thus providing a foundation for the development of coordinated optimization schemes for multi-type power sources and multi-terminal DC systems, as well as their economic evaluation.

articleTitle: Practical calculation model for short-circuit current of doubly fed induction generator in large power grids
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The short-circuit current (SCC) calculation of doubly fed induction generator (DFIG) is very complicated, which is influenced not only by flux coupling between generator stator and rotor, but also by rotor side converter (RSC) control or crowbar protection response. Based on our previous work, this paper analyzes the influence of different parameters on the calculation results of each component of DFIG SCC, as well as the influence of the neglection of some parameters on the calculation accuracy of SCC. By extracting the key influencing factors, a practical DFIG SCC calculation model suitable for large power grids is obtained. The model has the advantages of parameters-easy-to-access and clear defination. Meanwhile, according to the different requirements of SCC calculation, the corresponding calculation suggestions are given for the completely unknown parameters.

articleTitle: Evaluation method of tie-line transmission capacity considering uncertainty of renewable energy and system frequency constraints
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of renewable energy, the uncertainty of its output has brought challenges to the evaluation of tie-line transmission capacity. This paper presents an evaluation method of tie-line transmission capacity considering the uncertainty of renewable energy and the constraints of system frequency. Based on the chance constraint method, a new uncertainty representation method of renewable energy is proposed, which reflects the uncertainty of renewable energy into the system security constraints, so that the uncertainty of renewable energy can be effectively considered in the process of tie-line transmission power evaluation. Meanwhile, based on the ASF model, this paper puts forward constraints on rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and the maximum variation of grid frequency to ensure frequency safety. Finally, the multi-point approximation method is proposed to evaluate the power security region of tie-line transmission considering the uncertainty of renewable energy and system frequency constraints based on the above constraints. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: MeOERM: Progressive holonic decision-making in microgrid with multi-modal embedding-based model
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The integration of renewable energy sources and the dynamic intricacies inherent in microgrid environments present formidable challenges for proficient decision-making within microgrid control systems. The intermittent power generation and consumption patterns exhibited by Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and consumers in microgrids have the potential to induce transient imbalances in both active and reactive power, thereby diminishing power quality parameters and jeopardizing operational stability. In response to this exigency, the decision-making processes of Autonomous Control Systems (ACS) necessitate a paradigm shift toward the contemplation of holonic architectures. Extensive endeavors have been dedicated to optimizing the multi-parameter challenges inherent in the holonic architectures of ACS for microgrid control. Despite the implementation of numerous optimization strategies, endeavors to comprehend emergent phenomena persist, wherein the system's behavior eludes deduction from the discrete behaviors of its components. The present research introduces an innovative approach aimed at augmenting holonic architecture decision-making through the application of a multi-modal dynamic incremental neural network. Termed the Multi-modal Embedding-based Open Energy Router Model (MeOERM), this model is meticulously engineered to accommodate the multi-parameter characteristics of microgrid systems, adeptly respond to dynamic alterations, and judiciously leverage diverse data types. By employing multi-modal embedding to map microgrids and other diverse data sources, MeOERM achieves heightened proficiency in comprehension, logical inference, and the generation of domain-specific knowledge, thereby fortifying security measures. This investigation aspires to contribute significantly to the progression of intelligent control systems for microgrids by amalgamating the advantages of holonic architectures with the adeptness of multi-modal dynamic incremental neural networks.

articleTitle: Risk status identification of active distribution station area based on low voltage intelligent circuit breakers
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of distributed photovoltaic (PV) power generation in low-voltage station area, the problem of risk status identification of low-voltage station area brought about by large-scale PV access has attracted widespread attention. In this paper, a refined low-voltage platform simulation topology model is established based on Matlab/Simulink. Secondly, the optimal layout of the monitoring points was determined by extracting the time-frequency domain characteristics at the monitoring points of the low-voltage circuit breaker in the station area. Finally, based on the simulation model, the multi-dimensional steady-state characteristics are evaluated, and the identification method of different risk status in the active station area is proposed, which effectively improves the accuracy of risk state identification.

articleTitle: The signal processing scheme combining mathematical morphology method for DC protection
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Noise tolerance and waveform identification capability are the bottlenecks of traveling wave (TW) protection in DC transmission systems. However, current mathematical morphology (MM) based signal processing methods with a single function of noise reduction or waveform extraction cannot be applied to the overall process of DC protection. In order to improve the performance of TW-based protection by exploiting the strengths of different MM operators, a novel signal processing scheme combining the MM method for DC protection is proposed in this paper, which consists of the adaptive multiscale mathematical morphology filter (AM-MMF) applied in the protection start unit, the morphology gradient (MG) operators in the wave edge identification unit, and theMixMMF in the post-fault denoising and waveform restoration procedure. Extensive simulations are carried out in PSCAD and MATLAB to verify the necessity and feasibility of the proposed signal processing scheme. The simulation results show that the proposed waveform-based protection under the proposed signal processing scheme has high reliability and sensitivity in different fault types, high resistance, strong addictive noise, and lightning interference background.

articleTitle: Study and application of mega-watts interconnections for future urban distribution networks
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Traditional AC medium-voltage distribution network is designed in the open-loop mode and the contact switch between different regions is normally in cold standby state. However, with the rapid increasing of DC household appliances, distributed photovoltaic sources, energy storage equipment, charging facilities, DC data centres and so on, aiming at high safety, efficiency and reliability for power supply, the research and application of hybrid distribution network has abundant application scenarios and tremendous potential values. First of all, flexible interconnection of AC and DC grid is described and analysed. And then a novel scheme to establish AC/DC hybrid distribution network by adding the multi-terminal flexible DC interconnection into the traditional medium-voltage AC networks is proposed, which is capable of controlling bi-directional power flow for multiple feeders and providing not only various interfaces for the forementioned new types of loads and renewable energy, but also mutual power supply during fault-on occurrence. The basic composition of flexible DC interconnection adopts mega-watts active-neutral-point-clamped converters based on IGCT-in-series, with advantages of modularity, scalability and high power density. Besides, the security and stability improvement of the proposed hybrid interconnected distribution network for urban power grid is presented and discussed, and a converter prototype is built-up to verify the feasibility with basic experiment results.

articleTitle: Active Bilateral Frequency Support using LCC-HVDC systems for asynchronous interconnected systems
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The involvement of Line-Commutated Converter-based High-Voltage Direct Current (LCC-HVDC) systems in grid frequency support has been studied in previous research, with a number of practical applications. Existing methods, however, fail to achieve active bidirectional frequency support and are mainly geared towards large frequency events. Specifically, previous studies have identified the inability of LCC-HVDC to achieve dynamic regulation of the frequency of asynchronous interconnected systems. This is due to DC power variations causing fluctuations in the reactive power of LCC-HVDC, leading to fluctuation in AC voltage. In this study, it is shown that LCC-HVDC can achieve reactive power control by flexibly adjusting the DC current and DC voltage in a coordinated manner. Based on this, an active bilateral frequency support (ABFS) control is proposed, involving a flexible allocation of DC current and DC voltage, that aims to achieve dynamic regulation of the frequency of asynchronous interconnected systems while maintaining a constant reactive power consumption of the inverter. This enables the minimization of AC voltage fluctuation caused by DC power variations. Furthermore, the concept and stability of the proposed control are presented using the V-I trajectory, and the extinction angle limitation of the inverter has been taken into account. Therefore, the risk of commutation failure in the proposed method can be effectively avoided as well. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated using a modified four-generator and two-area (4G2A) system under a variety of load changes.

articleTitle: Corrosion prevention performance and mechanism of slow-release molecules in micro-nano insulating coatings for ultra-high voltage direct current transmission towers
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The rapid development of ultra-high voltage direct current transmission technology, the more stringent requirements for transmission and transformation equipment materials, transmission and transformation equipment in the use of the period of time often occurs in a variety of losses and failures caused by corrosion. Therefore, in order to slow down the corrosion rate of transmission line towers, the design and synthesis of organic corrosion inhibitor molecules have important scientific value and social significance for the protection of metal corrosion and sustainable development. In this paper, the potential value of benzimidazole as an organic corrosion inhibitor in the field of corrosion protection of transmission line towers is explored through an in-depth study of its application. The corrosion inhibition performance and corrosion inhibition mechanism of these molecules on mild steel in acidic medium were investigated by metal surface analysis and electrochemical testing, etc. This study provides new ideas and methods for the corrosion prevention of transmission line towers, which is of positive significance for the improvement of the reliability and safety of the power system.

articleTitle: Optimization strategy of power oscillations suppression considering ESS converter capacity limit
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Droop control and inertia control are the typical control modes for energy storage system (ESS) suppressing power oscillations. However, when the control effect is enhanced to some certain extent, ESS will limit the output power to the device maximum power (termed maximum power modulation mode) and be out of the expected power control because of the limited converter capacity. This paper focuses on the evaluation index of power oscillation suppression and compares the suppression ability of the rate of change of rotor speed with different ESS control modes.
