The study shows that the power oscillations can be better suppressed than droop control and inertia control modes by providing fast maximum power support; however, the long-term operation of maximum power modulation mode will cause frequent charge and discharge with large current, resulting in its service life decreasing sharply. To this end, an optimized suppression mode based on maximum power modulation and droop control is proposed, the former can alternately output or absorb active power with the converter capacity to quickly make up for the system power shortage, suppressing the driving force of power oscillations, i.e., the unbalanced power. When the evaluation index meets the limit requirements, under effect of droop control, ESS drops out the maximum power mode smoothly and further suppresses the rotor speed deviation to improve frequency quality. Simulation results verify the proposed mode effectiveness.

articleTitle: Inertia and damping characteristics analysis of grid-tied ESS based on power-frequency sag control
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Grid-tied ESS based on power-frequency sag control can effectively solve the problem of frequency stability reduction of the power grid caused by large-scale access of distributed power sources, while equivalently improving the inertia level and damping capacity of the power system. In this paper, the main parameters affecting the inertia level, damping effect and synchronization capability of the energy storage system and their influence laws are analyzed by establishing the dynamic model of its DC voltage time scale and using the stationary synchronous generator model based on the grid-connected energy storage system with power-frequency sag control as the research object. The results show that the sag control link and power control link are the main sources of the inertia and damping effects of the energy storage system, and the inertia/damping characteristics of the system can be changed equivalently by the optimal design of the sag coefficient and power loop PI parameters. The results of simulation experiments prove the correctness of the findings of this paper. The findings will be useful for designing effective control strategies for energy storage systems to assist in enhancing the inertia level and damping capability of the grid and enhancing the stable operation of distributed generation systems and their access to the grid.

articleTitle: A review of theoretical loss calculation methods in medium-low voltage distribution networks
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: Bad data identification is crucial in the theoretical line loss calculation process of distribution networks, as it helps ens ure the quality and reliability of system operation data. In power system monitoring and operation, the accuracy and credibility of theoretical line loss calculations may be compromised due to various factors such as different measurement data sources, sensor failures, communication failures, or human errors. This paper first introduces the impact of bad data on line los s calculations. Subsequently, existing methods for bad data identification are summarized, and the advantages and disadvantages of various methods are analyzed. Based on this foundation, traditional methods of theoretical line loss calculation are discusse d. Furthermore, in response to the problems existing in traditional theoretical line loss calculation methods, new research approaches for theoretical line loss calculation are proposed, and prospects for future algorithm development are discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of emergency load capacity of ±500kV sea wind power transmission line
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: The estimation of the emergency load carrying capacity for offshore wind power transmission lines constitutes an essential factor in section selection(landfall section), and the safeguarding of submarine cable engineering operations. This study establishes a transient thermal model for a ±500kV cross-linked polyethylene insulated submarine cable, pinpointing the key issue-declining carrying capacity- in submarine cable (landfall section). We detail computations for the emergency load carrying capacity and emergency durations for submarine cables, considering two distinct laying environments - pipe-passage and direct burial - and varying initial loads at the landing section. Our findings reveal a substantial negative correlation between the permitted operating duration under emergency load and the conductor's initial temperature in both laying environments. Notably, the temperature rise rate in pipe-passage laying lags by 0.54–1.0 times compared to direct burial, significantly retarding the temperature increase in the conductor, hence affording more time for emergency responses. In direct burial scenarios, subjecting a submarine cable initially running at 50%I–95%Iof its carrying capacity to an emergency load of 110%I–160%Icuts the allowed operating time by a minimum of 10 hours. More critically, an escalation of the emergency load from 95%Ito 160%Ileaves only 17minof emergency time, posing a substantial safety risk during power scheduling processes. Finally, an emergency load capacity analysis and assessment was conducted in conjunction with the Qingzhou V and VII submarine cable project to ensure the safe operation of the submarine cables.

articleTitle: Single-phase grounding transient spectral energy routing method for renewable energy distribution networks considering frequency band screening
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: In this paper, the characteristic distributions of single-phase grounding zero sequence currents under different fault conditions are investigated, and the limitations of the transient energy-based wire routing method are analysed. In order to solve the problem of wire selection errors that may be caused by arc-absorbing coils, it is proposed to select wires by excluding the zero sequence currents of specific frequency bands through the derivation of band screening formulae to apply to various fault conditions. The article also verifies the bus fault characteristics from both theoretical and simulation studies, and proposes an effective identification criterion that can distinguish bus faults from the longest feeder faults. The research method needs to obtain the line-to-ground capacitance, and the corresponding measurement method is given in the article, and the error analysis shows that the method has good resistance to errors.

articleTitle: Efficient simulation and accurate representation of control features: a novel phasor modelling method for GFM-based VSC-HVDC systems
publicationTitle: 20th International Conference on AC and DC Power Transmission 2024 (ACDC 2024)
abstract: GFM-VSC represents a promising research area with the potential to enhance the stability and dynamic response of VSC - HVDC systems. However, there is a need for the development of a fast modelling method that can accurately capture its control features for large-scale power system electromechanical transient simulations. Addressing this need, this paper proposes a novel phasor modelling method for GFM-based VSC-HVDC systems. The study begins by presenting a typical two-terminal MMC-HVDC system equipped with a GFM VSC with a droop controller. This is followed by a detailed discussion of three primary components: the converter station, the converter controller, and the DC transmission line. The modelling methods for these components are detailed, considering the operating characteristics of the MMC and the modulation ratio constraints of the converter controller. Additionally, a base value calculation algorithm is introduced to simplify the analysis and modelling process significantly, accommodating the wide variations in physical parameters. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, a comparative analysis is conducted between the conventional EMT modelling method in the electromagnetic transient simulation environment and the improved phasor modelling method in the electromechanical transient simulation environment. The results demonstrate the accurate dynamic response behaviour and the reduction in simulation time achieved by the proposed method. This study aims to provide a solid foundation for the stability analysis of large-scale GFM VSC based HVDC systems.
